RACE 07 may be 10 years old, but I still highly reccomend it. It is a must have for racing sim fans. Note: I HIGHLY reccomend that you buy this with the simbin bundle or with all of the DLC when it is on sale, as it gets pretty cheap.
The physics are still very good, especially for the touring cars. Cars behave as they should. The Force Feedback isn't the best compared to more modern sims, but it is still good. One thing this game is really good at that some more modern sims still can't get right is the sense of speed. Going through fast corners in a formula car is absolutely thrilling. The AI in this game is very good, and still some of my favorite to race against. The Graphics aren't the best, but they are still nice to look at, especially considering that this is a 10 year old game. Now, one of my favorite things about this game: The Content. This game has a ton of good content, especially with all of the DLC's. All of the cars are great and fun to drive, and there's lots of great tracks including the legendary Nordschleife. I have long been into spaceships and have been looking for a game that best simulates being a starship captain. This game certainly delivers. You are given directed control of all of your ship's systems, including weapons, engines, shields, airlocks, life support, etc. It truly feels like a geek fantasy. FTL combines a fun element of mystery and exploration as well as an excuse to take out your frustration on potentially hostile vessels, most of which will kill you. The game features a wide variety of usuable ships, each of which requires different tactics and playstyles, if you succeed in unlocking them. While the alien species in the game are certainly not particularly creative (rock people, slugs, etc), each race has different strengths and weaknesses that you can exploit to get the maximun efficiency out of your crew. For example, I couldn't help but smile when a giant praying mantis named "Smith" joined the ship's company.
A word of caution: it is an exceedingly dangerous galaxy. This game is very unforgiving. While you can save your progress, if your crew members die, they are lost forever. If your ship is destroyed, your save is deleted and you will have to start over. So far, my ship has been blown apart, consumed in a solar flare, and at one point my crew asphixiated due to a life support failure. You will have to rely on your skill, good decision making, and a whole lot of luck to beat this game. For instance, when fleeing space pirates, you might warp into another quadrant, only to find your ship being battered by asteroids. Keep in mind that more than half of the time you will lose, even on the easiest settings (if you value your sanity, play on easy), but that is part of the appeal in a universe where almost every other ship is hunting you. It is not about finishing the game as it is about charting the unknown and encountering other races, hopefully those sympathetic to your cause. I would highly recommend this game to anyone who loves space exploration and doesn't mind losing most of their ships to the cold depths of space.

TL:DR -
Blender requires a lot of effort to learn and understand how it works. It's EXTREMELY powerful software loaded with features, tools and capabilities. With the appropriate amount of time and effort (especially with assistance from somewhere like
or Udemy if you're anything short of an expert in 3D, Video, Animation, etc software) some really amazing things can be created.
If you want to create simple 3D models, Sculpt or skin models, 3D or 2D animations, Photorealistic static images and animations, composite 3D / 2D into video, and more....Blender is an excellent "No-price" option.
I, personally, HIGHLY recommend SheepIt for help rendering complex scenes (
) &
(for their Courses, learning flows & ReTopoFlow add-on add-on in the Blender Market @
. I have no financial interest in mentioning either of them. I am just truly just that impressed by them and they have both helped me a LOT.
Blender is amazing and fun, both of which are exponentially increased with acquired knowledge about how to use it. Blender 2.78c is also only an 85.8 MB download, this blows my mind.
---------------------------------------------------
Infinite Wind Version:
The most powerful creative software I've ever had the pleasure to experience. I never had an opportunity to use Maya, 3DS, etc. because of their price points. This really gives anyone the tools to learn modelling, animation, texturing, compositing, and......hell, at 4,439 hours on steam (this is only from July 4, 2015. I Started learning in 2012) at the time of this review I still don't know everything that it can do.
The add-ons are near endless. They amount of software which now allows for easy use with Blender is growing more and more all of the time. The hands down most amazing thing about Blender to me (I know it's a bit ridiculous to be most amazed by this considering all that it can do) is the ratio of functionality to file size. Blender is TINY. The installer for 2.78c is only 85.8 MB. I have lots of project .blend files which are MUCH larger than Blender itself.
Prepare for a succession of steep learning curves, which gradually decline as you learn how the software works, for every feature you wish to learn or utilize. It's VERY hard at first if you're like me and have ZERO experience with software like this (I did have CAD experience which helped). The absolute best advice I can give to any beginners who are serious about learning it is:
DO NOT get discouraged, eventually things will click and you'll learn faster and actually be able to do what you want, IF you put forth the required effort to learn something this complicated. This is something that requires a lot of time and effort in order to even hald understand what you're doing and how to go about it.
DO NOT only use youtube and other random media to learn it. There is good information available, but it is mixed in with tons of people who have no idea how to correctly do what they're trying to teach. (I spent 3 years learning strictly with this method and regret at least 60% of it. It is EXTREMELY diffocult to unlearn bad, or outright wrong information.) Be very careful about who you choose to learn from. It isn't as bad now as it was 5 years ago, but there are still some that will easily pop up in a search when you're looking for something specific
DO, DO, DO, (I can't stress this enough) at least try an actually paid learning resource. There are several of them now.
I chose
and have now been with them for 2 years. They are how I was able to realize that I had learned really bad information and developed some terrible habits that I have still not completely overcome. They are very good teachers and you get a lot more than just Blender lessons and courses. Their content starts with the most basic information and spans through intermediate and advanced on to expert. Some of them are even free as well as a 3 day free trial (If started when you have time to really evaluate what they offer, you'll see that it's worth it). I highly recommend them if you can swing a subscription.
I don't know how good the others are in terms of amount of content and price. I'd bet that just about any of the ones focused on teaching the software (which aren't youtube, vimeo, or other mostly random user created content) would be the best bet for a true beginner like I was.
has beginner tutorials, which were fine, but to really dive in and learn from the most basic things to intermediate then advanced.... A subscription service would definitely be the best learning path. It's so much better than just learning how to do random things and REALLY helps you to understand the software. Once you understand the software, a lot of what you want to do can be figured out on on your own. You absolutely will stuggle in this regard if you choose to just learn random tidbits about random features and functions of this software.
I'm TOTALLY NOT saying that all (or even most) youtube tutorials are useless. I'm just saying a beginner will GREATLY benefit from one of the subscription based course style learning resources. This gives a foundation and structure to the  knowledge which you are acquiring.
Just my 2 cents. I REALLY love this software, it's nothing short of amazing, addictive, somtimes aggrevating and frustrating and all the while a LOT of fun to learn and use.
I feel like I've only really scrateched the surface of what it can do but so far I've used it to:
Create all of the model assets for a game I'm trying to create (alone...sadly).
Create static ads, animated commercials and CG composited video.
Transform (and sometimes design ) static and animated logos.
Modelled Prototype with animated breakdowns, cross sections, etc.
Kill time and do silly (and fun) stuff.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
<3 Blender. The most awesome software I've ever used. Give it a shot. Also, check out the Blender Open Project movie shorts, They're awesome and really show a lot of what blender is capable of doing. They're under "Open Projects" on the official Blender site
. They really should add those to the video previews on steam (Or at least a link to them).

Most of the reviews here were from upon release. I've had the game since release and while it was somewhat disappointing earlier on, overtime and after several patches it has gotten a lot better now so here is a more updated take on things.
Yes, we're missing ps4/xb1 features, yes the online could be more robust, and yes there is an obnoxious amount of obnoxiously overpriced dlc (my opinion at least).
BUT setting aside expectations and comparisons....
What we do have here is still one of the best fighting games on PC. At least on my computer, the game runs beautifully and looks very colorful and pretty. Gameplay is very smooth and I personally enjoy the mechanics and pacing of it. - imo more enjoyable than MK. There is a huge number of characters and costumes already included, a very indepth tutorial mode with lots of ways to practice, and a pretty good selection of regular game modes.
There is also a lot of customizable music tracks dating back across all DOAs that you can setup any way you wish. I think something like over 100 tracks and most of them sound great.
I think you pretty much need a controller to properly enjoy this and my 360 controller works just fine. I've remapped some buttons from the game's menu to my liking (because I think the default configuration is kind of clunky) and it's very intuitive now. There is also a pretty large modding scene if you're into that, but you can't play online with mods.
I've sunk in about 80 hours into this so far since release and it doesn't get boring. The action is mindless, fastpaced and fun and a great game diversion for when you're looking to kill a little time. So while yes, the game could have been so much more, what we have here is still a very enjoyable PC fighter if you're looking for one.

For a while I was unaware of Metro series, but when I eventually found out about them I wasn't too bothered about them. It seemed ok, but it wasn't my type of game. But few years after I went to the local shop and bought Metro 2033 and Metro Last Light Redux editions for a bargain of a price.
The world of Metro has impressed me with how it is detailed, how these humans struggle for survival, and how depressing it might be. Metro Last Light definitely had more Holywood type of story, but it will never replicate Metro 2033. This game actually kept me playing, even if my eyes were burning from the screen. The game had me fighting for whatever ammo, money and gas filters I could find. The gameplay may not be open-world, but is definitely hostile and will provide plenty of challenge for newbies and veterans alike.

The Metro is a dark place, filled with monsters and human misery, but once you get out to the poisoned surface for the first time you will be shocked at what you will see.

If you are reading this review, it is because you are unsure you should buy the game. So to help you make this decision, read my following experience with the game from an unbiased, lover of survival genre gamer. I had just purchased and played Citadel, a good building game for sure and I recommend if your into custom building games but so far, it was lacking something for me. I was not sucked in and so I watched the streams of Dark and Light. My curiosity grew every day I started another stream or youtube video, as I am sure many of you have. So I bought it, and here is my experience so far.
Reviews are sub par, I know. But hear me out. You load up the game. Clean, easy to read menus and options. HUGE BONUS FOR ME - supports us Ultra Wide Screen gamers. Works great on my 34in Asus Ultra Wide 1440p. !!!!!!
Next, the loading screen, yes it sucks. Takes about 4 or 5 minutes for the loading screen before entering game. Be patient, do not alt tab, or force close. LET IT LOAD. Once it hits a brief glymps of the server list, a loading bar will go across your screen. Then the game loads and shows a percentage.
Once you enter in the game, some days yes, textures take a while to load. Then they load, and the game unwinds I should say and starts to run pretty smooth. Acceptable for me with an alpha title. We are all used to alpha titles, like Ark or Rust or Day Z Standalone. So if you have my mindset, you will like or even LOVE this game as I do.
I have put about 15 hours into this game over 3 days. I was VERY concerned this game would be just like ARK with a different feel. THIS IS SO NOT TRUE. The menus can look familiar, because they are. There is a campfire, thatch houses as you start to build, but comon, what survival game doess't have these items. There are similarities, but who cares, it is what is expected in a survival open world game. Here is the difference and what should suck you in.
IT FEELS LIKE A RPG, in a multiplayer world.  Everything you do, however you play, levels those skills or a skill category in a beautiful menu screen that shows you so very many items you can unlock. Not by clicking a hundred skills or items you learn. But you have to work for it, adding to the longevity to this game. I am level 21 out of 60 I believe, after about 15 hours of working hard. Chopping trees levels your woodworking, and your survival skills. Which unlock crafting wood structures at level 20, not before. So thatch it is for 20 levels. But this makes it exciting, to learn new things down the road, not in a minute or two of work.
I have had ZERO GAME CRASHES. I have had bugs yes, as expected in alpha. But nothing that made me ever want to turn the game off. I would say, maybe, you will consider refunding before the 2 hours, if your not a survival game person. But I encourage you to hang out, it took me about 4 to understand the direction of the game and leveling system. The beastary is beautiful! The creatures are unique for the most part or perfect for the setting of this fantasy world. You can even punch barrels in the existing cities to harvest apples and gold coins to save up and purchase ridable horse mounts from vendors. IT FEELS LIKE AN RPG, not Ark. I promise.
I have only tamed one Boar, road it and it died to a sneaky difficult to see ninja Goblin which comes out more at night and killed my boar! So I have loved the challenge and enjoyment of killing more and more Goblins to level up, since they can knock you out in one or two hits and steal your entire inventory! So I craft a bow or throwing knife and come back for revenge. Every time!
I have LOVED, embarking on an adventure with my guild buddy, arming ourselves with bow and arrows and a few apples harvested from the trees in search for new creatures that own us at times but make us arm up and come back for more until we are victorious! So much fun, NIGHT TIME is scary and dark! Beware.
I encourage you to try this game. Do not only look at the mixed reviews and pass on this. Even if you do for now, it will hopefully get fine tuned and become even better over time. You should just dive in now and enjoy it as I have, for hours and hours to come.

Bit of a 40k nerd so I largely bought this game because I love the books and every Dawn of War game they released.
First thing I love: they didn't make the Space Marine Favor relate to the Blood Ravens in any way (Imperial Fists if you care). Really got sick of those guys...Spess Mehreens are awesome though.
Overall this is a very fun RTS. It has a learning curve but I haven't lost a game besides the occasional assassination or data recovery mission in a awhile; rewarding to go from getting beat up pretty often to having consistent successes as you learn how each ship plays a part in battles. A great place to start is to play with solo skirmish with Imperials, get destroyed by a Chaos fleet that kites you? Play a game as Chaos, try to do the same thing, see how the AI scores hits on you. Learn how to ram and use torpedos, nothing will stop you.
Each race plays very differently and the balance changes they have made since the beta are excellent, the only thing that feels OP is the Eldar's pulsars but that is balanced by their fragile ships--skilled Eldar players still wreck but it's hard to master. I have had a blast learning how to play with each faction in this game and look forward to further expansions.
If you're an RTS fan you should pick this up FOR SURE. If you're a 40k fan then you need to have this in your libarary, stop looking for reasons not to spend $40 on the best 40k game since DOW 2, possibly Dark Crusade.
Negative: The campaign is basically a series of skirmishes linked together with a narrative. After spending a fair bit of time playing the beta and getting several level 8 admirals it feels little redundant. Still fun but I honestly wish they had more scripted missions or "boss" battles with badass ships/things to blow up. There are a few, but it's largely interspersed with a bunch of regular skirmish type battles just like in the solo skirmish mode.
Eldar still feel OP after the nerfs they made. Holoshields were way too hard to get through and they knocked down the invulnerability of an Eldar ship at speed, but they still can be a serious pain to deal with when you have ships doing about 2/3 their base speed. In assassination and data recovery missions agianst them there is almost nothing you can do, which is great fun when I play as Eldar but god help you if you're Imperial or especially Orks.
They destroyed the best skill in the game: micro warp jump. Way too big of an area that you can't use it anymore, not sure why that needed a mega-nerf.
Buy the game and make your own assessment. I'm loving it and expect it to be a game I can come back to for a long time.

These Simbin race games are built upon an ISI physical engine. If you are interested:
An ample of car simulators from Sports Car GT '99 through an array of Simbin racers to RFactor use this awesome physical engine core and the evolution steps of it. For a very subjective opinion (from an amateur racer, track day and car enthusiast) I became a fan of this physical core because of its pure honesty. All the rest of car sim engines are fun to drive because they are exaggerated. ISI based games are fun to drive because for the feel they are the closest to driving a real car around in my opinion.
I believe that the rest makes you a better gamer while ISI based games actually make you a better real-life driver. I have a history with them, I've owned many box versions of ISI based race games through all the years, driving hundreds of hours. There is something with the mechanics that works pretty similar in the reality. For me, one of the main reasons of playing race games besides the fun is the desire of improving my driving skills. Proven more times than I'd could count, the reactions and skills to make decisions near limits learned in these games saved me and others from accidents. Perhaps some lives too. Also they helped to improve my lap times driving on a real track during track days.
This game won't win popularity award from casual racers as it is kind of unforgiving. Sure it has issues like of anything else under the sun, some cars are better modelled than others e.t.c. but all of ISI core games has IT: realistic driving experience and organic feel, also played with a wheel you can learn useful skills that you can apply in real life, too.
About Race 07, graphics are a little outdated in 2017 although it looks decent for its time of release, 2007. As long as it's 20 pixels and a dosen of polygons and feels like a car, I'm okay with it anyway. Today, regard it as a MILF who is a great bang for the buck.
With the full version you get a truckload of tracks from deep down and dirty STCC and WTCC tracks through GP tracks to Nürburgring Nordschleife, dosens of car types and dosens of car models that are pretty different from each other, a minimalistic but flexible race / championship set of rules and that's it. A lot of variation with a touch of minimalism. Not a single piece of unnecessary bullsheet. It is focused on driving and it comes with a long learning curve and skill is needed to keep stuff on the road at the speed. I am absolutely into that.
For me, for the right feel car sounds are very important and most of the cars are modelled well here in my opinion: dirty and raw. Some cars lack a littlebit but the majority sounds and feels pretty good.
If you like Need For Speed games, Burnout Paradise or anything that exaggerates physics in general (there is no problem with that, they are fun just different), just pass ISI based games. You will be extremely frustrated as first you probably could keep the car on the road with the snail-trail only or wreck the car after the first corner - as you would most probably do behind the wheel of a real race car in a real race track anyway. But if you need some clean pure honest driving experience and don't care about bells & whistles and you wish to learn something practical too, maybe you'll like Race 07 (and Sports Car Gt and GT Legends and GTR and RFactor etc) as much as I do.

Great, chaotic fun. Double Action: Boogaloo is rough around the edges in many ways, but it mostly manages to pull through and be a bunch of great, dumb fun. This game, in case you know nothing about it, is a First/Third Person Multiplayer Shooter where you slide, dodge, and jump around to complete objectives. Sadly, there are only 3 objectives: Deliver a briefcase, do allot of killing and try not to die, and race to the finish. Each is just as chaotic and fun, though it does get repetitious after a while. Thankfully, diving around is loads of fun and adds a faster pace and sense of originality to what would have been dull and generic otherwise. It also adds a tactical edge, although few people play this game allot so I don't know what to say about that. And yeah, not many people really play this. It's a shame, but it's true.
Disregarding that, this game has about 5-or-so character classes, but unlike other games, these don't determine how the character you play as looks. I think it's also worth noting that they basically stole the model of Nick from L4D2 for one of the characters, but that doesn't really bother me too much. What does bother me is that balancing can be iffy in certain areas. While no one option is too powerful for its own good, certain ones can suppress other options. These include choosing a bouncer and going fists only, or choosing a sharpshooter and using the Mac Daddy to unhealthy extents. The ♥♥♥♥ing... Mac Daddy. The maps themselves aren't too shabby, although do have flaws. It's just a shame there isn't a lot of them and the community for this game is, once again, slowly dying.
Which brings me to why I recommend Double Action: Boogaloo. Why? Friends. This game is awesome for LAN Play, and just as amazing when you're going head to head with your friend(s) and a few pesky bots in the way. True, this sentiment is accurate for most games, but in the case of this game, it could not be any more accurate. If you have friends to play this with, really give it a shot. If you're a complete loner and don't have any friends... well, pick it up anyways. It might be worth it, but I can't really say so for you.

RACE 07 is a racing simulator developed by SImbin and focused primarily on the WTCC 2007 . I first played this game years ago and enjoyed it tremendously, and it still holds up today.
Pros:
-Good handling. Tried a variety of inputs, from Xbox controller, Steering wheels and keyboard. Works well with most, although keyboard handling was the most iffy.
-Graphics are still pretty good for a 2007 game.
-The game has a lot of mods and expansions. Most expansions are great, and others were okay. The most notable expansion, and possibly the best is the GTR Evolution expansion. Mods can also be downloaded online which enhance the experience of the game even more
Cons:
-Playerbase has declined by a landslide and, considering the age of the game, it is expected. There is not alot of people still playing this, which can be off putting.
-Compatibility is sometimes a problem on newer platforms.
Overall, this is a great precusor of what once was a great racing simulator. If you are a car and racing simulator fanatic, give this a go.

I will warn that certain animals (the lynx, the lynx cub, the adult badger, the baby bear, and the eagle) you must own other Might and Delight content. However, this is not as big a complaint as it used to be. They are adding more and more animals to the game, all of which unlock in the game itself, and there is getting to be a lot more variety.
I will stress that this is
going to appeal to everyone, but if you're looking for a casual, peaceful MMO experience, I can't recommend it enough.

After exploring much of what the game has to offer in its current state, I can say that the story is well written. It was a first time for me to encounter a visual novel that allows you to influence the actions and the state of not only a single character but a multitude of them. The prequel mostly focuses on the prince but considering how nicely written the story is, I will expect the full version to have a more balanced viewpoint among the characters. I also loved how the readers are able to 'hear' the characters' thoughts as it allows us to understand their personalities more though I would have preferred it if I weren't able to hear what Elisa was thinking because she is a heroine. As I can see it, she is one of those hard-to-reach type of woman in literature and concealing her thoughts would have added more mystery to her character. But that is only my opinion and I do not say that it was a bad choice. In fact, I would say that it worked just fine as the thoughts of such characters were hardly or even never revealed in other works and it was a refreshing change of pace for me. Ah, how I wish not to meet such a woman in real life. Just don't overdo it though, for I would say that the readers would enjoy a little bit of teasing but definitely would not like it if her actions became very predictable.
With regards to the art, I found the character sprites to be well drawn and I liked it when the corresponding choices were accompanied by chibi (small and cute) version of the characters. The music is soothing and fits the scenario well. But the execution is not well made. Excluding the typographical and punctuation errors that I have found, there were times that the transition is very slow or not transitioning at all that I had to click multiple times just to get to the next line or scenario. I also wished there was a backlog so I could reread parts that I failed to comprehend or misread. The skip button (control) is not apparent unless you paid attention and read the things in the config menu. And when I pressed the fullscreen button, instead of going fullscreen, the screen instead zooms to the upper left portion of the game interface. I hope you could fix these things.
Regardless, I enjoyed the game and I wish it was longer. Kudos to the developers and I wish you well in your future endeavors. I hope you continue to create more games as wonderful as this one.

Now for the serious review. These days, it seems like the only stick that shooter games are measured by whether or not they have good multiplayer. I hate to break it to you, but the shutdown of Gamespy means that Battlefront II, to my knowledge, has no multiplayer. But I don't care, because it's some of the best gaming fun I have ever had, and am still having since I bought the first Battlefront when it was first released on console. I've never played it with other humans, only the bots. The bots are not dumb. They are very competent, and you have to have some skill to win against them. And it's nice that your bot teammates are competent. There is a story campaign. There is a freeform mode called Galactic Conquest where you build fleets, recruit troops, and literally conquer the Star Wars planet by planet and battle by battle. And of course, you can just load up any map you want and play conquest, or even neat modes like capture the flag.
The game is also a great reproduction of the battle machines, soldiers, and planets of the Star Wars universe, so it's a must have for any Star Wars fan and gamer. Oh, and you can play as characters like Darth Vader. The gameplay is loads of fun, it's bug-free, the mechanics are spot-on and smooth, and the graphics are good for when it was released.
Why are still here? Get to the battlefront, soldier!

This is a decent fighting game and with fun and entertaining game mechanics. However the Steam release is also full of bugs and other issues. Get it from sale. It's worth playing if you've never played Dead or Alive games before but for the fans of the series it's a bit disappointing release. After all we did have some expectations for this port. The game uses older version of the game engine. It also lacks content compared to the console release.
The PC integration is almost non-existent with very limited graphics options. Resolution support is not done properly and you can only choose from a limited selection of 16:9 resolutions. 4:3 and 16:10 support would have been a nice thing to have. As an added bonus there's a support for 4K. The game runs 30FPS in menus and in cutscenes but the actual fighting is 60FPS.
Game has bare minimum keyboard support and no mouse support for menus. You cannot rebind the very nonsensical default keyboard keys to anything more standard and sensible. For example instead of the Return key to accept menu selection and the Esc to exit menu the game uses M and L keys. The UI doesn't actually show you what the keyboard keys are during the fight so player is pretty much left reading the manual or guessing what the keys might be. The game absolutely requires a gamepad of some description to work properly.
The sound options are also very limited. The game is also bit unstable and you can expect it to crash at any given moment for any unknown reason there is. Data corruption may or may not occur in some instances and you have to reset your profile.
The promised on-line multi-player component is still not properly out yet months after it was promised that it would be. The existing beta version is unstable and likely to not work. And as a result of that perhaps the biggest selling point of this game, the multi-player community, is very small if it exists at all. I've not managed to connect into a single multi-player game thus far.
Modding of this game has been prohibited by the Koei-Tecmo and Team Ninja, so that they could sell you tons of expensive costumes. Don't buy that stuff, you don't need it. Needless to say people still modded this game and that might have caused Team Ninja to delay much needed patches and other fixes for this release as a way to punish people for modding the game.
Because of the attitude of the developer and publisher towards the PC gaming community I'm very tempted to give this game a negative recommendation. However considering that this is the first PC release of the series in a really long time and I genuinely do like the game I'm giving it a positive recommendation. However I won't be supporting Koei-Tecmo in future as willingly as I did when I got this game.
Overall I've got very mixed feelings about this game release. If they'd fix even the basic stuff and use standardised on keys then it would be ok game. At least it runs decently even on older hardware and when it works it does work rather well.

I ran around as a badger for a while, then remembered I could be a lynx so I swapped. I ran into another lynx and a goat at the central tree, and we adventured together for about an hour with no real purpose. Just exploring, finding things to collect. Swam down a river. Found a waterfall and the other lynx fell off. The goat and I were sad and there was much :'(. Then we circled around the ravine and found our lynx on the other side and spent a minute running in happy circles around each other and going :D! Then we climbed to the very top of a cave just because we could, encouraging each other through the tricker jumps with meows and huffs and :)'s, and when we made it we sat at the top and admired the view for a few minutes and that's about when I realized I was enjoying myself more aimlessly exploring with two complete strangers for the past hour than I did during my 3 hours running quests on a combat-focused MMO last night.
There's an odd sense of instant camraderie that I think comes with the limited communication and lack of explicit goals. You explore, you find collectibles, those collectibles unlock more animals, fur patterns for the animals, and more emotes for the animal you're on, allowing slightly more communication. I felt like a part of the group as soon as we set off, following each other's lead and getting excited when we found something cool. I was legitimately saddened to leave my new little pack when I had to stop playing for a bit, and am certainly looking forward to jumping back into this for more peaceful adventures than I expected to be when I clicked 'play' this morning just to see what this was about.
This is definitely a different sort of game than most, but I don't think that's a bad thing. If you liked the Shelter games this one is definitely worth your time, and if you never tried them, maybe this can be your introduction. For $3, who couldn't use a little relaxing exploration with a little pack of new friends?

Each gem color signifies mana, which are used to cast skills, which you learn as your character gains levels and completes side-quest puzzles. Each match is a battle against an enemy that you encounter on your quest. Your character traverses a map that is similar to the world map in Final Fantasy Tactics. To compare this to other bejeweled games, such as: Puzzle Quest 2, Legend of Fae, Bejeweled 3, Marvel Puzzle Quest...

One fine day a baby Lynx cub was wondering the meadows alone, he collects flowers, swims in the rivers and takes a relaxing nap by the enchanting waterfalls, he is soon woken by the howling of another animal, he glances around only to spot a pair of older Lynxes upon the horizon.
He pushes himself to his feet and lets out a little howl of his own to try and attract their attention, fearing he has not been heard he decides to take a walk in their direction to see what all the noise was about.
The two older stronger animals were not alone, there was also a Frog a Deer and a Rabbit present.
They appeared to be paying a lot of attention to a huge rock which was stood before them, as the baby Lynx approached, the rock shattered leaving some shiny objects before them, which seemed to please the other animals as they proudly smiled, howled and jumped for joy.
The cub gave a shy look at them all as the Frog urged him to follow them, the little Lynx did so, throughout the day, the animals wandered everywhere breaking rocks, collecting flowers, even playing football together.
Soon the night began to fall and the animals slowly started showing sad tearful faces as they faded away.
The little Lynx cub howled, his cheeks wet with tears too as the land became seemingly more empty.
He soon heard a rustling somewhere close by, looking around he spied a pair of badgers coming towards him, an Eagle flew just above them in the sky, like he was guiding them.
The little Lynx cub smiled to himself, filled with a sense of well-being and safety, he flipped onto his back to watch the stars, the other animals gave him a smile as they passed by.
He had realised he had found a land where animals can run free from danger, the Meadow felt like home, he didn't know how he had got there, but he knew this was a land with a place for all, it was a place for love where there was everlasting peace................
Well that was a day in the Meadow now for the review, if you haven't already guessed I'm very much a fan of all the shelter games, I admit I was a little sceptical about this one when it first appeared but that didn't last long!! I honestly have very few complaints about this game, its relaxing, beautiful scenery and atmosphere are just what you need in your life!
Perhaps that statement says more about my life than I want it to... lol.
There is quite a range of animals to play as, some are mentioned above, I do have to say the worse choice is the Eagle, I find it relatively slow, you can't land or pick things up, I believe it's been deliberately made that way as a guiding animal though which to be fair is a great idea, although it would be nice to at least be able to land and have a walk about.
(The dark Eagle plus a few of the other animals can be unlocked from the start by possessing the whole shelter collection including soundtracks and books BUT all can be unlocked by simply playing and searching)
I highly recommend you try this game! What you waiting for! go get it! ;-)

A fantastic reboot of a dead franchise and a game which has heralded the rebirth of a genre on PC.
----
If you ever played with toy soldiers as a kid, this is the game for you.
There are some minor annoyances in the pacing of the thing as a whole - the early game tends to be a lot more interesting than the late game, which tends to feel like it drags on a bit. The cinematic combat animations can feel like putting commas, in the middle, of sentences, at, inappropriate times.
Overall though, what a fantastic game for tactical nerds like me. Soldier customisation gets you invested in your troops and the base building R&D side of things really feels like it's important - how you manage your technology is an integral factor in your success.
Also, this is a game where it's entirely possible to invest dozens of hours only to fail. Kind of a novel concept in today's gaming landscape of kid gloves and hand holding. The stakes are high and the tension is real.
Is it worth getting? If you're even remotely interested - Absolutely.
----

adds a lot of great things to the experience and if you want a more classic feeling, lengthy, involved and difficult experience with a bunch of added features then the (free)
mod has got you covered there too.
The sequel, XCOM 2, is also fantastic.

FTL is complex, challenging, and ever-changing.

I loved the table top game and was hoping to have a multiplayer game that simulated it.
Stylistically the ship models and general feel are spot on. However, the gameplay mechanics are… odd.
Just to frame this, an imperial cruiser is around 5 kilometres (3 miles) long and has a mass of almost 30 megatonnes (around the mass of 100 empire state buildings). These things are colossal behemoths of architectural magnificence in space. They are lumbering giants that bring entire star systems to their knees.
In the game they bounce off of each other like ping pong balls.
These ships are many kilometres long, but every ship in the game can burn retros and flip end on end in seconds. While I could possibly understand that with Eldar with their incredibly agile high-tech ships, watching a massive imperial ship do similar makes me wonder at the crew being splattered against the interior walls from the G-forces this would involve.
As a consequence of these immersion breaking dynamics, a lot of the multiplayer games I’ve played come down to ramming and bouncing ships out of the way at a speed that seems completely at odds with the scale being represented.
In my mind the speed of the ships needs to be drastically reduced and ramming impacts need to be much more… impactful.
The crazy dynamics aside, and without making reference to the oodles of bugs I have encountered so far (full release my rear) my other real issue in-game is the complete disregard for squad support.
More than a handful of ships in your fleet and micro becomes a real pain in the posterior, even with the ‘tactical cogitator’ which allows you to slow down time to make orders more easily. Micro is NOT helped by the fact that my three identical Cobra’s can’t fly in formation, nor can they all launch torpedoes at the same time. Want to put the torpedo firing on auto to try to mitigate this? “Scr*w you,” says the game “I’m just going to launch these suckers when I feel like it then”.
However, these frustrations pale in comparison to my biggest bugbear in the game – the multiplayer matching system. You get NO say over how many points you want to play, what game type you want to play, nothing. I want to practice a bit in some nice small 300 point cruiser clash games where I can micro comfortably and learn the strengths and weaknesses of my new ships, learn tactics and explore the game properly against live opponents. I cannot do this when I am placed in a 600 point protect the convoy mission where I have only one light cruiser due to mounting casualties and the opponent can just full ahead through the ping pong escorts I lay in his path in a vain attempt to shield my transports.
I really hope that these issues are resolved over the coming weeks, as I really want a BG game that I can love, but I am disappointed that it has been fully released in the state it is currently in. I was the first of my group of BG loving friends to buy the game and will have to advise them not to get it until the game reflects better the game we know and love rather than a game of destruction derby in space.

It is such an enjoyable experience there is no person I would not reccomend this to. Coming off "Saint's Row the Third", I was enjoying my time with the franchise, but it didn't stand out to an amazing degree, but this game took everything I hated about 3, fixed it, and added in all new things to enjoy.
Well, I'll start with the central combat mechanics, which I would say are overall better than in 3, with a ton more weapon variety, including all sorts of crazy and amazingly fun weapons, including the Dubstep Gun and the Black Hole Launcher (My personal favorite!), though alot of the more ordinary guns feel alot weaker than in 3. For example, the Alien SMG felt more like it was firing air powered brussel sprouts than laser shots. Also, I feel the weapon balance is a bit off. Though it may be really fun, and I definately prefer it to the alternative, from a technical standpoint, I shoud not be able to one shot with a completely unimproved melee weapon, recovering all lost health from a pickup he drops. Later on, I would clear entire flashpoints with nothing but a tentacle bat or a laser sword. Combat also includes the brand new superpowers, which are mostly really fun to play around with, and can do some real damage. However, I think alot of powers are either useless, or made obsolete by other powers. Why would I shoot a fireball at one enemy when I can surround myself in a temporary aura of fire, burning all nearby enemies as I get them well acquainted with my tentacle?
Alot of people point at the character customization in 2 as being incredible, and say they were dissappointed in customization in 3 and 4. Having very briefly played 2, I can say there is such a thing as too much detail, and that has it. 4 has plenty of choices to make whatever character you want, including different voices with different dialogue, though I found the developers really didn't put a whole lot of effort into the voices other then Male Voice 1 and maybe Male Voice 2, since, in my first playthrough as Female Voice 1, the subtitles constantly said something different to my character, which is a minor complaint, but it really annoyed me. Another complaint is they didn't seem to build on the wardrobe from 3, and rather replaced it, so alot of clothes I liked from before are gone, in favor of four of the same fedora with a slightly different rim.
Until I heard complaints about it and actually took a good look at the map, I couldn't even tell it was Steelport again. The jump and sprint powers make travel so much fun for awhile, though it did eventually become routine, and that verticality to moving on foot makes it feel like a different city, at least to me. However, that hits upon one of my main complaints: cars. In 3, cars were vital, and in 4, they added tons of new cars, most of which are incredibly interesting and funny in concept and execution. There's a ♥♥♥♥ing man-a-pult, for God's sake! However, I was almost never tempted to use vehicles of any kind, since traveling on foot was so much faster and more efficient, which is a real shame, because vehicles seem so interesting. The problem is really exemplified whenever a mission requires you drive around and you realize how much you want to get out, jump into the air, and dive nuke a city block.
The story is honestly pretty shallow in its broad concept. Break the simulation by doing activities while rescuing your crew. It's a means to an end, but alot of the individual missions, particularly the rescue missions are very fun, though many of the normal missions are very very repetitive and even kind of 'grindy', you could say, which is one of the biggest criticisms of the game by most. But all these missions present a bonding experience to get you to care about each and every character, and that's really the games strongest point: the characters. I absolutely love every character in this game. They are all well defined, and the game lets you spend casual bonding time with each one to make you actually enjoy having them around, not to mention every one is enjoyable in their own way. I'd imagine this would be rapidly trumped in a story-focused game, but as someone who hasn't been exposed much to those, one of my favorite character moments came in this game, and it was when Pierce and the Boss start singing along to the radio during a mission. The dialogue, humor, and sense of absolute careless fun from the voice actors makes it a scene with not much depth, but just a flat out good time, a scene that just makes you feel happy and invested, which is really what games are about, right? And the ending. I ended up getting the good ending first time, and it is such a good ending. No poetic depth, no thought-provoking parting message, no final riddle, but just a good, light-hearted ending that made you feel accomplished and all warm inside, seeing the characters have just a good a time as you.
Switching over to the other main strength, let's talk about the humor. This game is filled with absolutely hillarious moments. One big complaint I have about 3 is it really just has one joke:♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ BUMS,♥♥♥♥♥♥ SEX, GET IT, IT'S FUNNY RIGHT?, which can be good when done right and in moderation, but was seriously overdone. This game has references, parodies, that oh so random humor that's fun when done right, which it is here, original dialogue humor, and it still retains that dirty humor from 3, but in a much better balance with the rest of it to make those jokes consistently funny. The dialogue is amazing, and I willingly listened to all of it and wanted more just because it was so good.
In conclusion, I highly reccomend this game. Sure there are some goods and bads I left out, but I think this covers the important points, at least in my experiences. It had plenty of flaws and missed alot of potential in alot of its elements, but the action, powers, characters, and humor in this game, combined with an obvious sense of absolute dedication to fun has this game stand out as being superb, and I truly cannot understand how people would rather have some dark and serious "Grand Theft Auto" clone over this gem.

Braid is a platforming puzzle game which was released on Xbox Live initially in 2008 before later being ported onto PC in 2009.  You play the character, Tim, as you attempt to rescue the princess from a monster (very cliche!).
Game play in Braid looks like a very generic puzzle platformer on face value, however with the addition of the special ability to manipulate time by rewinding and fast forwarding, you can find yourself in some very unique situations.  The other gameplay elements are very much the same though, running, jumping and climbing around a standard platforming environment.  Each level in the game adds a little bit of a change to the time bending ability which keeps things fresh each time you progress.
Braid is a very simple looking game; the graphics are standard two 2D style, however they do have a very pleasing charm to it. The art style within the game is just gorgeous to look at. The art work alone apparently took over a year to produce, and you can really tell a huge amount of heart and effort went into creating it.
The plot in Braid is very intriguing indeed. You are certainly in for a few twists and turns and very unpredictable outcomes throughout - I was personally in no way shape or form expecting the end of the game to end up how it did; and that is a nice change from a game since they can sometimes become very predictable. After finishing the game, you are able to find additional text that expand the story even further too.
The music used in Braid was selected by the developer himself, from licensed music, this was done to reduce the cost in the development stage. What I really liked about the music is that each tune has a different feel to it when you re-wind time in game; its a really small element, but it makes a huge difference to how you feel when playing.
I found Braid to be a difficult game; purely because I am the worst person possible when it comes to 1) Puzzles and 2) Platformers. Put the two together and it's just a mess.  At times I had to resort to a trusty walkthrough to work it out, but for the majority of the time I was able to figure out each level on my own. Puzzle veterans may well find this game's puzzles to be easy, and still struggle on the platforming element to it!
Braid took me just over six hour to complete; this was purely a run through the story mode; there are a lot of Jigsaw pieces to find in the game which result in achievements, so will add a couple more hours of gameplay. Some of which are unobtainable at the first time of coming across them, so a little bit of replaying older levels is needed to collect them all. However I personally see no reason to replay the game only for the achievements.  The story and gameplay 100% linear.
I had no technical problems whilst playing. Braid can be played at all resolutions up to 4k in windowed mode and full screen. A controller, as always with platformers is highly recommended to play but can also be played with keyboard.
To sum up, I am only going to Recommend Braid, simply because the two genres put together are my least favorite of all time, however take that with a pinch of salt because if you really enjoy puzzle/platformers, then this game is certainly for you and you need to pick it up, even at the full price of £6,99 this game is a steal!

This may be the greatest puzzle platformer ever made. What's so great about it? Firstly, the timetravel-based mechanics make for unconventional and diffult puzzles. Learning to think about yourself in time loops is extremely challenging and rewarding. With each world (or level), the game introduces a new timetravel mechanic that adds another layer of complexity to the puzzles. The puzzles become so hard that at certain points I had headaches and had to stop playing. But that pain is worth the payoff of finally being able to figure out a puzzle after spending an hour steaming at the ears. You feel like a God, until you reach the next puzzle.
But the best payoff of all is the twist at the end of the story. The story is primarily told through books read at the beginning of each world. The writing in this game is extremely contemplative and existential, dealing with topics like memories, identity, and the nature of relationships. The writing beautifully weaves into the timetravel mechanics for each world. The design of the mechanics, their ability to be relevant to the story, and their ability to make the game's puzzles more complex at the same time, is the product of genius. The story, like a poem, doesn't explain itself. It leaves itself open to interpretation. The replayability of this game is in the different meanings that can be thought of upon further playthroughs of the game.
The music of the game fits the aestitic of the art style and reflects the mood of the story very well. The gravity of the twist near the end of the story is helped by the music. The music plays a role in telling the game's story.
In conclusion, this game is the greatest puzzle platformer because it ties the story, gameplay mechanics, and music together SO WELL that I would go back in time to experience the game all over again for the first time (small Braid joke). If you like puzzle platformers and you don't buy this game, WHAT ARE YOU EVEN DOING?

Braid's become kinda legendary since it's release. It's usually touted as one of the few games that manages to be "art" or at least it's managed to be considered art outside of the gaming community, which is apparently what people are really shooting for.

It's a puzzle-platformer where everything is built around time manipulation mechanics including going back in time, stopping time, speeding up time, etc.
The story and gameplay though is a deconstruction (there's that art game thing coming in) of traditional video game tropes, specifically the old Mario games.
The art and music are beautiful, and there's a lot of subtle hidden themes revealed through writing samples you gain throughout the game.
There's far more secrets as well, some are insanely difficult to find. Just search special ending for braid in youtube and you'll be astounded.
Overall it's definitely recomended. It's fun to play and explore, although some sections are very difficult.

Great match-3 game with plot in world of Warlords. The first and the best of them all in this series in my opinion. On upper level it have plot, main and side-quests, interesting sidekicks and somewhat strategic map (but level of strategy quickly diminishes to "capture them all" level). On mechanic level it have item forging, beast capture, and three different types of "simple" puzzle fight (but all three with the same rules). Game's only problem for me is the length of the end-game battles, that can be prolonged to more than ten minutes, if you haven't right equip. It makes endgame quite boring.

A lost opportunity.
If you are looking for something like Gratituous Space/Tank Battles, go on, unfortunately this is not the naval version of those games. The Campaign is short, the ships customizations are very limited (e.g.: very low number of maximum guns, you can't use extra space for anything, unlike in GSB, where you could e.g.: armor up), plus the battles are done in a weird, "give orders for a virtual turn then try to execute it" way.
The ships can't avoid environmental hazards on the way, nor will the UI warn you of these. They will even collide, and you can't control them as one battlegroup, just individually. The maps are more so than not too narrow and too small, etc. On the flip side, it seems equally easy to lead enemies into damaging environments, e.g.: beaching them.
Maybe it has some redeeming features in multiplayer, but looking at the single player side, I really doubt it. It has no replay value, a very short single player, and lots of ideas that should have been explored fully.
Also, sometimes you just lose your save game.

GET THE FREE VERSION FIRST!  One major issue with this game is antiquated controller programming.  So get the free version, make sure you can set the controller up right, THEN think about buying the game.  Now, on to the review...
If you're looking for a deep fighting game to play off line every now and again, the game will deliver.  Every character has a huge list of moves you can learn and practicing will definitely improve your game.  The graphics are good enough.  The game is perfect for stereoscopic (e.g. 3D Vision) users with the action taking place right at the range where eye triangulation works best and a small modification will push the interface out of the screen to prevent most of the depth crossing.
A lot of folks are complaining about overpriced DLC.  What they are missing is that the DLC is totally optional.  There's a couple of fighters (and those DLCs are actually reasonably priced) but the rest are just costumes.  What's more, the modding scene for this game has provided a huge list of additional costumes you can have for free.
That said, there are plenty of valid issues with this game.  The controllers are the biggest issue but you can now dodge that bullet by trying the game out before you pay.  If you're looking to play with your friends over the network, look elsewhere.  There's no lobby system in the PC version.  It also has stability issues.  The game saves enough that crashing isn't too painful but still....
So yeah - if you want to have some fun with a single player fighting game and would rather fight with buxom babes than watch somebody's head get ripped off and the blood drank, this is a good one.  If you've got 3D Vision, it's a really good one!

Leviathan: Warships was surprisingly easy to jump into: the simple commands and clean interface allow for strategy to come to the fore. The movement system creates the feel of a tabletop game, as well as giving you the amount of seconds it will take you to get to the destination.
With around 10-15 different weapons and add-ons you can bolt to your ship, there is a strategy here as well, rather than relying on a myriad of weird weapons. It also means the game is much easier balanced, as each weapon has its obvious strengths and weaknesses.
I hear the multiplayer is fantastic, and I recommend picking up a copy next time it comes on sale.
And downsides?
The networking is the worst implementation of server connection I have ever seen. If the game can't connect when you launch the game, there is no "re-try" button. The game must be exited and relaunched. However, this isn't such a bad thing as it launches in a swift 10-15 seconds. Also, your saves, replays, ships and stats are all per-server, which just simply sucks. However, if you stick to one server, you'll be fine and dandy. There is also an offline, and again that has its own separate saves etc.
But don't let that put you off! Really, this game is jazz-a-listic.

It's Blender. A triumph of free open-source development - almost everything you can do in other 3D graphics programs that cost upwards of thousands (modelling, texturing, simulating, rendering, and more), you can do here with equally good results. The interface has greatly improved over the years in terms of ease-of-use and intuitivity (I say this as someone who first tried Blender several years ago and found it unusably difficult) and makes 3D work quick and even pretty fun. I'll admit I'm not the type to use this for massive team projects or anything, but even a simple hobbyist like me has found a lot to love and make in this program - and so have thousands of others.
I highly recommend getting the Steam version of this program over the
download - not that there's any difference in terms of features, but the automatic updating that Steam provides is a wonderful time-saver, and it provides a quick access point alongside your library.

Lara Croft returns now to a 4-player twin stick shooter adventure.  The core mechanics of the game are very similar to Guardians of Light, but this game just doesn't seem to compare.  Puzzles seem a lot more challenging but much less creative.  Many of the puzzles merely require precise timing to complete rather than ingenious thinking to find the solutions.  Additionally, Guardians of Light required the players to work in tandem to complete puzzles but Temple of Osiris often seems to focus puzzles on one specific character, leaving the other players to merely spectate.  Combat retains the twin-stick shooter style, but the combat in Temple of Osiris just feels lacking in... something.
This release has several technical issues, such as the camera zooming so far out you can't see your characters or the characters randomly not retaining items and gems after quitting the game.  This is unbelievably frustrating, and is the prime reason why I would not recommend this game.
I like the added mechanics that make this game a different experience than Guardians of Light.  The game now has an overworld that you can explore to access the different tombs.  Additionally, you can control the weather and the day and night cycles.  Some areas and features of the map are only accessible under a specific day/night and weather combination.  This is a nice touch, but largely unnecessary.  The main point of difference I enjoyed (or would have enjoyed without the game-breaking bugs) is the chests that you can open to get new items.  Unfortunately, the game always seemed to lose the rare and uncommon items I found in the more expensive chests, plus all the gems I spent to get those items.
The game would probably be a lot better if you could play through in one sitting to avoid the save issues, but that is an unreasonable expectation.  I enjoyed the game somewhat, but I would have enjoyed it a lot more if it actually worked properly.  Bugs aside, the game does leave a lot to be desired in the core mechanics of puzzles and combat.
I did not experience any of the other game-breaking bugs most players seemed to have reported in the past.  The game never lost my progress in the campaign, it just repeatedly lost my inventory.

Quick Summary: Isometric shooter/puzzler, very similar to its predecessor Lara Croft and the Guardian of Light. Again the game is built for multi-player co-op (up to 4 players) and if you’re playing by yourself the dungeon puzzles will be slightly different since you’ll need to do everything yourself. Also, this time around you collect money (gems) to buy weapons/jewelry from regenerating treasure chests scattered around the game world. Unfortunately Temple of Osiris seems to run more poorly than Guardian of Light in terms of frame rate and loading, despite looking nearly identical in graphics.
You play one of 4 characters depending on whether you’re playing single player or co-op. You’ll be Lara Croft if you’re by yourself, otherwise you’ll be Carter, Isis, or Horus. The last two are Egyptian gods who are aiding you against the main bad guy Set (don’t count on your allies having any super powers though). Your primary goal in this game is to put all the pieces of the dismembered god Osiris back together in order to challenge Set and keep him from raining destruction on the Earth. You’re not the only one with friends though, a few powerful Egyptian deities are teamed up with Set and will come after you throughout the game.
As mentioned before, the game is top down isometric (like the Diablo games) but you navigate three dimensional dungeons with jumping, scrabbling up low platforms, grappling onto hooks, and puzzle solving. The “Temple of Osiris” is rather like an open world game where you navigate a decently large map looking for “tombs” that you can enter and play/replay as much as you want. The reasons to replay a tomb are to grind for more money or beat “challenges” (such as beating the tomb in under a specific time). Each challenge gives you a small prize, such as unlocking a gun or jewelry.
Like Guardian of Light, Lara and her cronies have access to a lot of firepower throughout the game. The default firearm is Lara’s famous dual pistols with infinite ammo, but as you find more powerful guns, these weapons all have limited ammo (ammo boxes pretty easy to find). Unlike Guardian of Light, this time you can also find jewelry (rings and amulets) which have both + and -. For example a ring could increase your gun damage but lower your resistance to damage.  The jewelry is separated into rarities (common, uncommon, rare, legendary) and the better ones only have +’s with no drawbacks. You’ll find a lot of gems throughout your tomb raiding, and you’ll be spending them as fast as you find them (when you open a treasure chest you get a random gun or ring/amulet).
Pros:
+The game has a decent story and some fun boss battles.
+More replay value than Guardian of Light with the new random loot system.
+More players possible in a single game (4 people now, opposed to 2 before).
Cons:
-Worse performance than the previous game. Even people with high level hardware report stuttering and frame rate drops.
-If you’re into Steam achievements, they’re harder to get in this game than in the previous one. It’s really hard to get 4 people into the same game for the 4 player achievements because not many people seem to be playing online.  Also, there’s no “drop in” multiplayer. You have to host a game and wait for people to join before you can start it. This is due to the puzzles rearranging themselves based on how many people are in the game.
Overall the game is fun and can take you a few days to finish. If you liked Guardian of Light, you should enjoy Temple of Osiris. By the way, the DLC don’t seem to be for gameplay (such as extra tombs) so you should be fine with the vanilla game.

I consider myself a veteran of interactive stories genre and a somewhat skeptical person, but I have to admit that Lost Crew did really impress me.

* Great immersive story. You really want to find a way to help those people and find out what's going on.

* Its insanely hard to reach any real ending, much less the perfect one. The best I did was 67% happy ending. But each time you really want to try and make it work!
* It has somewhat unique interactive fiction game mechanics. You won't find another game like it on Steam and I doubt you've ever played something like this before.
Cons:
* The 'tutorial' at the beginning is really messy and will likely annoy you. Please suffer through it.
* There is lots of trial and error and restarting. But each time there's something new, so you won't ever be bored.
* Again, very hard. There is no full walkthrough that I know of, so prepare to fail if you're not persistent enough.
Much respect to the developers, really hope to see new titles.

At first I was a fan of the unique nature of this game where you need to reset time as you learn new information.  However you aren't really solving anything but more so checking off different bad routes in order to get good information and then take the bad routes.  In reality there's only one "puzzle" in the entire game and that is solely due to the fact that the information needed to solve the situation is never recorded (unlike all other information in the game that helps you progress).  Basically the game creates artificial difficulty by not following its own rules.
I got near the end of the game (you must save all crew members to achieve the ending) and proceeded to still have not found some information needed to succeed.  Now I know how to get the information but in order to get it I need to undo all the work I did to get so close to the ending and then set things up incorrectly so that Michael feels compelled to tell me the information I need even though I know Michael has the information I need.  You'll find you need to purposelly achieve fail states in order to get the right information you need to achieve the one ending the game has.
The game is entirely linear with only one correct route and only one way to go about accomplishing that one route.  By the point I was at with the game I opted to just uninstall the game and write this review instead of restarting over as explained previously.
The game has a unique concept but the required amount of restarting just to get information you the player know to ask certain characters for (but can't) is arbitrary and therefore bad design.  I can't ask Michael for the information he has about the situation I'm going to fail until I restart and put Michael into a failure state and then I can ask him about the information that I the player (you play as yourself so you have all knowledge the protagonist has) already know he has.
The plot of the game isn't all that interesting anyway so I doubt the pay off is even worth it to finish it.  It's worth 2 bucks I suppose so at least the developer knows the correct price point.  It's only worth playing if you're interested in seeing the mechanic of time restarting used poorly.

Because of certain issues which I'll go into below, some of the game modes are really quite hard when you have no idea how to play the game. Genuinely wondered if it was a scripted defeat the first time (it wasn't).
I've only ever had one CTD error. For my system at least, which is a few years old now, it seems stable.
Generally, individual movement of ships or fleet is fun. The kinds of overall strategy you need to use in some game modes is where there's a bit of a problem. It's not a game breaker (well, at least not to me, though you might feel differently if you intend to pvp) but there's definitely an issue with how some game modes play out.
I'm not entirely sure if I can put my finger on why, whether it's balancing between races, or if it's translating the way the Battlefleet Gothic tabletop game works into a video game. But there's definitely something amiss - something I hope will get better as the game is patched (sadly gone are the days when a game arrived and worked how it was intended from the get-go).
In a nutshell, some of the mission types don't work exactly as (I suspect) intended. As the Imperium in a campaign mission you often end up chasing down a certain enemy ship (in game types like assassination or data recovery) which is far faster than you possibly can be. The solution always seems to be try to shoot for engines and block them into a corner. Of space. Which makes no sense, but that's not really the problem.
The problem is you generally have 3 minutes or less to stop that enemy escaping/ nab the data, so if you do anything other than use your "all ahead full" ability to scoot after them, ignoring everything else, before trying to shoot the engines while herding them into a corner, you seem to lose. So it's not boring exactly, but it does seem to be the only possible strategy, and I'd imagine against a chaos or eldar player (faster ships) online probably quite irritating.
The experience I've had of Battlefleet has been very positive, and much better than any of the umpteen other games Games Workshop have thrown their license at recently.

Very good game. Like deep feeling of Mother Russia.
PROS
1. Realistic Combat
I was very awed by the way the monsters moved in combat. The movements looked fluid as opposed to combat in Half Life, where the fight between characters are very "blockish" or "robotic". E.g. The watchers attacking Bourbon and Artyom while moving to Riga Station.
2. Interactive Background
It is amazing to see the demons fly around in the background and see them swoop into the active zone. Compared to other games, where the background is just an unending cinematic loop, this provides a sense of realism. E.g. The demons flying around Moscow.
3. Moral Points
It is interesting to note that there are points that will affect your morals in this game. While it is not explicitly shown, it is a good guide to note.
4. Traps
Holes in the ground, tripwires, hidden cans. All these traps make the game so much more exciting.
5. Sneaking
There are some occasions where you can sneak by and avoid combat totally. This really gives the game variety. If you don't want to, you can fight.
6. Story
Some Cthulu-like parts included. Very interesting. The dream modes don't really make a lot of sense but it is an interesting aspect.
CONS
1. Movement
Following characters around is not smooth. E.g. Bourbon leaving Exhibition to use the tunnels. He will walk to a point and rotate about that point before continuing his walk.
2. Guns
Very crappy. For a country that makes tons of weapons, it is strange that their post-apocalyptic nightmare will have such rudimentary weapons like the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. You would think that their technology would at least be in the 21st century, not Cold-War era.
3. Repetitive model
The adults look the same. In 2 different zones, the children scribble on the floor wearing the same clothes. Very boring.
4. Lousy Tutorials
Tutorials not teach you how to use the sticky grenade or the knife throw.
5. Confusing situations
The scenario in the hidden subway with the child ghost was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Every other spider web in the game can be pushed through, yet this scenario requires you to turn on your lighter to burn the web. There are no hints to use fire and people are known to get stuck at this particular scenario.
6. The gas mask.
How does it change the game? The only difference is an annoying "Press T to change the filter" and minor cracks in your mask to simulate damage taken.

Terrible grindy game, terrible toxic fanboy community.  Just see how worked up they get over negative reviews or critical forum posts, hilarious.
Still, the game showed some serious promise but the impressive ship customization is all behind a heavy wall of grinding the games upgrade currency making build experimentation far too time consuming.
The majority of the game modes are just playing keep away from the enemy, or chasing them down depending if you're on attack or defense.  Then there are also some factions who's primary form of combat revolve around this battle strategy so even around half of the normal "kill everything" battles end up being played this way as well.
The AI blindly follows mission objectives with its full combat force both to its benefit and peril as this is very easy to exploit.
The ship-to-ship combat itself reminds me more of the horrible naval combat in Rome 2.  Lots of ship ramming, keeping at long range for artillery style salvos while some smaller swarm ships distract and peck away at the enemy.  The boarding combat was also fairly disappointing as it is over the second you fire off the boarding action.  No prolonged fighting that causes damage over time or disruptions in enemy ship functions, just an instant flat level of damage based on your ships troop strength.  Like many modern RTS games the combat revolves around special RPG style ability use instead of more traditional tactical game play.
The campaign mode is bleak and while fitting to the setting it doesn't provide much reward for progress.  You start out with no real bonuses for controlling the campaign map but for every system you lose you gain an increasing number of negative modifiers.  Eventually there are special assets you secure from the enemy but doing so only helps mitigate other negative modifiers if you secure them.  If you don't?  You guessed it, more negative modifiers for you.  Sure it fits the setting, it just doesn't inspire much drive to succeed and not simply retreat to save your best upgraded ships from a battle that seems to be circling the drain.
I won't even get into the train wreck that is multi-player.

As a long time fan of the RTS genre, a platinum level random player on Starcraft 2, and a little experience on the first Compnay of heroes, I feel I am qualified to make a review for people who haven't played Company of heroes 1. COH2 has taken the starcraft formula and taken out the Korean/Robot mechanic requirements of upper level play, and replaced it with tactical thinking and an emphasis on micro.
This is what makes the game truly shine, the perfect flank on an entrenched position that won you the game. Not a flank in a typical RTS, where your just trying to maximize the DPS of your blobbed army. Alot of the units you use in the game are less effective when attacked in the rear or sides. The arc of fire on machine gun positions and artillery pieces mean that you have an actual advantage when flanking. I cannot describe the satisfaction of pulling off a successful flank and crushing an opponents otherwise superior force. Not a starcraft number game, but tactical thinking.
The explosions, those are what's gonna keep you hooked and coming back for more.
The sheer glee you experience when a satchel charge blows up a half-track or perfectly timed artillery strikes that wipe out an opponents entire infantry force. That is what the game is all about. The  combat is gritty and while it has an arcade feel, COH 2 tries to depcit war in semi-realistic fashion. I'm a rather quiet person, but the target firing howitzer still makes me howl with laughter when I one shot a king tiger. To make ME shout for joy, is quite the achievment.
There is always a "but" at the end of most positive stuff about this game. Despite the updates I still feel like one should be included. The game has been out for over a year and still has game breaking bugs. They are few in number and rare now with numerous patches, but still lurk around. Balance in the game is often brought in the game websites forums and reddit. I however feel that for 1v1s and 2v2s it is fairly balanced. I am basing this on my experience with starcraft 2. It's true germans have better late game especially in 4v4's but that's what makes the factions varied. It's no secret Sc2 that protoss has the best late game. No one really complains about it in the community, because its the way they were designed. I feel this holds true here, do you wanna play the more micro intensive scrappy factions like the a allies (terran)? Then go right ahead, It is the options that you have that are in spades here, especially with 4 completly unique factions.
All in all it's worth every penny to me, because no matter what bugs there are, what imbalances may or may not be there, It's always a blast to play Company of heroes 2.

Let's talk about "Enemy Within", shall we?
With the Enemy Within supplement/DLC, the flaws of the XCOM game are addressed, and it finally becomes what it deserved to be: a really great, turn-based strategy game.
In its original form, there weren't enough maps, and the missions felt samey: a repetitive grind to build a party that could take out the alien invaders main ships. The improved game introduces Exalt, a group of UFO cultists who are working to undermine the XCOM project and bring the aliens to Earth. The cultists are not very powerful, but they provide some much-needed variety. With the DLC in place, XCOM is complete, and it's worth playing. Buy the whole bundle in a sale.
Replay value is limited, as the story will always evolve the same way, but it's a good story, and some of the additions (like where your base gets attacked) elevate it from 'nice idea' to really nice game. It's surprising that 'Enemy Unknown' came out wih so little variety (shot down UFOs always find a wooded area to crash in?) but that problem is a thing of the past. Get 'Enemy Within' and you'll be a very happy Earthling.
