After playing this game for some time, I just can't bring myself to enjoy this game - and I'm sure the fanboys and "MLG" RTS fanatics will downvote this review to hell, but as a somewhat decent RTS player and a 40k nerd - I just don't enjoy this game. And I personally don't like it for reasons I will state below;
To say it's not fun would be a bloody lie - the setting, scale, and gameplay can be pretty fun and quite addicting. I always have wanted to command my own fleet of Imperial ships and bring Heretics, Aliens and Mutants to their doom, and this game definitely cuts it for me. The game itself is running on max settings on a pretty potato computer. But at the same time, several issues bring it down for me.
First things first - this is something that in particular applies to myself, I enjoy the DoW/CoH style games; Not to say that I think everything should be given to you from the start, but given that the game is so incredibly grindy - it reminds me of War Thunder, rather than Sins of a Solar Empire, and it feels like a chore to unlock all the ships, thus combat starts to feel repetitive after awhile. Not only did every single ship feel exactly the same to me, but larger in size and with a different appearance; Mission after mission, I never felt as though I actually needed to accomplish any objectives, I just ended up destroying the enemy fleet and triggering victory; Except in the case of Planetary Assault. My nemesis of the entire game was the damn Convoy missions - Which are extremely annoying to play, because you have to manage your entire fleet, as well as 3-6 Transport ships on top of that; You cannot manage everything, of course - but given that you have so much to manage, you'll find you get overwhelmed and your Transports will be destroyed because you can't keep track of them all. If you lose HALF of the transports, reguardless of whether or not your other transports are 1000m or 5m from the extraction zone, the rest of the Transports will warp out and you will lose. Which makes no sense at all, I would rather have some supplies than none, but oh no! We've lost 3 transports, lets abandon the entire planet and let it rebel even though we have a straight shot to it and can help! This brings me to the fact that the AI itself seems to cheat at its own game - it seemingly pops off abilities one after the other in 10-15 second intervals without any sort of cooldown. Balancing needs to happen as well - I understand that each particular race has a niche to fill - but it's extremely annoying that the Chaos fleet has a lot of long range weapons, but the ships will outrun you as well; And you can't kill what you can't catch very well, now can you? The Eldar fleet is just all around fragile - Their fleets will get annihilated very quickly and the only ship I've ever lost to them happened to be a Sword Class Frigate. The only race that seems to challenge me in some way (legitimately, I might add...) happens to be the Orks, which are very good at beating me at my own game of closing range and boarding like hell, then ramming the ship to bits. I also found some of the favours to be utterly pointless - Space Marine boarding parties and Terminator lightning strikes felt like a slightly buffed Armsman unit, rather than a squad of genetically enhanced, power armoured angels of death. Typically I had a 47% chance to succeed with those abilities, even if I had stripped the enemy vessel of its shields and did moderate/heavy damage to it. The only reason to choose the Inquisition favour is for the Emperor's Tarot, but even that doesn't keep you apprised of the ship you revealed for very long. The Mechanicus favour is mostly just to have a third upgrade slot, and the Imperial Navy favour is useless, as all you can do is call in a Torpedo escort that gets destroyed instantly.
Multiplayer can be fun as well - but extremely annoying at times, especially when you encounter a fleet that is much more advanced than you, forcing you to warp out and search for another game.
Another thing that you will find annoying after awhile of playing is the constant cinematic cameras each time you enter and exit the battlefield. It had me saying irritably, "Yes, I can see my ♥♥♥♥ing ships. Cool. It's not like I constantly see them at the upgrade screen..."
It would be nice if there was an option to turn them off. They get old after awhile.
All in all - this is specifically my opinion on the game, these are things that in particular bring it down for me specifically, but everybody is different and some people may love this game to death, but alas this isn't for me; But if you love 40k, you should try it out and see if you like it. If a review says this is boring, they are lying or are very tasteless indeed.

I was foolish and bought this game without doing proper research at the urging of friends.
I call this genre "Survival/Crafting", and I hate it. I had hope for Dark and Light because I heard it was a departure from the genre with a greater focus on RPG mechanics and exploration. I was deceived. Dark and Light uses Ark's engine, which is particularly obvious because the developers barely changed the UI. It still looks like it belongs in a sci-fi game.
When I first launched the game, I created a character and then spent an hour (not an exaggeration) in a loading screen, before the game caused a memory leak and almost blew up my computer (a bit of an exaggeration). When I did finally get into the game, I was immediately killed by an arbitrarily strong monster called a Dark Wraith at the edge of town. As in, right next to the gate guards, who didn't engage it until after it killed me. I respawned, and I spent an hour trying to collect one resource that had an abysmal drop rate, but which I needed to advance my skills. At that point, I gave up, and I've since applied for a refund.
PROS:
--Barring a few minor graphical issues, the game looked really cool. The destroyed moon in the sky drives home that this world is dying. Character customization is limited in terms of race, but you can change your appearance with a bunch of sliders. Some of the options make you look crazy. Again, Ark's engine. If you've seen the crazy characters people make in that game, expect the same thing here.
--The music was appropriately epic.
--Monsters have decent AI. In the distance, I saw a dragon swoop down and snatch another creature before flying away with its prey clutched tightly.
--Monster design is cool. By far the most interesting thing I saw was an earth elemental who actually tried to roll on top of me to deal damage. That is the kind of attack I would expect a thirty foot tall rock monster to make.
MEH:
--Combat is action combat. It needs work. It takes forever to unlock weapons (and anything else), and using the sword I could fight enemies much stronger than me by literally running in a circle around them and moving away when they took a swing at me. Most only had one attack and didn't use it more than once every two seconds. Spells are items called Runes that you need to craft and equip. They have charges, and you can only use one at a time.
--Since the localization isn't complete, buying and selling things is a pain. I couldn't tell which I was doing because of the weird phrasing and the mess of a UI. Some items also have different names in the menus than they do in the actual game. For example, one of the tutorial missions asks you to collect Rattan but actually wants you to collect Twine.
CONS:
--The UI was ported directly from Ark without much work, if any. All the options are the same, it looks like it belongs in a sci-fi game instead the fantasy game it's in, and some of the tooltips are the same. You can create a "House", which is just a Tribe, and some of the menu options will still refer to it as a Tribe. There are also options that don't even exist in Dark and Light but do in Ark. I didn't dare tweak them out of fear of what havoc they'd cause with the engine.
--The skill system. They were obviously trying to reward certain types of gameplay with crafting recipes, but everything takes forever to unlock and most of it is locked until you get to a certain level regardless of what else you do. Sometimes you will be asked to collect a certain resource to unlock a skill, but collecting it doesn't increase your progress toward unlocking the skill.
--The magic system. Mana is pretty standard, but your Mana REGEN is tied to a completely separate resource called Focus. All Spells cost Mana. Your Mana regenerates by automatically spending your Focus. Focus can only be restored with items, and if you run out of Focus you die. Focus makes no sense and is completely superfluous. Spells also don't say what they cost, because the game assumes if you've unlocked them you have met the requirements to cast them. I used console commands to unlock a shapeshifting spell to see how it worked, but even after making myself Level 50 and putting all my points into Mana, I couldn't use it. Best case scenario, that one spell is designed to be stupidly expensive.
--The world map is tiny. It's advertised as being huge, but I used console commands to fly and looked at the entire thing from above. Traveling on foot would take a while, but only because of natural obstacles and monsters with nonsensical levels (sheep can be Level 150, skeleton warriors twice as tall as you can be Level 20 and kill you more easily than a larger Level 50 monster) between you and your destination. Standing on a mountain a short distance away from the Human capital, I could see the Dwarven capital. What the f*** am I supposed to "explore"?
--Customization through equipment sucks. In a way that's typical for the genre, there are only a few armor sets and weapon tiers, they look mostly the same, and there's no way to change their colors or anything like that. Expect everyone to run around wearing the same clothes.
--Once you've unlocked all the crafting and skills, the game kind of just... stops. There's no endgame aside from hunting monsters you know you can kill or open world PvP. And, while open world PvP is fun, Dark and Light doesn't provide enough variety between characters to make it interesting.
VERDICT:
--Another Survival/Crafting game that claims to be an MMO but isn't, and claims to innovate but doesn't.

After playing the PC port for quite some time I will try my best to give the most unbiased review possible.
Despite the controversy over the DOA5LR Port, Team NINJA/Tecmo KOEI have finally dropped the long awaited fighter of their niche title. Quite a number of fighter players and DOA veterans such as myself have been anticipating the this game to come out for PC for quite some time, so does it live up to the "hype"?
First of all, let's start with the most important part of a fighting game, the gameplay. Does this game prove hard to play? ( massive FPS drops, game breaking glitches, etc ) I have a rather high end rig and seem to be having no issues, my specs include an Intel Core i7 4790K, GTX 970, 16 GB RAM, Game running on an SSD and I have had no problems with any of the stages regarding frame drops or strange floor glitches ( I believe it has been patched out, when the game launched I experienced some strange FPS drops on the Lorelei stage but since the patch it doesnt seem to exist ). The game even with a rig like mine seems to have some strange FPS drops sometimes in the Character Select screen, maybe because it is awkwardly locked at 30 FPS when the PS4/X1 version runs at 60 FPS, but yes in regards to gameplay the game is pretty solid given that your rig is somewhat beefy. ( Game is still pretty badly optimized in the long run unfortunately )
Now let's talk about the graphics and how the game looks overall versus the PS4/X1 editions, if you have a pretty beefy rig like mine then you can get this game looking quite a bit more amazing than the current gen consoles ( a little disappointing since it should either surpass or be equal to the console versions ) if you "upscale" the game to 4K, I use Nvidia's DSR to supersample it down to 1440P and the game has almost no jaggies for the most part. Antialiasing on the PC version is obviously far more superior than the PS4/X1 ports when you take a close look at the character models but again in regards to the characters it is pretty disappointing how my PS4 version just with the way the "Soft Engine" works and affects the way skin shines and appears, it is a very nice touch that I am very disappointed that whoever in charge of this port ( not sure if this was Team NINJA's choice or their boss Tecmo KOEI's choice, but either way they should be ashamed of this decision ) decided to leave this out.
The PC version is also left inferior with the fact that the only time the game runs at 60 FPS is during actual fighting, but everything else is locked to 30 FPS, making everything else not look as smooth which is a HUGEEE disappointment as well when most of our rigs are more than capable enough at getting the 60 FPS the consoles also get.
The lack of being able to purchase DLC the same way as the console counterparts is also very stupid, not everybody wants to purchase a whole entire $50+ pack of DLC, most people would rather just get a few costumes or themes that they prefer or for characters they like, I have no problem with DLC as the content is all optional and it helps the developers get more funds and hopefully encourage further and much more improved games but at least be smart about the way you advertise your DLC.
On the plus sides, as a huge DOA fan this title is still worth it in my opinion just because this is the first official time Dead Or Alive finally comes to PC and the mods that have come out this almost whole month have been quite good and they will only get far better over time as resources become far more available and people start to become more eduated about them.
THE FINAL VERDICT : Do I reommend this game? That depends, for huge DOA fans and those interested in mods I highly recommend this game. People looking at this game who are probably not too educated about Dead Or Alive or are in general just people that somehow know about this game maybe from a friend or an internet article and got curious, I do not recommend this game for you, however since Dead Or Alive is such a niche title I am going to put "I recommend this game", just heed my warning for those of you who do not know about this game, if you are not interested in mods or just want to try the game out get it for Xbox One or PS4, you will have a better experience there.
It sucks because I really want this game to succeed and I would like to see more come to PC especially but I believe bad business practices must have some sort of consequence.

TL;DR GAME GOOD, ME LIKE, BUY!!
GENERAL
i 100% recommend this game to anyone interested in survival games or even turn based strategy games.
seeing as theres a demo i wont talk about the mechanics or how to physically play the game and maneuver the interfaces, you could get all that pretty easily just trying it for yourself but i will say dont let how simple it appears fool you, there is an amazing amount of depth to this game once you get into it.
now i have heard complaints about the RNG, and i'll admit it can be harsh but honestly i've never personally felt it was unfair since you can heavily reduce the chances of a lot of things. sure i might die in one shot before i ever see my enemy (pretty rare) but how many times have i done that same thing to my own enemies? everything RNG throws at you it throws just as hard at the npcs, which to me makes the combat system one of the best i've ever played but more about that down below.
REALISM
Some of my favourite moments in all my years of gaming have come from this game, and for one simple reason.
This game is hard, and i dont mean hard like most games i mean its hard in a very realistic fashion.
i've died from simple food poisoning because i ate raw meat and couldnt keep hydrated,
from cholera because i didnt boil my water,
hypothermia because i braved the elements in nothing but a hospital gown,
blood loss because i didnt wrap my cuts,
infection because i didnt clean my wraps
Heart attack because i overworked myself
and starvation/dehydration because i knew better than to eat the raw meat or unboiled water
and dont even get me started on combat related deaths
but you'll notice with every new death i learned something, i learned the why of what was killing me and slowly figured out how to craft everything i needed to fix those situations,
spears for hunting,
fire to cook and boil food and water
makeshift clothing from rags and hides to keep from freezing
little by little, with every death and every new run, you learn better builds for your skills,
how to build a better campsite,
what fights to get into and when to run away
and eventually before you even realize it youve gone from scavegning to scrape by to scavenging for comfort.
COMBAT
with a combat system that exemplifies the desperate nature of every conflict and the risk that comes with that, you'll find yourself envisioning some of the most impressive fight sequences.
imagine being awoken to a stranger in your camp wielding a cleaver. you have nothing but a stone to defend yourself with and hes charging you stopping only to demand your surrender before running again to close the gap, you steel yourself as he gets closer and at the last moment you jump and tackle him to the ground, scrambling to get up before he does you seize the moment to kick at his head while hes down but he rolls away at the last moment, you lash out a flurry of blows with your rock hoping to end it before he can get up, but he manages to get to his feet with only minor injuries and slices your gut whle you try to catch your breath.
squared off and on even terms now you ready a defensive stance hoping to avoid the razor edge of his cleaver, dodging one swing you see your moment and headutt him stunning him for just a moment, but it was enough you bear everything you have crashing the hard stone into his chest over and over before he can get his bearings.
as he starts to cough blood hope starts to cling to you, you demand he surrender his gear and you'll let him live. he responds by savaging your arm crippling it and causing you to drop your stone. Pain obscuring your focus exhaustion setting in from blood loss and exersion you take a step back your only thoughts on the blade set to take your life you prepare to dodge knowing another hit like that and your done for.
your enemy seeking to close the gap dives towards you eyes widening as you sidestep and he falls vulnerable to the ground, you kick him, and you kick him, over and over, his ribs cracking underneath you. you grab your stone with your good hand and finish him taking your new cleaver and whatever else he had as your prize.

This is a game i can honestly say is good for any audience.
I originally had been wanting to get Shelter 2 when i happened across the ad for the upcoming "Meadow".
Being new to any M&D games i didn't know if i would get this, yet a few days after release i decided to try it, needless to say i really like what i found.
This game is probably one of the most relaxing MMOs i've ever seen.
The game again uses the famous art style of M&D and brings 9 of the animals from the previous titles in as playable characters.
Plus since the game is new the devs are adding lots of things for gameplay, so there may be all new modes and animals in the near-future.
MECHANICS:
The game could be classified as a walking simulator or sandbox, with exploring being a very large part of the gameplay.
Different animals have different speeds and sizes, and along with collectables scattered randomly across the terrain there are different stone pillars that can be shattered with different animal cries.
These pillars will yeld the rarer blue and gold shards, which unlock new animals or skins for the animal in use.
CHARACTERS:
Right now the game has 9 characters, each with their own unique abilities.
However some animals require previous Shelter content to unlock.
Baby Badger - Smaller, (Starting animal without other titles)
Badger - Small, (Must have Shelter)
Frog - Smaller, (Unlocks with gold shards first)
Rabbit - Smaller, (Unlocks with gold shards second)
Goat/Deer - Larger, (Unlocks  with gold shards third)
Lynx - Large, (Must have Shelter 2)
Baby Lynx - Smaller, (Must have Paws)
Baby Bear - Small, (Must have Shelter, Shelter 2, Paws)
Eagle - Large, (Must have Shelter, Shelter 2, Paws, all soundtracks, both books)
EDIT: As of the Nov, 30 update there are 10 animals.
Fox - Medium, (Unlocks with gold shards fourth)
CHAT:
The chat system for this game is the most unique feature for an MMO, in that it doesn't have an actual "chat" but rather uses different emotes to communicate.
This means any language spoken doesn't matter, as the emotes are easy to understand and use regardless.
5 emotes at a time can be assigned to your hotkeys too, so you dont need the full panel open all the time if you don't want them on your screen.
Each animal has 10 unique emotes, (excluding the eagle) ranging from greetings, happy and sad to angry or silly.
You also have several other emotes, used to communicate instructions or questions to others.
These emotes are grey and include things like a check mark and x for saying yes or no, saying you see a collectable, a cave, etc.
PERFORMANCE:
The game right now has varying performances.
I use a computer that is a little above required hardware, but the game usually runs without difficulty.
The only exeption is on highly populated servers where the lag can get bad.
Changing the graphics settings doesn't really help, but playing on a server with fewer people fixes the issue.
Also do remember the game isn't very old and fixes happen regularly so chances are this won't be an issue much longer.
In conclusion i can fully recomend this game, it has lots of content for any player who likes exploration and for this price it is totally worth a try.
As the game is now i would give it a 9.9/10 for the good experiences i've had with it and with how well its helped me relax after long days.

The game is text based adventure where you choose your own path that determines the kind of ending you'll get. The main antagonist in this game is called F.E.A.R. (the Federation of European American Rebels) led by Vladimir Utoshiki a.k.a. "Titanium Cyborg".  The other leaders of the evil organization, who are set on conquering the world, are having a meeting and it is up to you to stop them.  You have three (3) short days to search for clues to discover the exact place and time it's gonna happen.
You start by choosing the powers of your character.  However, you are limited to four (4) powers which has an effect on the outcome of the game and also the choices made available to you.  You can also pick the costume and looks of your superhero but they are rather limited.  Moreover, you can also pick the name of your character from a selection of "WTF kinda name is that" (e.g.The Incomparable Romance or Indifferent Thoughtstealer).  Perhaps, this is held back by copyright laws.
The graphics and art style are rather nice for a text and still picture game. The visuals are great which is a mix of digital comic books and small moving videos.  I loved the soundtrack and music at the beginning but it got rather annoying the longer I played the game.  I turned the music off when I started seeking 100% achievements.
The gameplay is fun coz there are lots of humurous scenarios, places to discover, several villains and criminals to fight and  tons of clues to choose from.  Some outcomes are hilarious and will appear depending on the path you choose.
If you love comic books the game is an excellent pick.  The game has a good replay value with unlockable cards.  Some paths may repeat themsleves and sometimes might go on in a loop, if you don't know what you are doing.  If you dislike reading stuff then avoid this game but if you are into this stuff that I described, then I highly recommend this game to you again.

Deathstate is very interesting sort of game, if you're a fan of roguelight games like binding of isaac you'll likely enjoy this game.  I'll be updating this review as I accumulate times but here are some first thoughts
Pro's/Con's
+Smooth gameplay (I have a fairly decent machine but i have had 0 frame drops while playing it, streaming and watching another stream at the same time)
+dynamic runs (think binding of isaac where every run feels slightly different)
+Diverse Characters (all but 2 of the characters feel very different and have different builds that lend to the characters starting stats and default ability)
+Controller support (they improved the controller functionality a fair amount in the most recent patch)
+Difficult Gameplay (game scales well and has difficult conent, desecration 3 is stupidly hard and it took me about 25 hours of actual gameplay to get my first clear with a stupidly lucky run)
-Dashing seems a bit strange and disadvantagous for controller (would be nice if there was a dash button that would just dash the direction you're facing)
-Limited end act  bosses (NEW BOSSES HAVE BEEN ADDED!)
-Mana/manaregen stat's seem incredibly underwhelming for how many items have them (max mana occasionally is important on expensive mana items due to -mana items leaving you with not enough to cast the spells)
-Level balance seems slightly off (world 3 is a good bit easier than world 4 and I personally think world 2 is more difficult than 4 as well but that's probably just personal bias)
In my opinion this game is definitly worth buying and if the developers keep up with it I could see easily sinking 100+ hours into it.

The word "remaster" seems to be a bit of a phase at the moment with the release of the Potato Station 4 and XParsnip One. One after another, games are premastered with little change. However, the developers at Deep Silver have done an incredible job at reimagining an already critically acclaimed game from THQ. It's a challenge when the aim of the remaster was originally to bring the console boys to the graphical realm of PC. Yet, porting Metro: 2033 to the Last Light engine works wonders for the mechanics, performance and visuals. It even goes as far as to have a little more on the side:
-Stunning visuals; the 4A Engine is a master piece. Metro 2033: Redux (and last light) are quite possibly the most impressive looking games on PC with high end antialiasing, super sharp textures, beautiful lighting and super soft shadows.
-Marked improvement on performance; the original 2033 was seen as benchmark for super PC's because of its draining performance. 2033 Redux has incredible performance, even better than the original last light.
-Interesting world; the worlds design is fascinating. Despite the literality of the levels the atmosphere is terrifyingly claustrophobic in the tunnels and curiously beautiful outside.
-Exceedingly detailed; there are notes, letters, passages of dialogue from guards and much more that add to the world. Even more has been added for this remaster! Dare I say I prefer this nuclear apocalypse to Fallout?
-Great mechanics; the stealth system from Last Light is a marked improvement. Weapons feel punchy and the micro management of things like gas masks and ammo adds to the emersion.
-Faithfull story; its stays mostly faithful to the original 2033 book. And the story is great! Fairly straight forward but pretty engaging. Characters are memorable and most importantly a hidden carma system adds 2 endings for you to discover.
-Rewarding Difficulty; the Ranger Mode makes a return. This time you can make it Ranger Hardcore! This kind of makes it the Dark Souls of FPS yet much like Dark Souls the payoff for beating the game is second to none and rarely adds to the horror survival element as you scavenge for ammo and mask filters. (Ranger Hardcore= Stealth Mode)
-Good pacing; the mix between horror, action and stealth makes for a fluid and engaging gameplay.
-Great port, most of the things you want are here.
-Not the smartest AI; the AI isn't bad... But it isn't great. They seem to run at you but the way they stalk you out is quite nice.
-No discount for existing owners :/ I would have been nice to see this. It was a pre-order incentive but for existing fans I can’t help but feel some discount is in order.
-Slightly Linear; Might be being nit-picky but the levels are slightly linear. Whilst there are areas to explore it does push you in one direction (Last Light is a marked improvement on this if you getting the collection though).
-Questionable accents; I suggest playing this game in Russian with English subtitles. The English speaking Russian accents are quite bad. Playing the game in Russian and ranger hard-core makes the game amazingly immersive!
-No real soundtrack; despite good sound design on the whole there is no soundtrack that detracts from the atmosphere (slightly).
-Lack of PC scalability; this is the same problem that plagued last light. There is no system scalability and few graphical options making it hard to customise and tweak to the best performance on lower end systems.
If you’re a new comer buy this Redux version, not the normal one. It's a marked improvement visually, mechanically and performance wise. The new details and these additions also makes it justifiable for existing fans who have played the game as well. It was one of the best FPS games of the past decade made only better by this remaster making it an incredible FPS survival horror game. It will scare you, it will punish, and it will leave you wanting more. Luckily there’s a sequel! Metro 2033: Redux is the panicle of the Metro franchise and a beautiful remaster.

One of the most atmospheric and genuinely terrifying games I have ever played. If you are looking for a short yet gripping FPS to lose yourself in, this is it.
I played on Ranger mode, which is one step down from the hardest in the game. No artificial difficulty here, I would say it is similar to Dark Soul's difficulty (though nowhere near as hard), in that you have to plan out your strategy and often find yourself redoing one section of the game multiple times. There are also multiple layers to the difficulty - not only are the enemies varied with different strategies but you also have to worry about things like air filters when you go above ground and conserving ammo (I had literally no ammo except for grenades for the last 5 or so minutes of the game).
I don't tend to enjoy linear titles as much as open ended, but Metro's linear storyline was so rich with character and emotion and really sweeps you from one section to the next, feeling organic and natural from one possibly fatal encounter to the next.
Highly recommended.

For context, I am a 3d hobbysist and have used Blender for about a year (not the 1.5 hours steam thinks I have used it!) to make sci-fi type images.  Blender is a very capable 3d, image and animation application. It is powerful, the cycles render engine can generate some great results and the modeler is capable too with some great free/cheap 3rd paty addons like HardOps. I am not an animator so cannot comment on that aspect (see other reviews) but after coming from commercial 3d software for over 10 years (Modo in my case) there is for me no reason to keep paying for commercial applications and continuos upgrades of features I don't need etc. Blender is free and has a very large amount of online support materials on YouTube and elsewhere. It has a large and enthusiastic community.  Initially it is a little different to other 3d apps that I have used but make the effort and do a few beginner tutorials and you will soon find your way around. I find Blender to be faster in terms of creation than most other 3d apps. Make no mistake, Blender is high quality, feature packed and can do pretty much anything. It also has GPU rendering so if you have a decent graphics card you may find this renders faster than your CPU! If you are a enthusiast or a hobbyist Blender is a no brainer. If you are a professional you are going to know what you need from your 3d software. - and Blender might well do what you need. I have been using Blender for a year now - and have been impressed by its stability (crashes about once every 2 weeks with daily use). Sounds a lot? Not compared to my previous experiences with other software - Blender in my opinion is as rock solid as you get for this type of application. Anyway, did I mention it's free? So you can try it out - do a few tutorials and you can see for yourself. Serious power for nil outlay.

GENERAL
i 100% recommend this game to anyone interested in survival games or even turn based strategy games.
seeing as theres a demo i wont talk about the mechanics or how to physically play the game and maneuver the interfaces, you could get all that pretty easily just trying it for yourself but i will say dont let how simple it appears fool you, there is an amazing amount of depth to this game once you get into it.
now i have heard complaints about the RNG, and i'll admit it can be harsh but honestly i've never personally felt it was unfair since you can heavily reduce the chances of a lot of things. sure i might die in one shot before i ever see my enemy (pretty rare) but how many times have i done that same thing to my own enemies? everything RNG throws at you it throws just as hard at the npcs, which to me makes the combat system one of the best i've ever played but more about that down below.
REALISM
Some of my favourite moments in all my years of gaming have come from this game, and for one simple reason.
This game is hard, and i dont mean hard like most games i mean its hard in a very realistic fashion.
i've died from simple food poisoning because i ate raw meat and couldnt keep hydrated,
from cholera because i didnt boil my water,
hypothermia because i braved the elements in nothing but a hospital gown,
blood loss because i didnt wrap my cuts,
infection because i didnt clean my wraps
Heart attack because i overworked myself
and starvation/dehydration because i knew better than to eat the raw meat or unboiled water
and dont even get me started on combat related deaths
but you'll notice with every new death i learned something, i learned the why of what was killing me and slowly figured out how to craft everything i needed to fix those situations,
spears for hunting,
fire to cook and boil food and water
makeshift clothing from rags and hides to keep from freezing
little by little, with every death and every new run, you learn better builds for your skills,
how to build a better campsite,
what fights to get into and when to run away
and eventually before you even realize it youve gone from scavegning to scrape by to scavenging for comfort.
COMBAT
with a combat system that exemplifies the desperate nature of every conflict and the risk that comes with that, you'll find yourself envisioning some of the most impressive fight sequences.
imagine being awoken to a stranger in your camp wielding a cleaver. you have nothing but a stone to defend yourself with and hes charging you stopping only to demand your surrender before running again to close the gap, you steel yourself as he gets closer and at the last moment you jump and tackle him to the ground, scrambling to get up before he does you seize the moment to kick at his head while hes down but he rolls away at the last moment, you lash out a flurry of blows with your rock hoping to end it before he can get up, but he manages to get to his feet with only minor injuries and slices your gut whle you try to catch your breath.
squared off and on even terms now you ready a defensive stance hoping to avoid the razor edge of his cleaver, dodging one swing you see your moment and headutt him stunning him for just a moment, but it was enough you bear everything you have crashing the hard stone into his chest over and over before he can get his bearings.
as he starts to cough blood hope starts to cling to you, you demand he surrender his gear and you'll let him live. he responds by savaging your arm crippling it and causing you to drop your stone. Pain obscuring your focus exhaustion setting in from blood loss and exersion you take a step back your only thoughts on the blade set to take your life you prepare to dodge knowing another hit like that and your done for.
your enemy seeking to close the gap dives towards you eyes widening as you sidestep and he falls vulnerable to the ground, you kick him, and you kick him, over and over, his ribs cracking underneath you. you grab your stone with your good hand and finish him taking your new cleaver and whatever else he had as your prize.

WHY ARE YOU STILL HERE?
if your still reading this then you have more then enough time to download the demo either here or on the mobile app and see what im talking about.

Didn't like the first game too much, gave it about a 3/5. Played the beta for CoH 2, wasn't too impressed. Game felt as lame and unbalanced as ever.  Played the game over a free weekend a few months ago, and I WAS HOOKED!
As of 11/27/14, this game is pretty well-balanced.  If you do not start the match by buying a certain number of units and upgrades in a particular order, you are ♥♥♥♥ed. This makes the for 5 minutes of every match turn out about the same way every time. I do not like this.  I also do not like the historical innacuracies, but whatever.
Pros:
-Fairly balanced amongst all 4 factions, game consistently walks a tightrope
-The game is a BLAST during large engagements, it's fun seeing everything blow up
-The time-to-death for all units is at least 2x as fast a CoH 1's, which makes battles less confusing/more fun to watch and play/the game much faster-paced
-The Macro and Micro are both smooth and minimal
Cons:
-I consistently have my game freeze for 10 seconds every so often, which can wreck engagements and my overall strategy.  Other than this problem, the game and its' graphics run well and feel well-optimized
-The historical inacurracies are appaling.  In CoH2, T/34/76s can beat Panthers regularly.  Scout Cars take a lot of damage from .30 caliber machine guns. Mortars are probably too accurate.
-I do not agree with the way that the devs decided to balance the factions out.  Germans are less about tanks/powerful single units and more about mapwide defensive coverage/zerg.  Russians play out in the way that you would expect them to play, but certain units like the KV-8(KV-1 with flamethrower) are practically useless while being extremely expensive.
Basically, you can only play each faction a handful of different ways.  It's kind of like checkers, less like chess.  Still fun, however!
I would give this game a 4/5.  The AAA graphics and units are great, but the game lacks depth and historical accuracy. If you are looking for these things, I would suggest Men of War: Assault Squad (the first one, 2nd one is terrible).  If you are fine with a less-hardcore RTS's, this game will a blast!

I'm a bit disappointed with this game because my issue, as many have already pointed out in longer and more detailed reviews, is entirely with the first-impression a game like this gives. I had actually followed this game for a while and finally got to play it today. I played for about an hour straight and my whole experience was the following : Make character, explore surrounding hexes of beginning campsite area, fail to find any items for 90% of scavenging explored hexes, attract unwanted attention indefinitely, proceed to either get mauled by feral dogs or have to surrender to some random jackass that, from what I understand, removes *at least* one item(including containers which actually takes the container plus all items inside it counting it as a single item) from your inventory(which, to add insult to injury, meant I lost my starting gown and was literally naked - no items at all). Rinse and repeat. No fun at all.
In fact, it's all because of RNG and the issue is the chance of success when performing actions. You start the game with essentially nothing. Following the first-time tutorial messages, you'll always scavenge the starting area to get a gown and, seemingly useless, shards of glass. Virtually every single start had me next to a small town with storage sheds and abandoned houses/mobile homes but the loot chance bar is at ~5% without any items to help you scavenge. The stealth bar was usually at around ~50% or ~75% without the hiding skill but was still constantly alerting enemies to my location(which then proceeded with me dying). Using the hiding skill reduces loot chance but increases stealth chance(even though I did alert enemies to position using the skill with it increasing it to ~90%). See the issue? Either stick with a very very low chance to get indefinitely useless loot in a spot I kept on spawning next to and alert enemies OR lower that alert chance but get no loot at all. I had *one* single "lucky" run in the 1 hour I played and it involved me getting a crowbar, which increases loot chance but lowers stealth. Well, guess, what, completely useless for me in that run because the areas I scavenged with the crowbar consistently resulted in injuries, no loot, and alerting various enemies, which is what ended that run because I quickly got beaten down by 3 dogs. This experience was the whole the 1-hour in, what, 10 runs?
It's not even like I'm bad at these types of games. I could do literally nothing about the starting of each run since gathering loot is initially very low, entirely run by RNG, and you start with nothing while also having odds of getting loot against you tenfold. I didn't even understand most of the menus because without certain starting-perks, certain stats are hidden against you(which I assume this includes combat too because I didn't see any combat stats like hit chance or item stats such as weapon damage, range, etc.).
To cut a long story short, it was a disappointing experience because it's yet another game(a rogue-like, too) that depends almost entirely on RNG while giving you no long-term benefits beyond death, meaning you're almost entirely playing against luck itself(and everyone already knows RNG/random number generator mechanics are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. See : Darkest Dungeon) sort of like a gambling game where it's a win-lose 50-50 respectively. You go as far as you want risking it every single instance(e.g. every draw of a card or every individual action in this game), except in this game you get literally nothing if you die.
I would've like it more if it didn't come off as so threatening and hardcore because, yes, a lot of roguelikes suffer from this issue. I still haven't gotten much out of FTL for exact reason, because the game starts off as very overwhelming and hardcore, and I got scared off by it. Same thing happened here.
Also, as a random aside since it doesn't fit into any of my ranting... Aside from the first couple tutorial messages, the game explained *nothing*. Even crafting was just weird, especially since the game presumably has crafting recipes that you have to find via scavenging. Oh boy... fun.
If anyone disagrees then I *dare* you to try and create a starting-the-game guide that doesn't essentially tell someone how to play the game, because if you can't then my thoughts will be pointed towards how linear the game would be in the end in terms of progression.

I'd recommend this game with a caveat: it's still in a rough state.
Quake Live is based entirely on Quake 3, which was released in 1999 and I consider a classic FPS experience. Ultimately, the gameplay is fantastic and preserved. The problems come with the extra features which were lost in the transition from being a standalone service to being rolled up into Steam.
Gone is the ability to modify your name (straightforwardly, at least). Gone are the prior stats tracking and (seemingly, at least) compatibility with the old Quake 3 maps. Gone are the old friends lists. Etc. I can't remember all the things that are different about this Steam versions, though to my mind they are all small things.
Ultimately, it's still the same game that came out sixteen years ago with the core improvements from Quake Live a mere five years ago. Fantastic game that I can't recommend enough, even with the shortcomings!

SOLUTION 1: To fix this game crash (this one I had to hunt for info) :
1 - Right click the "Speakers" icon on the bottom right of your desktop.
2 - Click "Recording Devices".
3 - In the "Recording" tab, Right click and select "Show Disabled Devices", "Stereo Mix" will appear.
4 - Right click "Stereo Mix" and click "Enable"
5 - Click "OK"
PROBLEM 2: After this fix, it allowed me to play the game, but the graphics were completely crazy.
SOLUTION 2: To Fix the graphical errors in Star Wars Battlefront 2 :
1. Go to
2. Click on Direct X 9.0
3. Right Click on 15.10.zip
4. Do a Standard Download
5. Extract Files (atiumd64.dll AND atiumdag.dll) to Same location as BattlefrontII.exe
C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Star Wars Battlefront II\GameData
6. Now the game should start without any graphical bugs or glitches!

People are demonizing Bethesda while the game itself had little reason to exist with its playerbase. The subscription model that's been here before didn't "save" the game apparently, but at the same time, if you've been playing it, you've got no reason to complain. Why's that?
You didn't have to ever paid Bethesda for their shoddy subscription, but to have been here after QL was moved to Steam. And that's been already ages ago, so if you're here to write a one-liner "REVIEW" coming from a "QL pro", get out. It's still a barrier to new players, but the game's turned out to be too unprofitable to exist as a freebie, which is odd in a way, and mentioned again down further. Then, how many have actually still got this game? You might think in thousands, but it's in millions.
This isn't a proper review either however, I'm mostly rating the changes.
With all the removed features from when the game was still web-based, I can't recommend this at all. There's no skill tiers, which means you're joining players of a random skill level. Stats have been reset, though I'm pretty sure it was easy to import it with a bit of extra work that would be paid by newcomers, after the payment change. No server rentals either, you're hosting servers on your own PC now if you want to do it from the game's interface. And the weird thing is, what is actually justifying the payment? Bethesda doesn't even have to run any servers anymore, since there's always going to be some made by users - tho' I don't know if it's possible to get dedicated ones. It's gone the opposite of Team Fortress 2, and it's CUT OUT the features it used to distinguish itself with from other FPSs. Quake 3 and even the open-source derivatives are just better without all the gimmicks, but sticking to the premise of being an arena shooter.

'Battlefleet Gothic: Armada' is a laudable attempt at sincerely recreating the now long and lamentably defunct tabletop wargame, 'Battlefleet Gothic' produced by Games Workshop as part of their old Specialist Games range. A spin-off of their iconic Warhammer 40,000 universe, this new iteration of the game perfectly captures the atmosphere of the 41st Millenium as envisaged in Games Workshop's famously grim, dark future where mankind's vast and crumbling stellar empire is beset within and without by physical and spiritual peril, the likes of which split the very stars themselves asunder.
The three core elements of the game, fleet management, campaign management and actual combat, are all redolent of the original tabletop experience. Fleet management harkens back to the RPG elements of Game Workshop's earlier titles, and whilst some might initially find the micro-management a little overwhelming, it becomes surprisingly intuitive and the various information panels (both static and pop-up) do readily clarify the player's various options, neatly and succinctly. Campaign management ostensibly provides chained systems of planets, which are a familiar staple of Science Fiction RTS games, however the player will more often than not find themself directed by the narrative to particular deployments of note, although it is worth noting, there is some degree of oversight in fully explaining the campaign interface and players should keep an eye on their deployment points, so as not to end turns prematurely and waste opportunities to claim systems not tacitly mentioned by the narrative. Players should also make regular return visits to Port Maw, to upgrade and re-equip the vessels available to them, as they earn reknown (the game's currency equivalent)
Actual combat will not be to every gamer's taste, as the game endeavours to remain faithful to its tabletop roots, thus whilst action notionally occurs in 'real time', heavy use of a 'bullet time' style mechanic is necessary to not only allow players to better manage combat, but to plan ahead and perform more elaborate manouvres, switch between various firing options (such as fore or broadside), utilise special abilities, make best use of certain weapons (such as ensuring torpedoes' trajectories take them to where a target *will* be, rather than where they *are*), and target specific systems on larger vessels moment-by-moment. That being said, this does allow for a decidedly tactical level of gameplay, provides immense satisfaction when strategies are successful, and is conducive to maintaining the atmosphere of the player as an admiral responsible for conducting every key facet the intricate ballet of void warfare between massive, kilometre-long vessels designed to utterly annihilate one another.
The most notable and annoying absence in the game however, is the lack of replay feature for individual battles in the narrative campaign. Whilst veteran players may appreciate this degree realism, and the fact that the campaign appears to adjust accordingly (failures losing you systems or assets), less experienced or more casual players may find this a frustrating oversight, as it appears one lost battle can significantly alter the character and progress of the overall narrative campaign and this can be especially disgruntling in situations where the player may feel their loss was more to do with the nature of the scenario and various unknown variables it was impossible to 'out play', rather than any failing on their part. Many such scenarios would still prove no less challenging if replayed, but the player would at least have the opportunity to try out different fleet compositions and strategies, and not feel cheated of battles that are arguably unwinnable unless one happens to chance upon the winning method straight off the bat. Hopefully, this is an issue which will be addressed in future updates.
That being said, if you are at all familiar with the Warhammer 40,000 universe, were lucky enough to enjoy playing the original tabletop version of this game, or are currently playing one of its many spiritual successors as part of the current renaissance in tabletop gaming (such as Star Wars: Armada, Dystopian Wars, Firestorm: Armada, Halo: Fleet Battles or Dropship Commander), then this is an absolute must as, small niggles aside, you will not be disappointed: Especially with the promise of further development to come, and the possibility of future DLC including other iconic races and forces.

==Update spring 2017==
The game still is in beta. There are no patches, balance is still horrible. Lots of bugs were fixed, but every patch introduced new ones. The initial review I made had hopes that the devs will work hard to make a perfect game, yet once again it appeared to be nothing more but a cashgrab.
==Initial review==
I had a really tough time thinking, should I leave a positive or a negative review. As you see, I chose to make it positive, but it is a really cautious recomendation, and to make it more clear, I will start from a negative part of the game.
Cons:
-First of all, the game is nothing more but a beta. It has bugs, it has lags, servers cant handle their job and go offline, and finally, the game simply crashes. Not to mention such funny stuff as random controls problems, that prevent you from moving or using any skills, which is bad on its own, but is even worse cause of "hangar multiplayer lobbies".
-Apart from bugs I want to mention heavy balance issues. While many old players (or the ones, who are good at such type of games) figured how to win regardless of situation, some newer and less hardcore ones really suffer from said balance. Some missions for some factions may be a real nightmare (convoy defence is the most problematic for new players, who get killed in 2 minutes with no chances of survival), some races can just outdamage you in first seconds of combat (pulsar eldar is a bit too good).
-Somewhat linked to the previous issue, ship variety. The game has "hangar" where you manage your fleet, from which you select ship to fight a battle. So what is the problem here? Well, first, you have a VERY limited number of active vessels per class. Second, some of said "classes" have only one option of vessel to select from (hello orks and eldar), others have a situation where you either select one good option, or pick any other and get  a much worse one (that is for chaos and imperium). Pluss, I must mention that not all options were brought here from tabletop, so it really limits you, if you want to get your fleet from tabletop on a new playground.
Pros:
-Spirit of the game. Yes, it is 100% WH 40k. It is pure "grim dark future". And if you are into it, as I am myself, you will find yourself roleplaying with your enemies, accusing each other in heresy, following the false God-Emperor, being a primitive creature or simply yelling WAAAAAAAAAAAAGH on top of your lungs. After some other games, after dull insults or simple "gl hf" such a great start of each combat gives this game 100 bonus points in my eyes.
-Each faction has its own unique playstyle and personality. Want to implement hit'n'run tactics? Eldar are waiting for you. Want to endure every single battle and defeat your enemies with an ocean of pathos? Imperium of Man stands storng! Want to go rebelious against the system? Chaos is that. Want to laugh maniacally and ram into enemies with guns blazing? DA BOYZ ARE HERE!
-Progression system feels really great. You gather your power, customize each vessel to do the job you want it to do, get levels, skills, gear and crew, recover them from half-dead state. While it has some issues and can kinda limit you, it also allows you not only to win in combat itself, but actually make this win much easier by carefull preparation and planning.
-Single campain seems to be pretty close to the official back, pluss it adds up even more strategical depth in planning your battles.
-It looks and sounds really great.
TL;DR version/summary: the game has its issues and they can be even a bit gamebreaking right now, but even now the feel about the game, fun and euphoria from gameplay are enough for me to recommend it. And if the developer fixes all the problems and gets even more content they already promissed, the game will be my GOTY candidate.

The game itself is promising with already lots of great things going for it. However, there is one underlying issue the developers need to address and make people aware of.
And that is - THIS GAME IS PVP FOCUSED!!
Nowhere in the game description does it mention the fact that your character is still present in the game world after logging off, and susceptible to attacks from NPC monsters as well as other Players who can kill you and take your stuff.
Had I known that, I would have kept on scrolling past this game.
Now I'm not normally the one to give games bad reviews, but I feel like there should be more awareness of this PvP focused "survival". I never played ARK or Rust because of those reasons.
I was in the middle of discussing these things on the server I was playing when out of nowhere someone on a giant bird grabbed my character, flew me really high up and dropped me to my death.
I laughed because I was already one foot out the door on this game, and that pushed me right out.
Devs - You need a big fat sign or warning over your game letting people know of the heavy PVP focus. Nowhere in the description does it mention that, and the reviews (at least the ones I read) didn't mention it either. I thought I was buying a more PVE focused survival game.
Someone on the server told me there are PVE servers, but I went back and looked and didn't see in the server browser where it has that information listed - PvP or PvE - neither are specified. So either that person was blowing smoke or there's some other hidden way to see that information.
Either way, I'm unhappy with my purchase and unfortunately I cannot refund it after playing it for 6 hours. Maybe later on down the road when the games been patched up and updated I might consider revisiting, but right now I can't recommend this game unless PVP is your thing in a survival crafting game.

A fantastic turn-based squad tactics game. Premise of Xcom is simple. You're in charge of a secret organization that's at the frontline of defending our world from an alien invasion. To do so you must train an elite team of able soldiers and give the invaders a fight they'll never forget.
Gameplay consists of a variety of elements. The main aspect are the combat missions where you move each squad member on an isometric grid in a turn-based format. Enemies come in a good variety, each one having their own strengths and weaknesses, and all having a smart A.I. Taking cover and using teamwork are essential to winning the battles. Your soldiers are all expendable and die permanently if killed in combat. Where this is not a big deal when you lose rookies, you really want to take special care for your higher levelled people (gladly they also have a higher chance of simply being K.Oed and able to be revived with a medic).
The combat is pretty challenging a lot of the time and gets you thinking tactically, even on an Easy difficulty. There were a few instances where I felt that the difficulty spiked a bit too sharply. Those were mainly regarding the main story missions. I think you're supposed to really take your time preparing for those, because the game doesn't have levels and the like that tells you how powerful you need to be in order to handle these missions, so it's easy to go in too soon without realising it. Moreover, the game constantly highlights main story objectives as high priority, which is also very misleading, because it makes you think you have to do them as soon as possible.
Aside from main story missions, there are many optional missions. Some require you to simply clear out an area off hostiles, others require you to shoot down a UFO and then send a team to finish off any surviving invaders, and at times you also get missions where you have to rescue as many civilians in an area as you can whilst aliens are trashing up the place.
Aside from combat missions, you also have to do some management behind the scenes. That mostly involves deciding what tech to research, how to outequip your team, as well as launching satellites over specific countries, each one giving you their own bonuses, and overall monitoring the level of panic on each continent and making sure it doesn't go into the red zone. In essence, there's a lot of choice on how to advance through the game.
I was quite surprised by the high level of presentation in regard to story cutscenes, voice acting, and things of that nature, considering that most tactics-based games usually have a very minimalistic approach regarding these aspects of a game. The music is also pretty amazing (particularly the squad selection track, which is my favourite).
Xcom is very good at sucking you in and making you really feel like a commander who has to make difficult decisions and look after his people. I'd highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys squad-based tactics games or any games with turn-based combat.

This is coming from a person who has been a fan of DOA since DOA1 in 1996. I do own the PS4 myself. I don't play online on either the Steam or PS4 version. I primarily play offline with local friends in both versions. Lastly, the game is fun and the only professionally developed 3D Fighting Game on PC currently.
The PS4 version only goes up to 1080P and has no anti-aliasing. The PS3 version only goes up to 720P and also has no anti-aliasing.
The benefits that come out of the "Soft Engine" are different weighting effects on the boobs, and Sub Surface Scatter on the character skin causing it to have more of a 'glow' like effect.
If you care about those two things over having a higher resolution and anti-aliasing then that's fine. I care more about the higher resolution and anti-aliasing.
The only other thing you'd choose the PS4 version over the PC version is if you want every single stage, of which the PS4 version currently has 4 stages the PC version does not, because each uses DX11 effects.
Fighting game system wise, the game is exactly the same as the console versions. The Steam version also still gets balance patch updates when the console versions get them. Overall, the game is well optimized, it's just not built from the ground up for the PC. So controller support and video settings are pretty bare bones. Lastly, online is just a quick play type of match where your opponent is practically random and you can't invite friends (though chances of finding friends if you coordinate is possible).
Overall, I'd suggest picking it up, especially if you don't have access to a PS4. You'll get the same overall game experience. I do wish the game had an online lobby mode just because the online netcode in the Steam version is better than the online netcode on any of the console versions (due mainly to no inherent console input delay). If you find a [5] bar match with someone in ranked it will run better than a [5] on the consoles.

I played through this game local co-op with a friend. We had an O.K. time.
But, what made the first game amazing in my eyes is not present in this game. And really, they're the only things this game does; the puzzles and the shooting.
The first game in this series was an extremely refreshing twin stick shooter/puzzler. The shooting was incredibly solid and the puzzles were INCREDIBLY INGENIOUS. This new Lara Croft twin stick shooter is shorter, the combat is easier, and the puzzles are also easier, less impactful, and recycled from the first game. In the end, this game is about 1/3 the length of the first. Less shooting. Less puzzles. Less fun.
I just want to mention the puzzles one last time. I want to do this because the first game took me by surprise. Your characters have limited abilities but the developers were able to create unique, well thought out puzzles around those abilities. There were points in the first game where me and my friend would have to stop and reconsider the uses of our abilities to figure out puzzles. Again, the puzzles in the first were really well designed. I played this new game with that same friend and we breezed through this game in a matter of days. Such a short disappointing game.
If you have not played the first game in this series, go grab a friend and play that game. Enjoy that unique co-op experience. Savour that game though because it is one of a kind and you will not find that experience again especially in this game.

This simple clicking cartoon game is WAY harder than it seems. Your superhero will often not fullfill his job. There are MANY paths to choose from which results in great replayability. Each time you can't defeat FEAR you just want to try it again, often resulting in another failure and so on. It's very difficult to find all the required clues in one go and you will often have only one at the eventual end (where you automatically lose). Even I haven't found ANY way to stop Fear yet (and I played it for 4 full hours (each round doesn't take that long)).
BUT don't despair. There are enough guides which can help you if you're really hopeless. And don't think you can't enjoy the game without winning. There are many funny choices (often resulting in achievements) and the combat (yes, you can fight in this game!) is very cool and it even has a very epic soundtrack.
Conclusion: It's very challenging, but you will enjoy this game, no matter if you win or lose.

TL;DR; Review; It's a rogue like. You will die a lot, and you will die to pure randomness sometimes. Is the game bad? Hell no, it's a lot of fun. But if you're not prepared to put up with rogue-like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t-RNG at times, it will♥♥♥♥♥♥you off.
Ignore [most of] the negative reviews that complain about dying or repetition and all that. These are people that either A) Got very mad and wrote it in the heat of the moment or B) Are just bad at understanding the concept of rogue-likes (Particularly that they are games where you die and you star over, and over and over, with many random elements).
I realize calling negative reviewers 'upset' is in poor taste, and I don't mean to say the game is without flaws. But steams default "Most helpful" sorting shows almost half the reviews as being negative, and most are complaining about how 'hard' the game is. (Despite the overall score being 90% and, the recent score as of writing this is also 90% with 40 reviews).
The game is hard. No dobut. And you will be upset sometimes about dying. As the tldr says, there is a lot of RNG at times. Take a drink of water out of a weird lake? Well, you might die, you might be fine. Sometimes its your only option because loot RNG ♥♥♥♥ed you and you have no other potable drinking source.
It's definitely not for everyone, but the same can be said for any rogue-like. I mean imagine FTL, one of the most loved modern rogue-likes. Most of the criticism thrown at NEO Scavenger can be thrown at it as well. It's repetitive (especially after playing several hours in a row), it punishing at times, and the RNG can screw you hard at times.
One criticism I can sympathize with is that the beginning is repetitive. You start the game out the same way each time. In FTL you can have a wildly different playthrough from each start, but in here, it's the same location and series of events each time. To me, it's not a big deal, I don't find it boring, and it's at most 5-10 minutes before you already have a radically different playthrough. But when you first start playing, you'll probably play through the beginning a fair few times. (Although it's not as bad as it seems, as the beginning can play out a few different times, which will keep you entertained the first couple of deaths).
There are clunky parts to the game, and for one the art style isn't my favorite. It's pretty, but it looks like it's 10 years out of date to me. It looks like a point and click CRPG from several years ago. Maybe that's intentional, and it's mostly a personal niggle. The quality of the art is fine, but it's the style I am not overly fond of.
Beyond that, there is a surprisng amount of depth here. There are tons of incredibly rare items, and you will fear for your life during most encounters.
It simulates a post apocalyptic scavenger situation fairly well (in the sci-fi sense, not some preppers training fantasy).
I'm just disappointed by the amount of "helpful" reviews that are essentially the same negative reviews over and over. While they have good points, if you know and like what you're getting into, they're not negatives.
But be aware, it is punishing. The RNG in this one can be especially brutal.
If you like rogue-likes, especially challenging ones, this is the one for you.
If you're the kind of person to throw your controller at the wall when you lose at a game, you should probably stay away from this.
Try the demo if you're apprehensive.

OK, I changed my review. However, I will not sugarcoat how difficult this program is. Perhaps, there are people out there who have the talent to jump in, and learn this quickly. This review is for people who are not artist, and who are not in the graphics industry.
I have put many hours into learning blender. I work as an analyst at one of the largest healthcare firms in the world. I write complex SQLs and build excel spreadsheets. I'm not a dummy, but I have ZERO artistic ability, and coming into blender I had ZERO experience in anything gfx related.
The interface is frustrating. It will take not hours, not days, but weeks to learn from the ground up. I have not given up, and I am closing in at 50 hours, as of this review. I barely know a thing. I can animate a 2d character like a f*n pro, though. I have bought books, watched youtube, and read articles. You will need them all.
The reality is this: even intelligent, competent people will struggle. You need to steel yourself, and your self esteem. This is beyond a doubt the most difficult thing I've ever tried to learn. I've put in many hours at trying my hand at 3d modeling. Its tough, man. Especially, if you struggled to draw a straight line your whole life.
It proably took me about 20 hours of hard, frustrating work to get a novice understanding of the animator feature. My guess is I will need to put in 125 total hours, before I get a 3d useable model made and rigged for animation.
I actually do love this program. I believe anyone can make a useable asset given enough time. Its just how much work are you willing to put in to figure this cryptic program out.

Grab the collection when it's on sale, this is a must have turnbased strategy game.
Gameplay:
You pick civilizations like you pick between species in Starcraft, but most of the civs you choose from are only slightly different from each other.
There are at least four dimensions to civ development: 1- cultural focus (warlike, merchantile, etc.), 2- direction of tech advancement, 3- unit or special building propigation (these are mutually exclusive investments for every turn), and 4- land manipulation for resources (they call it "tile improvement").
My only complaint is that the game gets tedious when you have more than a dozen cities to govern, and I don't believe that this is a symptom of turn-based strategy simulation, but a lack of imagination and experience by the programmers and designers involved. I'd love to write an algorithm and interface model for this game... is it mod time?

Not quite ready for release, but the positive reviews won't tell you this. A purchase now is buying an incomplete, and in many ways horribly broken game.
The main issue is that the campaign uses the unit balance for Multiplayer, and that is horrendously out of whack currently. And as the Imperium of Man tends to suffer the worst of this, and you only get an Imperium campaign, this ensures that immediately after the tutorial ends the average player will have to save-scum constantly to beat incredibly unfair fights because the units used against them are faster, have longer range and more assault capabilities.
As you only get a limited amount of fights you can take per week, and already by Week 5 even with a perfect save-scummed game you have to allow a system to be lost, this means that the campaign can literally become literally unwinnable very, very quickly indeed.
The campaign itself has some lovely cutscenes, but because it really is just the multiplayer re-skinned with the odd stationary objective added in, it doesn't currently have any real gameplay feel that would make it compelling to grind your way through it's poor balancing.
Multiplayer has proven more fun for me, because I don't play as the Imperium, but rather as Orkz. And now it's been patched in, only in 2v2 as having team mates averages out the imbalance issues. But even here, the poor state of release is blatantly obvious. There's no ability to type only to your team mate, for instance...
But the big one, and one which will absolutely destroy the online community, is that it's possible at any time for a team mate to concede the match on behalf of the entire team, with no vote mechanism or way to keep playing. I've actually been winning a match, but because my team mate died and didn't want to sit and watch until I finished it, he threw the game and gave us both the loss and took away my rewards for the destruction I had and would have finished wreaking. It's a perfect trolling mechanism; you can join teams just to frustrate others if you wish.
And sometimes the game hangs even trying to start a match. And the races the players are using at the team set up stage aren't the ones they actually have (so you can choose the wrong fleet set up to tackle them). And the text box is duplicated in the middle of the fleet set up screen for some reason.
That's not to say when the game works, is fair, and played in good spirits it isn't great fun... I've loved the roleplaying and rammin' head bangin' battles I've had online with people. But the game just isnt READY yet. When it's balanced, patched, and given a few more months love, I'll come back to this review and change it.
But that gets into the last issue I need to bring up; because they've chosen to declare that it's launch now, that means that in a few months when the game may be much more polished, you won't get the DLC for free any more. Also even if you purchase the game now, unless you do so from specific vendors, you won't get the DLC for free at all. The currently confirmed stores are the official Focus store, Steam, Gamesplanet and Amazon.de  I find this constant degrading of the respect for the public, and the ever increasing manipulation of them to squeeze ever more profit out of them highly distasteful.  I do not regret buying in early, because I've had hours of Orky fun online in my own way, but there's no denying that as an all-round product here and now, it's just not complete enough or polished enough to justify either a full price release and especially not to deny people the chance at content because of an arbitrary financial decision to claim it's now launched.
For now, just be very aware of what the game actually IS if you wish to risk purchasing it; it's still effectively an incomplete beta product at this point. The campaign isn't working very well, online support is flakey at best, and whilst there's fun to be had, you have to focus on a very narrow viewpoint to find it.

Just one turn more, just one map quickly... That's how it goes if you buy this game. XCOM: Enemy Unknown is a strategy game that can make you addictive!
But let's start at the beginning. XCOM: Enemy Unknown is a turn-based action-strategy game. Some of you maybe know the game from the 90s, where the first XCOM game came out under the name UFO: Enemy Unknown. 20 years later the developer decided to continue the series.
And the developer isn't just a random no-name company. The same company who developed the Civilization games are behind this game. And you will recognize it, because like Civilization this is also one of the greatest strategy titles, but with a whole different story.
In XCOM: Enemy Unknown you have to protect the world from enemies out of space. Yes, you have fight against aliens, but that isn't all. To defeat your opponents, you have to study the enemy, its technology, its strange powers and its fight strategies. You do this as the director of XCOM, an international department to protect the world from aliens. So beside your enemy, you have also to manage your own department with soldiers, weapons, scientists and mechanics.
This all is made in a way that makes really fun and maybe gets you addicted to it, but it's also very challenging. So if you get really fast mad by playing challenging games, do not buy this game. It's very hard to solve 100% of the game.
All in one, this is one of the top 10 strategy games of all time, a classic game not just for the old UFO fans, but for everyone who enjoys good strategy games!

This is the PC version of an old choose-your-own-adventure book.
What might work as a book - pick one of the options at random and see what happens - is just terrible for a video game. You cannot control what happens to your character at all. The comic book style looks great at first, but it's just clunky and clicking through the dialog quickly becomes a chore.
On my third playthrough I used a walkthrough, but because it was intended for the physical book it asked me to use clues where I couldn't on the PC version. I won't bother to try again
