This game is completely unique and 100% magical.
I had never played a Shelter game before this one, and I purchased this pretty much on a whim. Let me just say I'm totally glad I did.
I started out as a lonely badger cub. I trotted along for a while, confused at the mysterious symbols on the bottom left of my screen. I called out while I trotted along, hoping to find a friend. Eventually I heard what sounded like an echo, but was another badger cub returning my call. We trotted along together until we got to a river. I was heading north, my new friend west. We parted ways with a friendly emoticon and I waded into the river. I emerged on the other side to find another badger, and a rabbit. I introduced myself to their group with a hop and a wave. These guys were different from my first friend-they were FAST. (I didn't realize you could use shift to run yet, derp). I spammed my sad face and badger call when they started running. They tried to help me, asking what was wrong (?). Eventually though they left me behind, and I understood. They had places to be.
Shortly after that I figured out how to run, and started collecting the pretty flowers that dotted the landscape. I scaled the side of a mountain to find sparkly pieces that eventually gave me a nice new coat to try on. Eventually I got to the big tree, where I experienced my first group. We roamed the land as a cohesive unit, exploring and helping each other collect pieces. No one was left behind, and no one was forced to lead. We got to a cave after a while and everyone took the chance to rest. I had to leave at this point and spammed waves and sad faces. My group seemed to understand and they bid me farewell in return.
This game gives you an experience like no other. For the price there really is no reason not to buy it. I only hope that they continue to expand upon it, because I love the game and don't want to get bored of it once I've collected everything.
Some things they could add:
*More unlockables (animals, skins, emotes)
*Expand the map, it's already big but you become familiar pretty quickly
*Add more music, pleaseee!
*Make certain obelisks more difficult, for example animals have to speak in a certain order or do other actions such as hopping or sitting.
*Add a stamina bar and introduce food. Maybe just fruits/vegetables or include smaller animals like mice and voles? Make food replenish stamina and possibly other benefits.
*Include antagonists. Maybe wolves that mainly come out at night in more forested areas? Make them less likely to attack when in a group, literally fleshing out the benefits of "herd mentality". If you're "killed" by a wolf you start at the Tree and are separated from your group.
*Include actual in-game "mini games" like tag and hide and seek. If you're in a proximity of 4+ animals an option appears for everyone to select the mini game. Winners get random prizes like pieces or essence.
If they added things such as these and continue to expand routinely, I would have no problem paying $50+ for this game. There is nothing else like it.
ON A FINAL NOTE: This game isn't for people who like fast-paced action and need a linear objective to enjoy the game. It's about exploring, collecting, making friends, working together and using your imagination. :)

This game is something quite special to me. It is a true survivor game, that succeeds in making you feel accomplished by just surviving. You don't just find water or food that is ready to consume. You have to boil water to make it safe to drink, and cook food to prevent it from making you sick. You have to be extremely mindful of the weather and what you're wearing, as you can quickly die from freezing to death, or being wet. Even combat is extremely dangerous, where every threat can bring you down in the blink of an eye. Get shot in the head or heart by a pot shot? Doesn't matter if you're a pro soldier, you're dead. And then, even if you survive a battle, you can die from the infections of your wounds, internal hemorraging, etc.
I should make this clear in that you're not taught anything for this game. There is no tutorial. Experimentation, common sense, and a bit of knowledge about the world can take you a long ways. For example, you're not told to clean bandages prior to dressing wounds to avoid infections. Fire can be used to harden sharpened wood to make them effective weapons. As well as the variety of methods needed to treat sicknesses you can incur on your journies, which are just as dangerous as the guys with guns.
Make no mistake, you will die, many, horrible, deaths. This is not a game for those without patience and dedication. However, if you can deal with the pain of losing quite often, you will find that this game is quite fun. You are not a super soldier. You are not a prodigee of any kind. You're just some dude wearing nothing but a piece of cloth with an arm band. You're just as strong, or weak as anyone, or thing you can find in the wild.
Good luck, and good hunting. You'll need it.

text:
I can't help but to reccomend this game as it is Basiaclly a better version of the previous version (Metro 2033).
The novelties in this game are many and if you have played the predecessor you will spot them easily.
Apart from the new engine that makes the game very atmospheric (even more than the "original" version!) there are various minor and major changes that you may or may not look forward to.
The stealth mechanics have been reworked and you can unscrew lightbulbs as in metro last light and perform takedowns, both lethal and non-lethal. Furthermore gun customization was imported from Last Light, so you can now customize the guns the way you like.
Armors have been removed from the game (in the previous you could buy a stealth armor and a "JuggerNaut" armor) and enemies positions have been reworked (and other minor reworks that i won't mention because spoilers).
As far as the game goes it's pretty much the same as the other chapters, really atmospheric and challenging. The ranger mode really makes it so that the game is even more immersive, with removed hud, increased damage/difficulty and scarce ammo and bullets (the in-game currency)
One thing i really didn't like though is that I found the game to be extremely buggy in certain points and for no apparent reason too. I got micro stutters here and there and sometimes i had to restart whole portions of a level just because the game decided that it was time to start tuttering so that enemies could run past my sights and shoot me with all the comforts. On this side i think the redux version is really lacking and I can't help but think it could be executed really better. I could play metro 2033 with no problems with max details but the redux version really gave me a hard time.
In the end I think buying the game (maybe together with Last light so you can experience the whole package) is a great idea, but I really REALLY hope you don't run into the same stuttering issues I had because they'll end up ruining the whole experience of what I think is a really enjoyable and fun game. I Totally Reccomend This!

Ok I think I've got enough experience with this program to write a decent review on it...
Blender has had a notorious reputation, at least in my experience, with being a difficult program to learn. I agree. For someone who has never touched a 3D/CG program I cannot reccommend enough that you don't chose blender. It is difficult to catch on just because of the shear amount of things packed into it. It has made improvements, big improvements in my opinion since I first used it, it can still be a challenge to navigate and understand. If you have dabbled in 3D/CG software before, this will still have a bit of a big learning curve and some things to get used to, *cough* right-click *cough**cough*. Like I mentioned before it can be a bit confusing just because theres a lot you can do with it.
All that being said if you choose to stick around, if you choose to take the time to learn this, either on your own(via youtube, etc.) or paying for lessons (CG Cookie, etc.), if you choose to deal with the initial frustration that may accompany learning this program (some people might be frustrated longer than others it all depends), then you will have access to one of the most powerful CG Creation Suites in terms of what it can do, and how much it costs(free by the way). If you want to take it on I'd recommend sticking to only one feature, like 3D modeling. Focus on learning that before you start trying to learn animation or compositing (Thats not the trick that's just how I went about it.) When you get familiar enough with it everything else sort of falls together. Now lets get down to buisness...
Pros:
-Can do a lot
-3D Modeling
-Animating
-Compositing
-Video Editing
-2D Animation (Grease Pencil)
-Sculpting
-3D Painting
-Game Creation (BGE)
-Python Scripting
-Capable of photorealism
-Add-ons (Free and paid)
-can optimize some aspects of blender bringing it close to some professional program equivalent
-Pretty big community willing to help out
-youtube tutorials
-Paid course tutorials (CG Cookie, Blender Guru, etc.)
-Community Forums
-just google it =P
Cons:
- A lot to learn in one suite
- Not for the faint of heart
- Nor for the short of patience
- Don't expect to learn this overnight
- Right-clicking, not huge but can take a bit to get used to
- because there's so much you can do in blender, when asking the community anywhere a question you need to be
specific (ie., "I wanna know how to make my flower look like this one." Like in the compositor, materials, textures, etc.
not a very good example but meh.)
- Blender is generalized not specialized/optimised
-In other words comparing its Sculpting to something like Zbrush you'll see some stark contrasts
-Same holds true with some of its other features
-Personally, though, I think its animation (rigging, weight painting, animating) is better than Maya but that's me.
- Blender Game Engine (BGE) is real nice and you can make some impressive things, however it does fall short when you compare it to other game engines like Unity or Unreal

Personal experience with this is I was first exposed to blender when I was 12 in 2006 I dabbled in it and was really confused what was happening eventually after a few days I just gave up. I didn't feel I was making any progress let alone know what I was doing. I didn't touch it again until nearing the end of my sophomore year in college since then I got more involved with it. When I found out it came on steam I was already in 2nd semester Junior year so what you see are hours after I found it here I've had a longer time with this than what you see. Prior to this I was taking classes that taught 3DS Max, Maya, Zbrush, and Mudbox. Blender was self-taught (not counting CG Cookie).
All That being said I'm sure I might have missed some things but I hoped I explained enough to answer most questions on this.

This game is not for everyone. The main character, Kyle Crane can be VERY bland at times, although they improved on that a bit in the DLC the following. The Story is above average, but not exceptional. I would argue that some of the sidequests on whatnot shine more light on the world of Harran and concepts than the main story. The gameplay CAN get repetitive if you play for long enough, but I would say thats at intervals every 10 hours or so.
Dying Light was developed by Techland, who developed a bunch of other Zombie games that I never played but I hear incorporate similar systems. There is a loot ranking for weapons, crafting materials, valuables, etc. Parkour in this game is as flushed out, if not more than lets say Mirrors Edge. However, once you hit a certain rank and unlock the grappling hook parkour becomes less of a requirement and more of a leisure which is interesting, so no hardcore parkour all the way through. The Controls with a controller can be VERY odd at times, but on PC I feel as though the control scheme is flushed out a lot more. Dying Light has a certain humor that can really be found through exploring than pushing through the main story, and believe me the humor is worth it (easter eggs, weapons). The atmosphere of a CubanEsque city is also VERY nifty.
Let us talk about what you are buying here. Dying Light Enhanced Edition comes with all the DLC, including the major ones, except for 3-4 minor cosmetic dlc. Would I suggest this game full price? Nah Boi. 30 bucks or under, and you got yourself a good steal.
Now for some cringy rating. I would give 8 Deboas/10 Deboas. If the game ran slightly smoother, then 9/10. If Kyle Crane (queer name) was a bit more engaging, and the story was polished just a tad, I would say 9.999999999/10 deboas. Remember, no game is perfect!1!!!!11!1!!

The visuals look great and the fighting is smooth. You don't have as many of the crazy moves of other fighting games and have to rely mostly on kicks and punches. However, the fights are still highly enjoyable with different difficulty modes to play. There are many characters to choose from and you can also play in tag team mode. The story mode was highly enjoyable and fairly immersive, although it won't win any oscars.
You can buy more costumes at quite a premium rate. However, maybe they will become more reasonable in the sale, If not you would have to be a die hard fan to get them.
As the game stands it is still worth getting but I would like those achievements to hunt at some point.

I went into this without any experience in Game Books, but I was excited about it. I've always been a fan of choose your own adventure stories, and thought that this gameplay would add another dimension to that formula.
This ended up being something else altogether though. While the freedom to do as you wish is present, the punishment/reward system feels out of whack. My success seemed determined on my finding a specific set of clues, which would see me following a very specific direction in my story. Every other attempt I made, regardless of whether I saved the city and the civilians around me in each mini-encounter, the game would end part way through with everyone dying in a bomb blast.
I like the presentation and think the adaptation into a video game worked, just that the game book at the core that drags the experience down. I'm not sure if it's just this game book i have an issue with, or wheter it would extend to the whole platform/genre, but I'm not eager to try any others after having played this one. Whatever sense of exploration I wanted to feel was bogged down by a heavy sense of tediousness.

Let's start by saying that after few matches the game it's not bad graphically and the gameplay it's good.

Speaking about multiplayer the game is missing the online features at the moment and it's one thing that I'm upset about but anyway don't panic it will arrive soon.

Pros:
+Super powers are relatively fun to use
+New weapons
+Fun (while it lasts)
+Some new customisation options for your character
+New enemies provide a new combat experience
Here comes the bad part
-Super powers render all vechiles useless, however the entire customization option for them is still there and feels like wasted time
-Super powers are great at first, but i only found myself using less than half of the powers provided in general gameplay and combat, and only used the others when forced to in missions
-The game felt short, i dont know how long i played the third for as i did so on console but I completed the main quest, all side quests and find all collectibles in less than 24 hours of gameplay, so judge for yourself how much you want out of this game.
-I did'nt really enjoy the environment, at first i thought using steelport again for another game was a bit meh, then i began to like and enjoy the subtle differences they threw in, but THEN i began to notice the cobying and pasting of buildings and areas, this may have been the same in III however i didn't notice it as i was driving around rather than running and flying, i just found myself with a permanent sence of dejavu when moving around the city.
-The collectibles were pretty easy to get all of, most being in similar places on similar buildings i found i only used the collectible finder to pinpoint the area of the last few.
-limited enemy types, in III we found ourselves fighting pyros, Brutes, Sinper helicopters, ect. But now we have...The police, The aliens, The alien whith a slightly different weapon, and the warden (which granted are quite fun to fight)
-Overall i found it a bit easy, i play through most games on the default normal dificulty, but i found myself having to ramp it up to get even the tinyest bit of challenge
In conclution, this was a fun playthrough and for a few bucks was a great buy, however it just feels incomplete, i am happy with my purchase but would be a bit iffy if i payed $20, also i could only get the "low violence version as i am in Aus, but thats only a problem for some. I would reccomend waiting for a sale and buy the dlc bundle as well because i fell ther is just not enough content-<24hrs for 100%

Saints Row meets Prototype-like mobility super powers! And it is as fun as you'd expect. Explore the simulation and kill everything opposing Saints while jumping over buildings and turning your enemies into frozen statues.

The controls are a bit wonky by default, and I'm not sure if the wonkiness can be fixed when using an XBOX One controller. The DLC prices are insulting to my intelligence. It's the kind of pricing that makes me wonder if they're proactively trying to encourage piracy.
I've not yet beaten the game, but the story mode thus far is pretty mediocre by fighting game standards (fighting game stories generally being VERY bad.) The controls, though mapped strangely seem pretty solid. The counter system is a bit trickier / requires more precise timing than some previous DOA games.
My dual Geforce 670 GTX setup occasionally has frame rate visibly dip, but generally stays well within a playable frame rate. The lack of online play is a bummer, but hopefully won't completely suck on release of the feature.
The lack of current gen console features is rather dissapointing, especially when compared to some of the very smoothly done ports like Metal Gear Solid.
If you're a fan of DOA and you don't do console gaming anymore, this is worth picking up. If you have a current gen console, this may not be worth the investment. I also hear you need a beefy rig to maintain decent framerates. Also, the game doesn't support 2560x1440 resolution for some odd reason.  Annoying.
The new and improved jiggly bit system that made it to PS4 and XBOX ONE are apparently absent in this, so that's a minor gripe (there's this thing on the internet called porn-o-graphy, I hear).
Thus far, no real must have mods have popped up (the nude mods don't look very good, so I've no interest), though there's a Shemue mod that looked kinda fun. If and when modders figure out how to make and import new costumes, I'd be really curious to see what cool stuff folks come up with.
Until then, this game is worth recommending to fighting game fans, but with reservations. If jiggly boobs and special effects are more important to you than a decent fighting system, this version of the game may dissapoint. From my limited experience thus far, it seems like a pretty good fighting game with a decent (though not great) port. My biggest gripe is the devs need to pull their heads out of their butts and price the DLCs reasonably.

Stuff I liked:
1. Win/Loss counters. I really needed this thing to see how I'm doing in general.
2. Random BGM now switches between games in a set instead of using the initially selected BGM for the entire set. Just a pedantic thing, but now it's "true" random.
Stuff I didn't like:
1. The stage disabling feature doesn't matter for matches where you're Player 2. Even if you've personally blocked a stage, if the other player picked it as their favorite, it'll still be used.
2. Still not having a character select screen before matches. The "Random" option is a mind-game that I miss being able to do.
Other notable things:
1. The Respect tab works, so we actually have a clue what the "Respect" parameter means now. Though (based on speculation) having that rely completely on other players watching your replays, favoriting you and stuff means that you need some degree of fame (or infamy) before you get any (and will probably be gamed via fake accounts and stuff)... which sort of makes sense; gotta build a name before that name means anything, right?
2. It looks like it's harder to peak the Power/Defense/Technique chart. Did the algorithm become more strict or something?
Note that none of the above has anything to do with what this beta is meant to test, and unfortunately I can't tell if it's better or worse in battle, though it seems battle statistics load up faster, so that's a good sign.
Will withhold judgement until further review, so disregard the thumbs on this review.

Neo Scavenger is a quite unwieldy post-apocalyptic turn based survival RPG-roguelike. What sounds complex ultimately ends up being just as complex as it sounds, meaning that more often than not, the player character will ultimately die very soon due to quite ridiculous RNG. Either you'll simply find no food while scavenging. Or you'll get an infection while scavenging. Or you'll get ambushed while scavenging. Or you'll get shot by another NPC survivor from several hundred meters away while being armed with as little as a multitool / knife. You'll die to starvation, you'll die to bleeding, you'll die to infection, you'll die to dehydration, you'll die in combat and even more often after successful combat due to injuries taken, you'll die to electrocution, you'll die falling down somewhere .... the list goes on and on.
NEO Scavenger is absolutely brutal, lethal and frustrating, which makes it one of the most deadly roguelikes I have played recently. It does a lot of things right, but it is lacking in two key elements: Accessibility and fun. Sadly, NEO Scavenger is neither. Not due to a lack of presentation, but due to a lack of intuitive controls as well as descriptive tooltips. Every battle is massively lacking in information about status effects or success & failure of actions taken and even taking the actions themselves is resolved in an extremely unwieldy and bothersome manner by picking an action not from a list but from icons which resemlbe items within your squarish inventory, which have confusing icons and no descriptive tooltips whatsoever. NEO scavenger is not only a lot of trial and error, it also leaves the player completely in the dark regarding mechanics and the result of actions taken. More often than not my character died to injuries I wasn't even aware I had taken due to a lack of information during combat or during random events while scavenging.
NEO Scavenger had a lot of potential, but the way it currently is and the way it will most likely remain indefinitely, I am unable to recommend it to anyone, not even die-hard roguelike fans.

The 'Race' series comes from a little Swedish company called Simbin, not the most evocotive name. But when you take the entire series as a whole, they have created an absolute master piece of PC gaming.
Race 07, the core game of the series, is primarily focused on the WTCC (World Touring Car Championsip) for 2007, along with serveral 'support' series you can race also. Having learnt leassons from previous racing sims, Simbin have just kept adding to the game, & despite the final collection numbering near double figures, the game is still stable, reliable & entertaining as day one.
The one thing that should grab the attention of serious racing-sim fans is the fact that behind the less glamourous series' is in fact nothing less than a licensed version of the rFactor engine, a sim that has gone beyond being a game, it is tool that is even used by top racing teams to train professional drivers!
Once you have the full works of the Race series, you can race everything from Caterhams, MINI Coopers, WTCC cars of various series, Formula BMW, GT cars, muscle cars... The number of different cars on offer is quite astounding.
However, the real bonus to the Race series is that Simbin have left the game entirely open to being heavily modded, & in fact, have made allowances for making the game easy to mod, from car skins, to tracks, graphics tweaks to entirely new cars that have never existed in the game. Despite having added a huge number of mods of various types to my install, the game remains stable & utterly reliable, something that could quite easily be the make or break of a modding favourite.
On the downside, you pretty much need the whole hog to ensure mods will work, meaning you do have to commit to it. Also, given the quality of the 'sim' part, if you don't have, or never intend to, get a steering wheel, don't bother with it, you'll just be wasting the game & not getting the full experience.
It adds up to a game where you can race almost anything you want to, on pretty much any track you like. There are even online racing clubs who use the game.
I've reached a point where I actually wouldn't even consider buying new racing sims as Race has everything I need, with all the quality & realism of a truly great game that could only be this great on a PC.

Tl;Dr: It was really good game before Steamworks patch, now it's greenlight-level turd. Don't buy it, even heavily discounted, unless they fix UI/matchmaking/OpenGL rendering.
While the game was partially on Steam, it was pretty much a great Quake2/3 "sequel", with small but dedicated community and nice way to play old maps on really good working engine. However, it's not anymore.
Since the game went full Steamworks (and, by the way, from Free to Play into 10 euro product) - it wen't to crap, and i can't recommand it anymore. Even while i got to keep it for free, even while i can now host my own servers, it's just not worth your time (and money) anymore.
First of all, for some idiotic reason Zenimax/iD decided to change something in graphics engine. It's either not openGL anymore, or they've just missed some setup, point is - while nobody played Quake Live for visual fidelity, i liked my anti-aliased, clean, neat and simple look of the game.
Suddenly, from quite polished albeit oldschoold product, it changed into what looks now like some indie asset flipping Unity turd. Way to go, Zenimax!
But that's obviously not the main issue. The interface now is just bad. You want to just jump into quick match? Well, bad luck Kevin, now you need to browse through 100 empty servers manually. Because apparently automated matchmaking system was fine in F2P product, but it isn't in 10 euro product. Match browser got dumbed down from pretty cool filter based UI to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ "one-search-form" tag system. And it's just inconvinent and sluggish. Way to go, Zenimax!
Did i mentioned that all servers are now empty, since all players got their statistics/achievment reset? Personally, i don't give a crap. It's nice that i can now unlock Steam achievments. But in reality, it does matter. Becuase there is simply no players any more to get the achievments with. As a Q2/3 player, i often just jumped in Quake Live to play on The Edge (q2dm1) or Longest Yard (tltf) not giving crap about other/newer levels. Guess what? Nobody plays them anymore, and even now everyone can setup server - it just dilluted the server pool, effectively creating thousands of empty hosts. Way to go, Zenimax!
I can imagine the game had problem keeping up in F2P model with host subcribers. But it's not problem with the price, or even with achievment/stat reset. It's problem with really, really bad patch, that messed up a lot of polished components of the game. Even such minor stuff like fonts are now wrong/glitched.
All you had to do was implement Steam achievments and put 10 euro pricetag on this game. Instead, as developers you decided to fix what wasn't broken, and broke the last quick paced online arena shooter. It's not Quake Live anymore. It's Quake Dead.
Don't buy this game, go for old Quakes or Unreal Tournament alpha instead.

I can't help but to reccomend this game as it is Basiaclly a better version of the previous version (Metro 2033).
The novelties in this game are many and if you have played the predecessor you will spot them easily.
Apart from the new engine that makes the game very atmospheric (even more than the "original" version!) there are various minor and major changes that you may or may not look forward to.
The stealth mechanics have been reworked and you can unscrew lightbulbs as in metro last light and perform takedowns, both lethal and non-lethal. Furthermore gun customization was imported from Last Light, so you can now customize the guns the way you like.
Armors have been removed from the game (in the previous you could buy a stealth armor and a "JuggerNaut" armor) and enemies positions have been reworked (and other minor reworks that i won't mention because spoilers).
As far as the game goes it's pretty much the same as the other chapters, really atmospheric and challenging. The ranger mode really makes it so that the game is even more immersive, with removed hud, increased damage/difficulty and scarce ammo and bullets (the in-game currency)
One thing i really didn't like though is that I found the game to be extremely buggy in certain points and for no apparent reason too. I got micro stutters here and there and sometimes i had to restart whole portions of a level just because the game decided that it was time to start tuttering so that enemies could run past my sights and shoot me with all the comforts. On this side i think the redux version is really lacking and I can't help but think it could be executed really better. I could play metro 2033 with no problems with max details but the redux version really gave me a hard time.
In the end I think buying the game (maybe together with Last light so you can experience the whole package) is a great idea, but I really REALLY hope you don't run into the same stuttering issues I had because they'll end up ruining the whole experience of what I think is a really enjoyable and fun game. I Totally Reccomend This!

FTL surprised me with its flexibility, difficulty, and overall enjoyment level.  I ended up buying this game on sale based on some reviews that I watched and soon decided that it would have definitely been worth paying full-price for.  Additionally, they came out with a mobile version of the game that is just as great.
First, the world is constantly changing.  I've played through the campaign several times now and never had a similar playthrough.  There are times when you cruise through space without meeting much resistance and feel invincible, only to hit a solid wall of enemies that instantly end your game.  There are also times where you're constantly blocked at every door and have to fight your way through.  Both situations are rewarding in their own way, as well as all situations that fall in between.
Ships are diverse and relatively easy to unlock.  They are not given to you for nothing which leaves you with a feeling of accomplishment, but they are very attainable if you want to put in the time.
I have been playing this game on and off for several months and have come nowhere close to beating it.  Perhaps this speaks to my inability to master the game, but I like to think that it is difficult enough to keep me challenged in a world where games have switched to a method of instant-gratification.  I never become frustrated enough to quit, but i'm not cruising through the game feeling invincible either.
Be prepared to spend lots of time gripping your arm rests as you worry that the next shot through your shields will be the one that ends it all!
We aren't seeing enough intellectually challenging platformers like this.

I really like the game, mainly playing for Chaos and Eldar fleets, graphics really good if you turn anti-aliasing off, not sure, if they fixed that yet, maybe they already did. They were some issues in the beta in multiplayer balance, but overall the launch was good compared even to some established game developers and publishers. Mechanically it is really well thought out and the customization keeps me like in XCOM getting attached to the ships. The favors are awesome in their aesthetic and traits.
I havent played the campaign yet to the end, but seems to be good and with a formidable AI. As a grand strategy fan I would have wished for more strategic play, but I understand the standards of RTS. The fleets are very different and you have to learn how to use them. That is something very remarkable for the current market of RTSes, where in multiplayer even when there are different races and units, they are mechanically similar. It is not as much variable as Starcraft, but nevertheless. In the department of art and design and gameplay, this game really shines. The opinion on customisation and RPG elements is a subjective one, I think it is a good idea to implement it in an RTS, Im okay with it, I liked it in King Arthur and like it now, I dont mind that it is like a battle between wizards. Subjectively, I enjoy the gameplay very much and even more the owning and tailoring of my ships.
To some valid criticism:
The main thing is balance, matchmaking, speed and grind. I dont know how matchmaking improved since the beta, but in the beta, it was pretty painful and degraded an otherwise awesome experience. It is also valid to point out that there is a lot of micro-management in the more chaotic battles and the grind for skirmish and multiplayer is a little bit too time-consuming. I would reduce the time to get to the full admiral in skirmish and multiplayer and give players more tactical cogitator debit in multiplayer. And the upgrades are a little bit unbalanced. In the crew department, the navigator could have a turning bonus and the boarding mechanic is I think overpowered, so that I always pick upgrading the troop level. I always go for the disruption bomb and the recon skills are pretty unattractive. I personally think, the stasis bomb is useless unless you are fighting against a dumb enemy or the Orks and the only use of it is in catching some coward in breakthrough, data retrieval and assassination, who you cant overrun because of the different speeds of the fleets. After they nerfed the nova cannon, it became also useless.
Overall, it is a very enjoyable game and a dream come true for even people, like me, who are not familiar with 40K, but who are fans of steampunk, this is pornography for this genre and for fans of space and naval RTS.

This is just the first iteration of my review.
I have played the first handful of missions from the campaign and some battles in multiplayer.
I liked the campaign very much. Everything works and the story is interesting and reflect the setting of Warhammer 40,000 very well.
My multiplayer experience was not as well as that of the campaign. There are two reasons for that. The first is that the party system of the multiplayer has some bugs. If you change your general and/or your faction, you cannot rejoin with your former member of your party. The only thing that helps is to restart the game.
Also you cannot choose which kind of mission you want to play in multiplayer. It is chosen randomly. Most of the time is Cruiser Clash.
The last thing is balancing. I am not experienced enough to judge how balanced the different factions are. But I can judge that I am playing against players that have a lot more experience than me and therefore are able to destroy me and my teammate hard. I guess this results from a bad matchmaking system in combination with the fact that there was a multiplayer beta in which a lot of people could already train their skills in this game. I guess this problem will become more irrelevant if I play the game more, but it should not happen anyway.
Graphics, sound and gameplay are good to very good. The setting is a matter of taste. If you like Warhammer 40,000 or dark/gothic science fiction you will like it.
All in all I review this game as positive, but it has some flaws, too.

The game does have some optimization issues still which I'm sure will be addressed throughout the release process.  Especially noted in the introduction 'loading' screen (the infamous dragon screen) which will take a couple minutes to load into your server of choice (I'm running a GTX1080 with 24Gigs of ram and notice this even).  Besides this, I've also noticed some issues playing on 'official' servers with lag on gathering resources, rubberbanding here and there but not often.
TIP:  To true get the most of this game at it's current point with the least about of issues, play on 'unofficial' servers for now until capacity management and performance is improved.

I own a lot of FF books, loved them since I was a kid. As soon as I saw this on Steam, I threw money at it. Was I disappointed? Yes.
The graphics are really nice, well-done comic style that really fits the theme of the game. The name generator and much of the text is anywhere between amusing and downright hilarious. Gameplay is set over the course of several days, giving you a chance to stop (or ignore) different crimes, explore different locations, and make a lot of decisions about where to go next.
So what's the problem?
It is too faithful to the unforgiving nature of the original books - specifically, those books where you had to collect certain items ('do you have a <statue, etc>?') and / or paragraph numbers to go with them, meaning that if you took one misstep, you would end up failing. The better amongst the original gamebooks didn't use that system, and gave you more chance of being able to complete it without having to follow an absolute sequence. Yes, there is a rewind feature ... but that made it feel a bit more hopeless to me. You have to pick the exact right way through, otherwise, you get to sit through that same damnable ending of the bad guys win, city is destroyed, you fail. Along the way, you will find lots of clues that you're supposed to match to various locations; I've played through maybe 3 or 4 times, and managed to match one or two clues, total. Frustrating. I keep thinking, yeah, I want to beat this ... but every time I go back to play, I think about how frustrating it is, knowing that if I don't follow that golden path, none of my choices are going to mean anything, and I am going to see that same ending again. Also, stopping crimes / capturing bad guys nets you Hero Points (for use with the in-game collectible card system) ... if you fail the adventure, said points are generally wiped out by the loss you take for failing the main objective.
Maybe I was more flexible as a kid, and the books were harder than I remember, but I can only think of one out of the dozens I played through that gave me anything like this much trouble (Starship Traveller)
tl;dr: might be worth it for the nostalgia and the fun of the first couple of playthroughs, but can get very frustrating, and feel very shallow.

Now that visual novels are quickly becoming the next big thing on Steam it’s getting harder to find out which ones are worth the money and time, and which ones aren’t. Appointment With FEAR might not reinvent the genre but it does its best to give you a unique experience nevertheless.
I can be very short about Appointment With FEAR. It’s a challenging, but fun interactive graphic novel where you make important choices and battle enemies, graphic novel-style. In other words, you fight crime, to the best of your abilities. And while you’re doing all of this you also have to find out where the evil organization FEAR is having its next secret meeting. The thing is, you only have three days to find out. Oh dear.
The game starts with you selecting a gender and, after that, your abilities/superpowers. Then it will show you an avatar that you may use as your character. If you don’t like it you can switch between several other designs and once you’ve made your final choice you can then select a primary and secondary color for your costume and after that a totally random and wacky name (that probably doesn’t come anywhere close to what you had in mind).
Once the game begins you’re given choices about what you want to do and where you want to go. So you can go to work and on the way there stop a thief or get to a seemingly more important situation. Your CrimeWatch will also frequently give you updates about situations and villains.
Some situations will help you find clues that you can later use to try and solve other situations; getting a note from a person on the street might help you prevent an assassination on the president later on, for example. All you have to do then is select the appropriate clue from the list and the game will give you new options to work with. If you never received the note then he might be assassinated. This is just one of the many situations the game throws at you. In fact, there are so many choices that you never really know if it’s the right one until a few hours into the game, after you played a few more games. Yes, your first game might not last as long as you think. That’s partially thanks to the fact that it’s game over if you didn’t find out where the secret meeting is located within the given ‘time’ limit (there’s no timer, but obviously doing activities progresses your day).
Each of the superpowers has you finding different clues so you can’t just make the same choices each and every time you play with a different character. These superpowers also impact the fights with villains and other enemies; some might become harder, others easier. Fights are turn-based and you can select an easy, medium and hard attack, with the latter one having a bigger chance to miss (but of course it does more damage if the hit connects). If any of the stamina stats is depleted then the battle is over. So far, the battles haven’t been much of a problem and they’re usually rather easy.
Solving crimes and problems will help you earn hero points. These will show up once the game is over and if you earned more than 15 points you’ll earn a free FEAR card. If you fail to solve a problem a predefined number will be subtracted from your total score. Let’s back up for a bit. ‘FEAR cards ?’, I hear you saying. Yup, there are collectible cards to be earned just by playing. Beat an enemy or properly solve a problem and it might earn you a card. There are quite a few cards to be collected and these range from common to very rare. By finding and collecting clues you can try to increase the percentage of getting a better card. Each clue will increase this number by a few percent. It’s a time consuming activity and it will take you probably tens of hours before you have the complete set. The problem is, you’ll probably have lost interest after 5-10 hours of playing. There just isn’t enough gameplay to keep you occupied for longer than that.
The presentation of Appointment With FEAR is more than solid. It has a comic book vibe (with lots of unused space on the sides, unfortunately) with some cool animated effects, even though the use of effects is kept to a minimum. The characters and drawings are done very well, but some of the civilians’ faces could’ve used a little more work in my opinion. Some of them are just plain ugly.
Clicking the mouse will move the screen down in comic-book-style-fashion, which looks cool and is absolutely something you would expect to see in a game about being a superhero.
Unfortunately the music is quite repetitive and the sound effects are also kept to a minimum so that department could also have benefited from some extra work and polish. There’s no voice acting, by the way.
Length-wise a game will last you roughly thirty minutes max I think. But it’s fun to just fool around with the choices to see what happens. However, should you decide to try and complete the game it will probably take you at least 5 hours before you’re done with the first character. After that you can try out the other characters and even though the clues are then found in other places many of the other events will play out the exact same way as your other character. So, like I said, it will probably be fun for 5-10 hours. Others might enjoy it more, of course, and some might enjoy it less. It’s hard to say really.
Appointment With FEAR is a cool game with quite a bit of replay value. I have to say that I expected a more straightforward game here so I can say that I was, once more, pleasantly surprised. It’s a game about making choices so if you’re looking for an action packed game you will have to continue your search. But, if you liked what you just read and/or if you’re intrigued (even if it’s a little bit) then this is definitely something you have to check out. Recommended !

This genre has changed for the worse, not because players don't like fighting games anymore but because fighting games aren't anything like they used to be.
Back in the day anyone could play SF2 and button mash their way to a win. This encouraged new players to try their hand at it, and it encouraged regulars to step their game up so as to not get embarrassed by some noob. Nowadays all these fighting games are overly complicated which discourages players from even trying them out.
Problems plaguing the game and this genre as a whole:
1. Replacing characters = Learning a completely new set of moves, timing, and character hitboxes. Where are Blanka, E-Honda, and Sagat?
2. Gameplay = This game is so SLOW I honestly feel insulted. I feel as if Capcom thinks I have a case of the DOWNS and doesn't want me to overwork my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ brain.
3. Artstyle = I don't care for it. Why are all the characters misproportioned? The characters in the street fighter series started out proportionate so why or how they evolved into cavemen and alien women I will never understand.
4. Storyline = A person would in fact have to have more than a mild case of the DOWNS to think this story was even remotely good. I mean what is this♥♥♥♥♥♥ In regards to the story, I really think Capcom has to start again from scratch.
5. Super Powers = Overcomplication.
V power, don't need it, never asked for it, don't even want it. DISLIKE!
On top of all the super abilites and moves each character already has, V power gives them even more!
Why?
When SF3 was released the player base was on a huge decline. Some argue it was because the market had become saturated with clones and others that consoles killed the arcades. The real reason players left was because everytime Capcom released new content it completely changed the way the game was played.
Eventually, the game became so skill based it was impossible for a new player to win against a regular ever. Now when a noob shows up he gets utterly ANNIHALTED and writes the game off, because the time required to get to a competent level is simply not worth the investment.

First things first: This game is perfectly playable - and vastly enjoyable - with a gamepad. There. I said it.
I'm not saying that it is the BEST way to get the MOST out of the game but the reviews I'm seeing posted that state the game is only playable with a steering wheel are misleading at best.
The only thing that will ruin this great game is a lack of patience. And it does require patience! If I flick the thumbstick too much the car spins; if I squeeze the trigger too much while trying to turn the car spins; one wheel off the track and on the grass? Guess what? The car spins!
However, after a couple of hours focussing on one car (Mini Cooper) on one track (Brands Hatch) I eventually became accustomed to the physics of the game and began to put in some pretty decent lap times. Then, emboldened, I even started removing some of the driving assists. After more hours I became very comfortable and was putting in consistently quick laps.
Now I've just got to learn how to handle the rest of the cars. And how to race round the rest of the tracks. And I can't wait.
If you have patience and either a gaming wheel or a gamepad, buy this game - it's all of £2.49! It is so much more rewarding than any other racing game I have played. Also, there is a modding community that is still very active and has done a great job professionally recreating pretty much every circuit ever raced on. So if you fancy taking a Touring Car or a Formula 3000 car for a spin (literally in my case!) around Snetterton, Aintree, Sepang or even the Top Gear test track then this is the game for you.

Pros:
- High FPS, Well optimised
- Loads instantly, no waiting time
- Great readability, no issues learning the game mechanics
- Map is quite large, good amount of places to loot and explore
- Many iconic places and its quite easy to learn your way around the current map
- Animations and Sounds are great (Weapon sounds are very satisfying)
Cons:
- Server-side/Net Lag (Quite emense when there are a fair few players online)
- Infection from Zombie attacks has too high of a chance
- Drinking/Hunger goes down too fast (Food/Drink becomes too big of a distracting issue)
- Bullet drop is insanely high (Would be great to see the bullet visually)
- Game becomes repetetive after a while, but I'm sure there will be many new features in future time
- no Official Servers are currently up. Only 1 fake server (Which I guess is considered a place-holder)
- Development has paused for quite a while, even during the games time on the trending new-releases list
- No visual way to tell if you're loosing health fast (Died many times because I accidentaly forgot to eat or drink)
- No way to tell which icon to the right of the screen is for which condition (Infection, poison, broken-leg etc)
Conclusion:
Overall for its current price and status, I wouldn't recommend the game. It's great fun to start off with, but requires more features in its current state. I'm sure this game has an amazing future ahead, and I can't wait to see what comes out of full release.

TLDR; First of all, compared to a lot of games. This is a good game, nevermind the nice and true rendition of the Warhammer 40k / Gothic universe. Secondly, in my mind a game should be rated on its own merits, not how it is compared to others. The game is fine, and somewhat cheap. I wouldn't recommend it at the current state as there seems to be some minor issues, which I personally feel leads to a lot of frustration.
There's several different missions you can play. Each mission is divided into the defender and the attacker possition. There's; Breakthrough, Planetary Assault, Cruiser Clash, Data Revocery, Asssasination, Station-Assault and Convoy.
My biggest issue is that these missions clearly have a faivored race, meaning that some races are a lot better in specific missions. Some players argue on the forums that it isn't unbalanced, but rather a question of skills- If you're one of those elitist gamers, you'd problably agree and you should ignore this comment (and the rest for that matter).
I've been waiting like a small child anticipating christmas, once I got to the end in the beta version. The graphics are great and all that, but what it comes down to is basically the issue with the missions. In the campaign you play an imperial commander and slowly advance in their order. On the mission table you then have to chose which planets you'd like to travel to and then complete a given assignment. Each round you have a given number of deployments that dictate how many missions you can take. Each misssion (win or loss) uses a deployment, and you "end turn" in order to get more. All assignments come in the form of the previously mentioned mission-types. This clearly leads to a lot of frustation, when you realize that some missions are close to impossible (atleast for a mortal-gamer). This means you can either take the "easy" missions or use your deployments to try and complete a specific task. Since the chances for losing a ship is increased by a substantial amount in the tricky ones, you also have to take into account that you might have to ignore remaining deployments since your valuable ships are all destroyed, lost in the wap or repaired.
The game finds, and starts multiplayer games quickly, that's a pro. But my personal experience constantly matches me with higher level ships, that's a big con! I realize this might have something to do with the amount of current players, but nevertheless it can be frustrating, since the chances that you lose your ships (one way or another) you'd be struggeling in the match right after. Also as some already have mentioned there is a slowmotion effect, I think was initially designed for the campaign, but when an opponent uses this, everything slows down and you have that to combatent aswel.
It's not that this is a bad game all the way through, I just think there are too many bulletpoint that can frustrate a gamer, which leads the experience of this game into a more raging than comforting one. The graphics are great, although it would be nice with the possibility to skip the introscene to every battle. After the 15th game, people know how their ships look like. For some reason the game doesn't autosave after each game, which is also somewhat strange. Why would anyone take a defeat if they had a chance to retry the map?
Hopefully some of these issues will be fixed in the time to come. If I happen to notice it, I will also edit this thread.
With all this being said, I will continue to play this game - atleast till next month where a lot of great-looking games will be released. I do have a feeling, that I'm not the only one. So hopefully when that times comes, this game is able to compete otherwise I'm quite sure the community will deminish.
This isnt ready yet, but it has the making of something awesome. Lets just hope the Devs keep up on it and just add more and more things to do!

Single Player - This part of the game has been extremely enjoyable for me. In many ways it reminds me of XCOM where it creates difficult situations in which you cant save every planet. Not to mention the "Iron Mode" setting making any ships you lose unable to be repaired. This really creates what feels like an intense multi-front war for survival. Complaints about high difficulty even on low difficulty settings are largely exaggerated. I suspect many people aren't taking advantage of various mechanics (not to mention the fact that you can save and retry as many times as you like).
Micro Management - I was somewhat concerned about this, as there are so many abilities across your fleet. I have yet to run into any real intense micro management due to the games "Tactical Cogitator" mechanic that allows you to slow the game down to very near a stand still, allowing you to aim skill shots and target abilities with ease. This in combination with auto-cast functionality on pretty much every skill (things like silent running and "Micro-warp Jump" aka blink don't seem to auto cast), an auto target option so your ship will always attack something even if not commanded to, and various other behavioral settings, make micro management minimal. I suspect many people complaining about this being an issue are again not taking advantage of many of these mechanics.
Multiplayer - Is a blast. Plain and simple. With the variety of skills, passives, and traits (have to admit I love the Chaos's Nurgle trait and its death rot cloud!) I have been consistently surprised at the various strategies and play styles i have faced.
Bugs - I will admit I've ran into a couple extremely minor ones, though i see some people have had more issues but that seems to be decently isolated. At times in 2v2 multiplayer, friend invites don't work but that is easily solved with a game restart. Only other one i have had has been the occasional engine flare art on a ship not showing up.
Conclusion - While not the best game ever made, it's certainly very good. At this price point, including the promise of 2 free race DLCs (Space Marine, and one yet to be announced)  if you purchase it within the first two months after release, its a great buy.

Before starting the review, I want to get two points out of the way that those giving this game a negative review usually complain about:
The game isn't that hard, simple. The problem is not the difficulty, but the players themselves. Too many are playing this game on the highest difficulties when this is their first time playing a game such as this one. Not just that, but
Easy and Normal modes are there for a reason, for you to use if you struggle. For you, to IMPROVE. Many on the forums and the reviews are spoiled by gaming nowadays, they want it all and they want it NOW.
They don't want to spend hours to learn and improve their skills, and that's the issue. And the beauty of this game is the fact that
You obtain XP and rewards and you can still overcome whatever the game throws at you.
Seriously? Most of the time playing this game you control a bunch of ships, usually at the beginning a mix of 1-2 "big" ships and a couple smaller ones. Is micromanagement really a problem in an RTS that is about commanding a bunch of ships? If you think so, then you haven't played that many RTS's. Hell,
Not just that, but
, so you don't have to worry about it.
With that said, I want to mention that I wasn't trying to sound arrogant.
Those points (IMO) aren't valid to give this game a negative review.
Now the review, I'll try to summarize everything and expose my biggest complains at the end of the review.
Now that those points are out of the way, let's talk about the game. If you had always that itch for a W40K RTS based on space ships, then this is your game. Even if you are not a W40K fan, you are more than welcome although the universe of W40K is one of the reasons that makes this game so special (IMO).
The gameplay is very simple, you have an "armada" (duh) under your command and you have to use it wisely in order to be victorious. Like any RTS, you give them direct orders. Most of the ships have skills, that if used correctly, can be the difference between victory and defeat. There's different types of victory or "modes". Sometimes you have to defend a point, others "grab" some info from an enemy ship. Overall they aren't ground breaking but are good enough to keep the game "fresh".
You can choose your ships, modify them with new skills, upgrades and you can even upgrade your crew. Each ship has a weakness, so don't ever think that a big ship can assure your victory. And each one has a role, one type of ship is better at CQC, others at long range. Is pretty simple in theory yet complex enough to allow players to create a unique armada that fits their playstyle.
There's 3 game modes, Campaign, in which you command an Imperium fleet in a "risk" style map. If you have played games like DoW1 Soulstorm, is more or less like that although more scripted at the beginning.
It has some great voice acting and perfectly recreates that W40K feeling.
Giving some replayability, and best of all, you will never get "stuck". There's always a way to be victorious even if things get tough or don't look so good, however, that doesn't apply if you are always defeated (The logic is strong on this one yet many miss it).
Skirmish vs AI. No comments, the name says it all. Although it has a rank system like the campaign and MP.
Multiplayer, that needs some serious tweaking.
It uses a rank system like the SP modes, in which you start with the lowest tier of ships and you have to "grind" your way up. It sounds nice, if it wasn't for the fact that matchmaking is kinda broken and it can match you with a guy who has way stronger ships. If you want to play this game for the MP, wait for it.
The game looks nice and clean, most of the time. The graphics aren't that great, and the game has some bugs related to the graphic options. In fact, I have a few complains that I will talk about later.
They perfectly recreated the ships, and everything fits perfectly. The ships are canon, and that's the biggest plus (If you are a fan of W40K).
It is very competent, sometimes it feels like playing against a human. They will always try to win, never stay passive. It will make very logic decisions (Most of the time) and use every tool at its disposal to defeat you. I.e. a battle with the AI is never a walk in the park, although on the lowest difficulties they won't react that quick nor use skills that much.
Personally, I have no complains about the sound effects. They do their job, but sometimes they bug and you hear nothing. The quality is there though, and with a 7.1 headphones you can perfectly feel the "kick" of an explosion. The soundtrack is average, not in a bad way. It's nothing extraordinary, but that's mostly because of the universe of the game. It adds to the immersion, it is very "W40Kish" but too similar to the soundtrack of other W40K games.
First and foremost,
Basically a couple game modes need some tweaking. Depending on what faction you are up against, they can be really frustrating, unless you get really lucky. I think the devs didn't spend enough time playing these game modes before releasing the final game (As far as I know, they added most of them with the 1.0, so people couldn't test them back when the game was in Early Access). In my opinion, Planetary Assault and Data Recovery are the ones that need some tweaking.
Next,
Again, nothing that I haven't said before. Unbalanced and has a horrendous matchmaking.
SURPRISE
... Yeah, this game it's been in EA for a long time and from what I read from the forums, there still bugs that have never been addressed. In my experience, so far, I haven't had experienced that many bugs, but I have to mention it because there's a good number of complains and I can understand that. I may be lucky, but others aren't so. Personally, I've experienced sound bugs and a couple times I lost my mouse cursor, but could be worse.
The campaign, not the campaign itself but the
I'm sick and tired of always playing as the Imperium, simple. I think they just wasted a great opportunity of making a campaign like DoW, allowing players to pick their favourite race giving the game almost unlimited replayability. Like I mentioned before, the campaign itself is great, with a perfect atmosphere and top notch voice acting, but a change would be most welcome, specially when most W40K games focus on the Imperium.
I.e. wait for it to get patched and properly balanced, the game is really good and it has a promising future but right now, it needs to be polished a bit more to become a true gem. If you want to focus on the MP, just wait a couple months and come back.
Edit: I've updated the review after beating the main campaign on HARD. Again, it is not impossible as many like to claim.

Single player campaign short review only:
I dont care about the multiplayer aspect in games and thus this is campaign review only. I would not recommend the game for its singleplayer campaign alone due to reasons I am about to explain, however I can under no circumstances give this game a thumbs down due to my own gameplay limitations.
The Warhammer 40K vibe is definately present in the game as far as the story goes and it is presented well, however it is the gameplay that detracts from my enjoyment of the campaign.
This is a space game and you get a limited amount of vessels within each category to customise with certain skillsets. These skillsets are bought with honor points your earn throughout the missions on the campaign, however these skillsets quickly narrow down the strategical options due to specialisation, be it brawling by using ramming or long ranged weaponry. You dont build bases, you dont get reinforcements in battles and you are stuck with a limited number of vessels which you better know how to handle, the campaign story missions can be very unforgiving and thus the specialisation needs, you really need to know your fleets capabilities. Its extremely easy to fall into a certain rotation if it works, improvisation is better left for the easier missions.
Be it defensively or in offense I find myself doing the same over and over with a limited number of ships. This could be due to self imposed restrictions based on my personal skill level. If you buy the game for the campaign alone I would only recommend it at a cheaper price.
Multiplayer offers many more choices and human opponents, it most likely offers a very different game experience, for that I would recommend the other reviews on the game or youtube.

Could it be, no more mods to other games to get my digital BFG fix? The BFG videogame to end them all?
Yes, and no.
The game launched a tad too soon with some rather sizable flaws present. However unlike many other devs who push junk to steam with the title "Warhammer", this game holds great promise. This has the potential to be the next great Warhammer game after DoW and Space Marine.
The devs listen on the forums and feedback is usually answered to, which to me screams of hope that the game will turn out better and better as time progresses.
Now I'm just making it sound like "it will be a great game, it isn't one now". This is wrong to a degree. If you're still reading this, you're wondering if it is worth it to get the game right now, aren't you?
It is well worth the money I feel.
Gameplay is solid, basic balance is there (However needs work on some aspects), visuals are amazing, the game is dripping more WH:40K goodness you could ever want. I myself have encountered only one crash, one. And even this crash I suspect was caused by my computer rather than the game.
For me the game runs butter smooth on my mediocre rig even on epic settings.
The UI does the trick and controls are easy enough to handle, my only gripe is the hotkeys. Buuut these should get fixed sooner than later.
The combat is satisfying, and being an IN player, I like to make use of that ramming prow. I have not yet encountered a more satisfying feeling in a game as I have in this. There's quite nothing like ordering your ship to Brace For Impact, put engines to All Ahead Full and watch as engines push a flame the size of the ship itself and your space cathedral thrusts into the side of an unfortunate heretic ship, both ships jerking from the impact, sparks and pieces flying off the victim out into the cold abyss of space. Eventually the enemy ship gives way and blows up spectacularly and your cruiser plows through the wreckage coldblooded. Sound epic? I hope it did cause the game is absolutely glorious in making the combat feel great.
The basics of the game are as follows:
You have a points limit per match, and you fill it by selecting ships worth of different amounts of points. These ships will then go to face off a foe who chose their ships within similar limitations. Simple right?
But it doesn't end there, you can customize your ships loadouts to some extent. While you cannot choose which guns you mount on your cruiser of choice, you can choose which abilities it can bring with it. Which upgrades you want for it. Be it better armor and close range ballistics upgrades for a brawler build OR go with maneuverability upgrades and increased ramming damage. OR spec your ship to long range with better accuracy and faster shield regen. The options are there and you're in charge of how YOU want to play your ship.
And the more you play with the same ship, the more skills and upgrade slots you get for it.
You can also choose from 4 different favours, each granting different bonuses to the ship.
As of the moment of writing, we have the Imperial navy, Chaos, Orkz and Eldar. Space Marine fleets advertised as a preorder bonus have not yet been implemented. But it's quite alright, I'd rather see the existing races balanced first before any more is added and I'm sure most of you agree with this.
So in summary, get this game. Get it now. Balance will come and the game will get refined better and better. It is already glorious and the emperor himself is probably out there playing the game even after 38 millenia have passed since its release.

This game has nothing to do with the horror/semi-action series F.E.A.R., it's an adaptation of an old Steve Jackson book. Got that?! Everyone ok with that? Good, moving on. This game is awesome!
Steve Jackson's CYOA books have a strong positive reputation, so I won't focus this on the base material. I'll focus my commentry on the adaptation. Tin Man Games have stayed faithful to the original material, focusing on using the format of the VN to enhance the experience. Sound and music stings, strong colour illustrations, the whole adventure has a nice oldschool sense of fun, and there's a lot of new content here. They've done a lot more than just transcribe the book.

Appointment With F.E.A.R.  is a -very- slick videogame adaptation of a classic 1985 Figthing Fantasy gamebook.
For those who don't remember Fighting Fantasy, they were a series of excellent choose-your-own-adventure books with a roleplaying bent. Most of them featured warlocks and demons, so the superhero-themed Appointment With F.E.A.R. really stood out as a unique part of the series.
You begin the game by choosing your hero's superpower, look, and name. There aren't a huge number of options to choose from - only four powers, ten faces per power, a range of colour choices, and randomised names - but from that point on, you'll be bombarded with a crazy range of equally crazy superhero crises, all day, everyday.
You'll face a series of tough choices  every few minutes  ("Do I apprehend a mad poisoner, or rescue a public pool from the Ice Queen?" "Rescue a kitten or stop a chainsaw massacre?"). These scenarios will play out very differently depending on your choice of powers, as well as clues you may have found along the way.  Logic can help you a lot of the time, but other times you'll just have to rely on dumb luck. There's some basic fighting involved, and your victories will reward you with collectable cards and high-score-related victory points. Also quips. Quips are fun.
Still, preventing street crime alone won't save the city - you need to carefully navitage each of these situations if you hope to gather enough information to stop F.E.A.R.'s grand plot. Be warned, this isn't an easy gamebook. I've replayed the game around five times without getting close to success, and the game's backtracking options haven't helped me much either.
So...is it worth $6?
That totally depends on whether or not you like choose-your-own-adventure gamebooks. I *loved* this series as a kid, so it was an instant purchase for me. If you're unfamiliar with the series, well, it's a neat distraction. You can easily kill a few hours trying to navigate this game's labyrinthine crimesprees, and the sheer variety of events keeps things replayable for a while.
Now excuse me, my Professor Amazing has accidentally killed another civillian with his Energy Blasts, and I should probably flip back a few pages...

I played this for roughly two hours and played through to the end twice. Unfortunately I ran into a few problems during my second play-through, but I still really like this game.
- You can't stop every crime, catch every villain or save everyone, some choices are very amusing while others are tragic
- As well as subduing run of the mill villains you need to investigate and gather clues in an attempt foil a plot to assassinate the president and save the world
Appointment with F.E.A.R. - part 1 (first impressions review)
So in my first play through I was 'The Streaker'. you are given the choice of randomly generated names and I thought this one was perfect! You also have the choice of four different powers, I chose strength and flight. Although there were active alerts on my 'crime-watch' I took my time leaving my apartment on my first day to finish my coffee and make sure that my suit was looking nice. I decided that make the most amusing choices possible during this play-through whether or not that would make me good hero or not.
-----The game spans three days and each day you set out to work. You of course have a day job as a reporter and your alter-ego is quite mild mannered. You're always late to work and your boss is constantly yelling at you.
-----Every time you walk down the street, take the train to work etc. you always run into an incidents such as a crime in progress in citizens in dire need of assistance. You have series of choices of what to investigate at each location. For example the commotion of beeping cars in the street where you will notice a car chase or ignore the beeping and instead purchase a newspaper for news or clues about crimes. At the same time your crime-watch usually alerts you to something else. You have to choose what to investigate or deal with, you have no choice but to allow some crimes and incidents to go happen in order to stop others.
-----If it is a villain you engage you will be put into combat with them. You have a limited amount of stamina points which basically function as health. You exchange attacks with the villain until one of you is defeated. When it is your turn you have the choice of three attacks each does consecutively more damage and is more likely to fail. So there's a little bit of strategy to combat i.e. take most of their stamina with a strong attack then finish them off easily with a weak attack. I never lost a battle. But I think that was because I always chose strength as my power and so had a lot of stamina.
-----If you deal with an incident you need to make the right choices in order to save the victims. If you hesitate or make the wrong choice you can fail to save everyone. For example I investigated a giant shark that was terrorizing swimmers at a beach. You are actually given the choice to tell swimmers that it's not a shark but just a school of bluefish, which I'm sure wouldn't have turned out well if I'd tried that. Instead I thought I did the right thing by making sure that everyone got out of the water instead of flying towards the shark. However a boy was caught and horrifically eaten by the shark. My hero basically slunk away in shame.
-----Also after defeating villains in combat you usually have the option to allow them to go free instead of handing them in to the authorities. Sometimes you do this in exchange for clues. It was amusing to allow the chainsaw wielding Bronski free who immediately starts his chainsaw, laughs maniacally and runs off the down the street waving his chainsaw around. But when I defeated the assassin I decided to allow him to go free, unfortunately as soon as I did that he took his gun and shot the president, whoops! I felt pretty bad about that.
-----Some incidents cannot be stopped without the right clues. You cannot prevent the president's death or know the location of F.E.A.R.'s meeting which you instructed that you must find at the start of the game. I basically failed the game both times I played it through. Although I tried to play seriously during the second play-through and I actually found the clues I needed. For some reason towards the end they disappeared from list of clues. I'm not sure what happened. So the last half an hour or so I was basically playing towards an inevitable failure which was disappointing.
-----The game is short but it has re-playability value. For one to be able to achieve a positive ending if you failed like I did. Some of the things were the same on the second play-through. But in a lot of cases you make different choices for an alternate experience.
-----I think the game looks quite good. It has some very nice artwork and interesting characters. There is minimal animation, sometimes panels shake and text in combat such as 'KA-THUUUUUUNK!' have some colorful special effects.
-----You can make some very silly choices and the costume of my character's alter ego consisted of the exact same caped tights clad action hero only donning a large pair of spectacles and a fedora. So initially the game seemed like it would be pretty amusing, it was sometimes even later. But it wasn't really lighthearted as I first expected, with people dying bloody deaths and so on.
-----The game also rawards you with trading cards. Not steam trading cards. Your collection only seems to exist with the game itself. You gain a random trading card at the end of events such as the defeat of a villain in combat. You can also expend luck points that you accumulate to raise your chances of finding rare cards. You would need to play through the game several times in order to collect all the cards.
It was a bit depressing that I failed to save the president and the world on my second play-through. I think something may have gone wrong somewhere with the game somewhere to erase my clues. Bar that I enjoyed this game and I think it's quite good. It was worth waiting a few extra hours for it to become available this morning, instead of playing something else.
