I Have Nothing to Fear Except F.E.A.R. Itself…
It’s not secret that I adore Fighting Fantasy game books - I reviewed the recently released iOS app of House of Hell a while back
- but what many folk don’t realise is that the beloved Fighting Fantasy series wasn’t simply full of books based in a fantastical realm of dragons and demons.
With books such as Space Assassin and The Rings of Kether providing a sci-fi fantasy setting and House of Hell and Beneath Nightmare Castle scaring the bejesus out of kids up around the world it was the Super Heroes and Super Villains setting of Appointment With F.E.A.R. that excited me most growing up.
Steve Jackson created a world populated with puns and thinly veiled parodies of famous comic book folk (both creator and character) as you, The Silver Crusader fought the good fight and protected the citizens of Titan City. It was a very exciting variation on the concept of a fantasy adventure and I adored it. I never completed it legitimately though, it was very difficult and I always favoured the ‘fingers in the pages’ technique to get me through the story.
Jump forward to more modern days and the good folk at Tin Man Games announced that they were halting work on their Appointment with F.E.A.R. adaptation to pursue an exciting new direction. Part inspired by Inkle Studios’ work on Steve Jackson’s Sorcery! and part inspired by a decision to go from game book to graphic novel in style they invoked a little storm of hate from the rabid Fighting Fantasy fan base. How dare these upstarts mess around with the classics, eh? Well, I’m glad that they did. Because their final version of Appointment with F.E.A.R. is a joy to play.
This release also represents the first Fighting Fantasy game they’ve released on Steam and as I am well versed in their iOS apps, I decided to concentrate my review on the Steam release. Getting the housekeeping out of the way it supports PC, Mac and Linux as well as featuring a Kev-pleasing Big Picture and Controller support mode from launch. Throw in a pile of Steam achievements and more, and you will know that Tin Man have gone above and beyond for their Steam debut.
So how does a tactile app translate to the world of the personal computer? Well, in short it is pretty much untouched from the iOS version (which I’ve had a splash around on for comparison reasons) but this isn’t a criticism. It retains the interactive graphic novel feel and has a pleasingly free form interaction element as you can click on some elements on the game screen to generate small effects and animations. The game also allows a bit more control over ‘who’ you play in the game with pre-set elements with a degree of customisation, but all held in the grip of the developers to retain the ‘realism’ of the Fighting Fantasy world that Jackson created way back in 1985.
The influence of Inkle’s inspired Sorcery! Apps is evident from the get go as text from the book is laid on the screen line by line, being influenced by your choices. Some of the more odd choices you can make are complimented with great achievements that serve to shame you for your odd decision making prowess, and since starting the game a few times I have been poked for blaming dinosaurs for heinous crimes, for mentally making toast and for being vane, and I needed it to save me from myself.
Decisions do not always result in success, and the game rewards/punishes the player with a Hero points system that dictates how good a hero you are, and if you are likely to get a bonus card at the end of your run. Oh yeah, I forgot to mention them. So, Tin Man have added F.E.A.R. cards to the game as unlockable collectible cards that you collect during the game (and mobile users will be able to trade these via Facebook) and they add an extra element of replayability to the game as a whole. As you play the game you also unlock Luck Points that can be exchanged for a better chance of getting a rarer card. It’s not an essential addition by any stretch of the word, but it is a worthy one regardless.
The game makes good use of the quips used by super heroes, tracking them and providing me with a hearty final laugh in the ‘Game Stats’ section that follows each adventure - even if ending in resounding failure. The humour that runs through the game is the life blood of it’s very being. It may be set in the Eighties, but Watchmen this ain’t. Instead you are at the centre of a silver age style adventure, armed with a familiar looking ‘Crime Watch’, a selection of put downs and a hard♥♥♥♥♥boss who seems determined on firing you. Life as a super hero can be harder when having to live the mundane ‘incognito’ lifestyle that you use to protect your secret, heroic identity.
On the whole I have spent about three hours on Appointment With F.E.A.R. so far, and can see myself dipping in and out for a good few weeks to come. I even pulled my original Puffin published book off of the shelf, cracked out some dice and sharpened a pencil to give the original a revisit. I was blown up by a car bomb within fifteen mins. Good job I kept my finger in the pages. But could I do this on the game if I wanted? Well Yes, actually. The game has a very clever checkpoint system that allows you to jump back a little and attempt to avoid humiliating failure on a replay. Or reset the whole game. Or choose new super abilities. Perhaps it wasn’t wise to fight a giant stone creature with a Psi-powered super hero, and you think it’s worth going back through as a super strength character. Well, the option is there.
Finally, and I mention this as it is a very pleasing thing to note, the game supports the OpenDyslexic typeface that makes it easier for people with Dyslexia to access products with text. In a game so reliant on reading I can only applaud the good folks at Tin Man for ensuring that this app is open to as many people as possible. Sometimes a game is all we need, and there are enough barriers in life it is fantastic to see more and more developers working on accessibility. Bravo to you all!
So in summary Appointment with F.E.A.R. is a very polished and accomplished effort from Tin Man Games. For any one who has ever raider their older sister’s room, stolen some tights and a cape and taken to the streets to avenge the death of a beloved uncle it is an ESSENTIAL purchase. To those right minded folk who would never consider such acts of perversion and vigilantism it’s a great way to still live out a super-powered existence.
My character is like Jonathan Creek with the ability to punch a bad guy through a shipping container.  Who wouldn’t love that, eh?
Appointment with F.E.A.R. is available now on Android, iOS and Steam (as well as being in the Humble Store if you are so inclined). It is almost essential gaming for anyone who enjoys graphic novels, interactive fiction or watching helplessly as a Ripper Shark kills a child in a very familiar scene….
Reviewed on the Steam version provided by the developers.

Recommending this game is very polarizing. On the one hand, it's arguably the weakest entry in the franchise. I especially detest that the Dex story arc is mentioned, but still swept under the rug, never to be resolved. It also has very limited replayability, the accquisition of powers being story-driven rather than as unlockable extras means that you have to either wait until the very end of the game to drop a nuke, or you have to cheat.
On the flipside though, powers make vehicles useless after the first four hours, and by association, the car shop are pretty much never used. But if you want to use vehicles and fight without powers, your save gets flagged for enabline cheat codes. It also means that you have to stop and re-enable powers at certain points in the game just to move forward when the story demands that you use the powers you want nothing to do with, and cheated just to get rid of. Worse yet, if you play the majority of the game without using powers, you'll be at an extreme disadvantage in the final boss fight which literally requires you to use all of the powers you've obtained since the start of the game if you want any chance of winning.
In conclusion, if you get lucky like I did, and you can get the whole game with all of the DLC included for around ten bucks, get it. If you have to pay more than fifteen or twenty for it all, pass. Not much of an improvement over the first game, especially from a technical point of view.
In the thirteen hours it took me to complete all of the game's challenges (sans the online multiplayer ones) I experienced seven crashes, four instances of the game locking up entirely and three cases of the controls no longer responding in the main menu. I also encountered several gameplay bugs, such as bombs falling through the floor, not being able to climb ledges after grappling to them, getting stuck on geometry and skipping small sections of the game by accidentally triggering normally unreachable checkpoints upon death.
I experienced intermittent stuttering and frame rate issues on an i7 3770K processor, GTX 680 2 GB and 16 GB of RAM at 1920x1200. These slowdowns persisted even on lower graphics settings and resolutions. Several times the frame rate inexplicably got stuck at 10 frames per second for the entire game session, requiring the game to be restarted. Loading times are also significantly longer compared to the first game.
As for the game itself, it feels very much like the first one. It's a solid game, especially in co-op, but there's little in the way of innovation besides four-player co-op and a new loot system that lets you open treasure chests containing randomized equipment of varying quality in exchange for collectible gems. The majority of puzzles are very similar in concept to those from the first game: grapple up ledges, roll balls, place some bombs, pull a few levers, step on switches. The overall experience was a little too familiar, feeling more like an expansion pack than a sequel.
Lara gets a torch this time around, but its use is limited to one or two environmental puzzles. The rest of the time you will be using it to compulsively light braziers for a chance at extra loot, which is a fair bit of busywork for little reward. The one truly new gameplay mechanic revolves around the staff of Osiris, which lets you manipulate parts of the environment and solve puzzles by reflecting beams of light. Compared to the spear from the first game, the staff makes for a decidedly more rigid puzzle solving experience. While the spear let you solve puzzles in creative (and sometimes unintended) ways, especially in co-op, the puzzles that require the staff all have solutions that are pretty much set in stone. There's not much room to stray from the intended path anymore.
I completed the game entirely in local co-op with a friend and did not experience any truly gamebreaking issues aside from the aforementioned bugs and the occasional crash. However, the game does not appear to create a separate save file for local players besides the host. Upon leaving and rejoining a game, others will have their inventory replaced by whatever the host is carrying. After experiencing a crash near the very end of the game, my co-op partner joined again, only to find that his entire inventory had been wiped with no way to restore it.
I can not comment on the online multiplayer, as I have not yet been able to connect to any online games. The handful of games I found through the lobby system (after searching for roughly half an hour) were all canceled during matchmaking, leaving me to stare at the main menu while the game unsuccessfully tried to connect to other players.
In its current state, I would recommend getting the game only if you are a fan of the first one and are willing to overlook potentially aggravating technical issues. If you're on the fence about buying, it might be smart to wait a little longer and see if a patch will fix the most glaring issues. For those who are new to the series, I would absolutely recommend checking out Lara Croft and the Guardian of Light first.

Grab the collection when it's on sale, this is a must have turnbased strategy game.
Gameplay:
You pick civilizations like you pick between species in Starcraft, but most of the civs you choose from are only slightly different from each other.
There are at least four dimensions to civ development: 1- cultural focus (warlike, merchantile, etc.), 2- direction of tech advancement, 3- unit or special building propigation (these are mutually exclusive investments for every turn), and 4- land manipulation for resources (they call it "tile improvement").
My only complaint is that the game gets tedious when you have more than a dozen cities to govern, and I don't believe that this is a symptom of turn-based strategy simulation, but a lack of imagination and experience by the programmers and designers involved. I'd love to write an algorithm and interface model for this game... is it mod time?

Zero Gear is a cart combat multiplayer online party game. Its more than eight player racing, the maps have a variety of objectives such as three-on-three European and American football. There are battle modes such as using boxing gloves to knock other cars over the edge of a sumo ring into the abyss below. Other maps are skeeball and even a pachinko machine with your cars. Its a true party game for anyone that has seven other friends online with this budget game. The game does offer a four pack for the price of two, which is always incentive. If you have no friends, the real problem is that five years after its release, there is no one playing.
The game plays easy with an accelerator, a nitro boost, a mini jump for sharper turns. You can gain nitro by drafting behind other competitors or touching a floating dreidel. In fact almost touching it is good enough. The boost will put you at your top speed in an instant rather than slowly increasing speed or shooting you forward, so its just as useful to use the boost when you've got the minimum or maximum amount. In other words, just hold down that boost button. If you ever fall off a track or stray too far from the path, you can use a respawn button. There is optional full mouse camera support and even a free aim button so you can target another competitor.
Like all cart combat games you have weapons. In this case there are two buttons to use a weapon in front or behind you. Its shallow in term of weapon variety and you get them by driving through hovering boxes. There is a bubble shield, a boxing glove, a pink love robot that will follow and then hug on the nearest driver until it explodes. You can also get a mine to drop, and a tornado that will throw anyone caught in its winds. Ice blocks will freeze an enemy and send them gliding forward with no ability to turn. Even frozen in ice, their tires will spin, so that feels like an overlooked detail.
Perhaps the most context sensitive item to use is the spring that lets you jump. While the spring can be used to jump over things, I consider this to be more useful for doing backflips and barrel rolls to get more boost. When you're in the air with any jump, you have full tilt control of your vehicle.
If you're all alone you can play with bots, but victories feel hollow without a single player campaign or cup of any sort. You can setup quick matches and assign the fifteen events you want to play. With the quick matches its just you and three other bots playing the same even twice for whatever reason before you progress to the next map. You can always setup a more complex server, but it takes a bit longer.
In terms of customization, you have a lot to chose from. Your car, your gear, your helmet and your face wear. Everything is customization and adds a lot of silly character to the game to make you stand out from the pack online. You can be a hovering brain wearing a clown nose with blonde pig tails driving a boat car. A nice option is randomization, so you can end up with a pink squid wearing a moon helmet driving a bomb with spike tires. Speaking of spike tires, when you use them, you can tell if you let off the accelerator the tires stop completely even if you continue to move forward.
As for the tracks themselves, the races are all closed circuits with only two or three laps. The shortest course has eight laps, but it feels like a strict circle.The driving surfaces are needlessly wide so the focus is more on the weapons instead of the driving skill. Each course has a few ramps and jumps here and there. You'll even go down a bumpy ski slope, a wavy slide and a water slide. Each course is bright and colorful. Its all very appealing to the eyes to make that quick fun joy ride feeling.
There's a lot of creativity with the courses, a pool and water slide, driving on a billiard tapble that connects to an air hockey course. Even the standard race track circuit shows a lot of flair. The desert themed track has you racing outside and then through a crystal mine across wooden roads. The creativity and effort shows, but the thing that holds the design back in my eyes are the lack of hazards. There's a dirt stadium that could use some slowing mud. These wide tracks just need something else on them like a shallow river. The water park has a lot of water, but it has no affect on you even if the water slide can rotate you backward as you go down..
Then there are quirky events such as the basketball, American and European football events that have you trying to score a goal with a gigantic sports ball. While I like the idea, the practice of it in Zero Gear is lacking, its dull and imprecise. Speaking of dull, nothing can trump the tag chase event in terms of boredom. The tag chase has a timer where only one person's time increases. The one that fills their meter first wins the event. Well this takes forever, because everyone else's meter goes down. To make things interesting, the mode will change where the one that is it will decrease in time, making a long mode even longer. These cars are so tiny on such an open wide map that its tough to tag anyone. If the person that's it falls off the level, its up for grabs in the center again.
While a lot of the other events are fun and unique, they feel thrown together such as the pachinko and skeeball games. These are simple games based on points. You use your car to drive off a cliff or ramp and fall down into the pachinko or fly into the skeeball. The skeeball feels like skill, the pachinko feels like dumb luck. This is strictly filler content to flaunt as a frill.
There is controller support, just not in the menus. Default controls needed to be adjusted because some of the buttons were forgotten about. Even adjusting the controls, there is no menu button to adjust, so there's no pause with a controller. In fact there is no pause, because an online game keeps going even with bots. Instead there's a menu with no way to rebind the menu.
Zero Gear feels like it can benefit from from better events and a single player series of races against more intelligent opponents. There is something good here, but it needs to go deeper and bigger. More weapons, more races, more hazards. I'm sure it was fun when its multiplayer was still alive, but with such a small budget game, I wonder how alive it ever was. The game lives and dies on its multiplayer. Judging from the 25% of people with the first achievement, people went into the game, saw that its multiplayer only and went right back out.

Be prepared to spend lots of time gripping your arm rests as you worry that the next shot through your shields will be the one that ends it all!

I should point out, i am an AVID fan of the 40k universe. I play practically every tabletop game that is made by games workshop and even the rpgs etc made by fantasy flight games along with having read just about every book set in the 40k and old world universes. So i feel i have a reasonably good knowledge base within which to set this review.
I will also point out, that this is my first proper game review. I am usually more of a watcher and a waiter when it comes to beta/Early Access games, but this one in particular caught my eye. Firstly it is due to my love of the old Battlefleet Gothic tabletop game. I played that game endlessly with friends and family. I love the idea of piloting a half dozen lumps of ceramite and plasteel 5+ kilometers long into HOLY BATTLE WITHT THE BLIGHTED HERETICS!!! ahem..... its exhilirating... and so is this game.
I feel that this game has kept particularly true to the tabletop game in regards to its play style. it feels simliar to me. When i moved my ships around the table and tried to line up nice dual broadsides or a choice torpedo spread, the sluggishness of those gigantic hunks of metal moving around the void is extremely similar to how i feel when im trying to turn my battlecruiser abeam of another vessel to unleash the EMPEROR'S HOLY WRATH UPON THE FOUL XENOS!!!!!! .... sorry... caught up in the moment.
My point is that the games feel very similar and i like that. Even the other races have a feel similar to playing them on the tabletop, excepting that a battle can be over in a matter of minutes if you maneuver correctly and pincer your foe, or corner them (in the case of a data retrieval or assassination mission). however, i have also had engagements that lasted over an hour as my opponent and i tried desperately to out turn or out thrust one another and bring down their last ship (with my last light cruiser on 100 hp and busted♥♥♥♥♥shields/guns/engines..... (speaking from experience on that one).
Ok since i feel like im blabbing on a little much, i will attempt to get back on track and wind this novel up.
So Pros:
- Nice graphic effects,
- I like the sounds and music (very gothic)
- The gameplay is fun and challenging if a tad repetitive
- Replayability (4 races with a view to more and many different ship configs) is great, i never felt bored, usually i would log on thinking "hmm id really like to try eldar today and see if i can get the hang of keeping those damned holofields up all the time"... or something similar. there was usually always something i wanted to do in the game.
- The campaign is fun and varied - i was pleased to note that there are a bunch of non standard mission types mixed in with the "standard" complement of missions (cruiser clash, data recov, assass etc) it keeps the campaign feeling new and not TOO repetitive.
Pros:
- Price. The cost is kinda high, but i also kinda feel its worth it... almost...maybe slightly less.... but then ive ALWAYS thought that... about basically everything GW has ever put out... so why should this be any different :-P - ever bought anything from Forge World? case in point.....
- Bugs. As ive seen mentioned and experienced myself, there is still a couple of bugs that carried over into the main game and a few typos and tooltips that need to be corrected to show the data for the race that you are playing... eldar dont technically have "lances" etc...
TL;DR
I like this game. ive played it a fair bit. i dont mind games that have a bit of a grind in it, makes it feel like im a fleet captain learning to use a fleet in combat. it appeals to me and my sense of the 40k universe. I love 40k, i love almost everything to do with the universe and all it contains. it is vast and detailed and that appeals to my twisted little mind.

This has become one of my favourite strategy games very quickly.
The fights themselves are fun, quick and requiring micro but not to the extend that it is simply about who can click the fastest. The battles are very tactical with the deciding factors being about who can get the best use of ships rather than economy management.

Some people have stability problems but I have had only one crash in 22 hours.
All in all an excellent game.

As one of those titles who comes from the golden age of videogames, the Dead or Alive franchise has to meet certain expectations. The core formula is still the same as the late 90's PSX release: babes and bouts, and the tagline can still be the same as well: there's much more behind the gorgeous busts in this fighting game.
The graphics looks decent, but being the latest iteration of an older title is not top notch, the previous generations of fighting game had remarkable graphics, sadly this aspect is being overlooked lately, of course it is still totally nice and enjoyable, but it is not something as revolutionary as it was back in the days. On the other hand the design is extremely beautiful, the models are perfect and the characters have a magnetic appeal and a wide variety, it is impossible to not find someone to pick and like. Moreover there's an impressive number of outfits for each character, the costumes DLC are too pricey (2x times the cost of the game each) but there's enough variety in the game even without those DLC. Moreover the mod community seems to be pretty excited about this game, so much that the first mod came out in less than 24 hours. It was a nude mod but it counts as well. The stages are rich in variety and interactivity, and also for that the battles are still spectacular, flashy and fast paced. The cinematic camera option allows for some satisfying moments, especially when one of the players is send crashing throught a wall and then down in the street and the fight continues outside the building, or when the battle unfolds on raft moving down a waterfall.
The core gameplay is fun: easy to pick but hard to master. It is rare to have depth and simplicity in a fighting game. Alternative titles such as Virtua Fighter or Tekken are much harder to approach for newbies. The basic system is an intuitive triangle one: strike beats grab, hold/defend beats strike, grab beats hold/defend. The game is overall very offensive, with a fast paced gameplay: strikes have a great variety of range and angles and allows the attacker to build pressure; the player on the defensive can turn the tables around by timing an hold right or has the option to keep his defense up hoping not to be crushed in the meantime. A lot of dept is added by strategic use of guard breaks and stun moves, togheter with critical burst ( some sort of super moves) and by spacing strategies which are essential to master at an higher level. The interaction with stages is still there and it is an active part of the fighting strategy. Balanced match are not onesided: juggle and long comboes do not hinder too much the defensive options, there is always some window to turn the tide with a well timed hold. Usually the fights boils down to who makes the best guess and who controls the space better. It is extremely fun to play versus any human player around the same ability level, meanwhile the AI is usually good at holding, almost on godly level if you set maximum difficulty, but it seems quite easy to fool if you know how to space properly. It is always challanging and fun to fight until a cetain level of mastery.
The tag-team mode adds another layer of complexity to an already deep gameplay, forcing the player to rethink strategies and to perform new tag-team comboes to keep the pressure up.
The big issue is the absence of online play on release, and today that's one of the most important option in a fighting game. Yes there's plenty of game modes avaible and a very rich, long and enjoyable story mode with fully animated CS, but in the long run the game longevity suffers from the lack of online play.
The PC port has a decent quality if compared to the console versions, however much more could have been done to improve the graphics. Ultimately once these small problems are set aside what remains is a solid game with a great cast of characters. It is definitely a fighting game with attitute, and for its price on steam it is well worth picking if you're into fighting games, for a first timer who's not too picky and enjoys the graphics design and the characters it is a good starting point.

SOLUTION 1: To fix this game crash (this one I had to hunt for info) :
1 - Right click the "Speakers" icon on the bottom right of your desktop.
2 - Click "Recording Devices".
3 - In the "Recording" tab, Right click and select "Show Disabled Devices", "Stereo Mix" will appear.
4 - Right click "Stereo Mix" and click "Enable"
5 - Click "OK"
PROBLEM 2: After this fix, it allowed me to play the game, but the graphics were completely crazy.
SOLUTION 2: To Fix the graphical errors in Star Wars Battlefront 2 :
1. Go to
2. Click on Direct X 9.0
3. Right Click on 15.10.zip
4. Do a Standard Download
5. Extract Files (atiumd64.dll AND atiumdag.dll) to Same location as BattlefrontII.exe
C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Star Wars Battlefront II\GameData
6. Now the game should start without any graphical bugs or glitches!

If you played the first Lara Croft game (Guardian of Light) you'll know what you're already getting into. A top-down shooter, like Van Hellsing or a Diablo 3 Lite, with puzzles and many enemies. It can be played either solo or co-op (I went through it solo), as puzzles do not need multiple people to solve.
Like the last game, LC:TOO is a quick adventure (took me around 9 hours or so with a lot of exploring), with good pacing through the levels, and I thought the level design was well done. Puzzles are not complicated (I think the first game had harder ones), but this allows for smoother pacing, and less standing around. Not a great trade off for some (like myself), but others will be happy for this. Chests in the game provide more rings and amulets to give you buffs (like items in the first game), and you have to spend the gems you collect to open each chest (more gems spent, better chance at a better item).
The game is not overly difficult, nor is there an option to increase said difficulty. Like the first one, there are challenges for each level, and after beating the game you can go back and run the levels again to try and beat all of the challenges which adds to replayability. Like it's predecesor, LC:TOO also rewards weapons and items for finishing challenges. Unlike the last game, where you had to select a specific level, the map in this game is designed around a central hub, so you just need to run off to whatever tomb you want to take another shot at.
I have seen some complaints on the forums of high end gaming rigs having issues running the game. My specs are average (I think) and are as follows:
CPU: i5 2500k (quad core 3.2GHz - not overclocked)
RAM: 8GB
GPU: Radeon HD 7777
Ran the game on High settings (which it defaulted me to), and only once did it noticably slow down, but it was only for a couple seconds.
All in all, the game is a fun romp through a bunch of tombs. I think that's the key thing with this game. It's not challenging. It's not revolutionary. It's just good, simple, fun.

This game is outstanding! It's brutally difficult, makes you have to think tactically and strategically. The devs have really put their heart and soul into this game, and you can tell by the in-depth gameplay. From wearing the same rags on your face you used to stop your bleeding, to wearing mismatched shoes on the wrong feet. There was a lot of time and research put into it, so undoubtedly the quality is there.
No AAA 3D game has been able to capture the helpess, lonesome, sometimes fearful feeling and atmosphere this game provides with the exception of FO3. You will die from black mold inhalation, starvation and dehydration, mauling, having your cranium caved in with a looter's boot and many other miserable deaths before you start to get a grip on the game. No matter how well you're doing for yourself it WILL throw you a curveball that 7/10 times you might not be able to hit.
The game consists of quite a bit of reading, but I assure you, when you do come across those scenarios, the writers for the game have a gift of making you feel like you ARE the character. Whether you're coming across ZomZom's and feel the sheer terror of the situation you're in, or coming across an eerie bumpkin living in an isotope mine, the written out scenarios are extremely captivating and engaging. And not to mention, EVERY choice you make will have a tremendous impact on how the playthrough pans out.
Onto the combat, it's EPIC, and plays back into what I commented on above, the quality of writing. It will feel like you're battling for an eternity, constantly tripping on the poor terrain and having to choose whether to take a chance on getting up, or roll around dodging your attacker's next move. Chasing down scavengers through the woods as they desperately try to flee your relentless attacks. Or my personal favorite, fighting a evenly matched opponent when you both have nothing but your bare hands for lethal weapons. You will fight, you will fall, you WILL cough up blood, and sometimes you will yet again, get your head caved in after a long and tedious fight.
Anyone, and I mean ANYONE who's a fan of post-apocalyptic games must add this to their collection. NEO Scavenger is living proof that you don't need good graphics to have a fun game. The things you can do in this game are practically endless. There is so much to do, and you have such little time. I'm STILL trying to survive longer than 6 days per playthrough. But the good thing is, you learn something new each playthrough. Whether that be how to play, or a new strategy that works.
There is no room for mistake, there is no room for impulsive decisions or recklessness. This game is everything a survival game should consist of, and then some!
My only complain is I've saved a few games to end off for the night, only to return to no saved game. Fullscreen mode is a lie once you unconciously hit escape to leave a screen like we're used to, and there were a few times I had to exit out and reload my save to fix a scavenging glitch (I would press 'E' to scavenge and nothing would happen even though I still had sufficient points left over for my turn).
9/10 - Would hopelessly flee from a Merga Wraith only to run into a Dogman pack again.

If you like puzzle games, liked the original, enjoyed FORCED, or even enjoyed games like Trine and want something a bit more to play with the brain switched on, buy this.

So, here's the thing about Meadow: This isn't a game for everyone. I'm just going to say it up front so that you can probably understand the rest of my review/opinion on this game.
Meadow is a social interaction game as a secondary goal; its primary goal is to be an exploration game, and that is what it is. You explore, you get rewarded for it with advancement in the game, and you're also rewarded for your exploration by finding some beautiful landscapes, amazing visuals, and a wonderful array of music.
However, this is not for everyone. Given that it is 100% passive play, I found that most of my enjoyment from this game stemmed from the fact that I was playing with friendly folks that I've never met before, we were exploring to help others achieve greater standing, while at the same time achieving even more for ourselves. And it's funny just how... friendly the community is when there's no way to speak via text. Everyone I met was friendly and willing to help me, even when I just started out.
My first few hours playing the game were spent as a Badger Pup (as it will be for most people), and maybe I was lucky, but within the first... hour or so, I had gotten "adopted" by a person playing the Adult Badger model, and he/she led me and about three other noobies on an adventure that spanned the whole map. We saw amazing caves, breathtaking vistas, and got to learn how the game worked through gathering the items necessary to earn a new avatar.
Now I've unlocked everything, and I still want to play just so I can spend time with others and help those who are new to the game and wanting a similar experience.
What are its cons? There are two, in my opinion:
Con #1: This game is an obvious cashgrab. You buy it cheap, but find that you have to unlock stuff. You can have "free" cool avatars to play as if you buy their other games, soundtracks, or online books.
Con #2: Learning curve. This game has a bit of a learning curve, in the essence that once you join, you will have zero idea how to play and/or advance. You're going to have to figure it out for yourself, since there's no one who is going to tell you in-game. No text, no words, no questions; only emotes, and you figuring it out for yourself. They'll lead you where you need to go to figure it out, but you need to figure it out for yourself.
But hey, even if Exploration games may not be your cup of tea, at least try this one out? It's three bucks.

Crafting Dead Standalone is a game created by Ferullo Gaming. The development team in the last like 10 months of development has been a one man mission. F3RULLO14, the Developer has worked hard on the game and it seems that it has paid off. The game is extremely fun and I have played around 20 ish hours now.
Pros:
Exciting and Fun PvP battles.
Gunplay is excellent.
Friendly Community.
Graphics, Art and Particles look imense and are quite stunning.
Smooth Gameplay in terms of FPS and Performance.
Low end PC's can run the game with around 60 fps.
Suggestions are listened to and appropriately brought into effect.
All around fun with friends or alone.
Fun and adventurous map.
Cons:
Depending on location, network can be a little choppy, but this is beta and being worked on
Small development team however bugs are being fixed and new content.
A little better advertisement in terms of gameplay could be shown on the store.
Overall, the game is awesome, fun and exhilarating for an early access and I can see this being a hit in the future. People leave negative reviews however they clearly don't acknowledge the fact that its early access and development is increasing.
Patches are really common which is good for a game and keeps an active player base. The map is a good size for the max players on the servers. I also saw a customization tool for map generation coming in the future so this should be good for server owners.
Furthermore, the network is being optimized every day and new mechanics are being added. There is an active discord which provides user support and customer support. This is really good for supporting new players interesting in buying.
The sniping in the game is one of my favourite parts and I really enjoy getting shots. The bullet drop follows a more realistic pattern such as ArmA or DayZ. It really is one of the most engaging indie zombie survival games, which I would recommend. Another satisifying feature is the rag doll bodys the way the players drop when you kill them. The fact that you can also team with people or decide to slaughter them in cold blood is awesome, it really gives an imersion you cannot beat. Ghillies suits actually hide you! Unlike some games.
The price is only $9.99 which is a bargain considering you get the game throughout alpha and into the future where more development is being created like Cars, new weapons and lots of fun content. I really love the way Ferullo Gaming executes its development and this really develops a huge addiction in the fan base.
Lastly I would give the game, at the stage of Early Access, an 8/10 as the extra 2 would be when the network is a little more stable and more developers are added. Map updates should come regularly and this should be fun to be apart of.
Please support the game, it really has amazing potential.

This game provides you many ways to develop yourself into anything you want in a harsh, fantasy world of 3 factions fighting each other, while also trying to survive the wilderness in a hardcore way like in any survival sandbox game, but with an MMORPG mix? This is something new and way more stressful if you are playing on official servers.
There is so much freedom in this game that you can be anyone you want, if you want to be a cold-heart killer, go and kill vendors in your city and
(as of current state). This cripples the need of gold spending, but does not make the game any different because you will eventually get enough experience points in few knowledge trees to get the tools made quickly.
The more I play this game, the more I realize that Sandbox Survival MMO games are essentially a game that let you play in a giant painted picture. I've got to give a lot of credit to art directors, the world is absolutely beautiful. I have been amazed by the looks of certain locations such as the giant trees with wooden hanging bridges above the mushroom swamps, misty swamps with an abandoned graveyard and cathedral in the middle of it that you can barely notice until you come closer through the thickest mist you will ever see. A giant island with a dead dragon skeleton is astonishing especially with a land formed around it, not to mention snowy mountains, small place to explore but the storms and freezing mountains make it feel real.
What we lack the most in such games are proper engineering work, so you could maintain such a vast, huge world smoothly, but that I mean that the performance does not seem good. UE4 is known to have memory leaks in games that have giant worlds at once, one screw up of a software engineer can make a game unplayable for you when you leave one section of a map and enter another. If you fly on a vulture, expect to have a massive FPS drop to a singular digit when you fly long term, period.
Speaking of vultures, there are many creatures you can encounter to kill them for resources (you monster), look at their cute faces and get gnashed by a panther from nearby. Just imagine a world full of beasties, now accept the fact that you can tame them. It is a purpose of utility, what are you going to do with them, and how you are going to use them. Sheep can be a great farming hoard that can help you get wool (actually called Fur in the game) if you give them grass and leave them to "craft" it. You can tame giant scaley lizards that have a strength of a Godzilla to smash stones with just their jaws, horns and a tippy-toe that give you a lot of resources, a moving combine, it feels great to smash everything until you realize you have deforestated the whole continent and you start feeling very exposed and lonely. But not to worry, yourt buddy got you a lifetime of supplies! Also don't forget you can travel further to tame more creatures, even bigger, like frost dragons! Also you will see elementals of each element in nature, and you can summon them to build your army too.
I did not expect to hear a big playlist of originally composed soundtracks for this game, it feels special. Tracks on certain parts of Sacred Path give you feel that you entered a giant world of tranquility, danger and... You be the judge.
I do not recommend this game as a full-time purpose entertainment. This is far from finished, we are talking about 30% finished, so it means expect a lot of frustrations in a technical field of your character/mount getting stuck among the rocks. Economy system is very pointless since anyone can come over and kill a vendor to not let you buy anything at start that would make the game way more enjoyable. Dungeons and caves are locked in the meantime without an actual ETA when they start, and that is where you should think about whether you would like to try out the gamne, or watch somebody else play it to keep on track of things. Please do me a favor, and do not play it on a public server way too much, you will lose stuff, and its a part of the game, it is a frustrating part of the game, very risky moments will be there.

For weeks on end i told people about this game as i open beta tested it, I thought it had serious potential to be an amazing game. Im very familiar with warhammer 40k, and battlefleet gothic the TT game.
The single player experience is MINIMAL, very small fleets going at it, hardly in the feel of the epic large to be large 40k universe. AI is poor, consistantly running into eachother, mines, asteroids, torpedos, you name it.  700 pint limits even in custom games, progression on a pre exsisting admiral is needed to test things in custom games, 2v2 battles (pathetic size) even at their max of 700pts(again pathetic) will be split into 350 for each player, pathetic and insulting.
Multiplayer is ballance hell, the meta is stale, Chaos is all about kiting at max range and stealth. Eldar is about hit and run and stealth (and never ever ever getting shot or bad things happen) so they are easily the most micro intensive, however their strategy is limited, they cannot close with imperial or ork ships or they will lose, so they must stay at range, constantly running away from everyone, some call it a valid strat, others call it bland and un fun. Personally i didnt mind that at all but in MP you will find that people tend to not like playing against chaos or eldar simply on the merit that they arent fun. Imperials are good counters to EVERYONE, good guns against orks, average troop carrying for fending off boarders, good lances and attack craft and torpedos to keep chaos down, and simply armored to the teeth to handle the eldar. Orks are orks and they have guns and lots of orks, they are slow, not manuverable and strange, only strong at close combat, but not one trick ponies, after working as the imperium most players will catch on to them easily.
Meta during the beta,
Chaos attack craft (nerfed- still viable)
Nova Cannon Spam (nerfed- still viable)
Chaos 15k Kite (viable)
Ork Nova Kannon Spam (Gamble)
Ork or Imperial Torpedo Spam (more viable than ever)
Eldar pulsar spam (viable, high rish high reward- nerfed, still viable ish)
Now on to mechanics,
Customizing and upgrading your ships is nice, but you never get to upgrade them all the way for some stupid reason.
managing all aspects of your ships movement and firing takes micro control and some skill,
in an odd design choice, many several weapons and "skills" are designed to work on an autofiring setting, at a certain point, you hardly are even doing much work at all in the way of commanding your ships to attack, a few simple hot key clicks and you just watch what happens, adjusting only a few things as the game goes on.
The game is fun for a while but gets stale very quickly once you have it mastered.
Barring some massive update that radically changes the game i cant say i would reccomend this game to anyone, even the avid 40k fan like myself. for all its pretty grandour it still feels like a game that was rushed and unfinished with several glaring design flaws.
I have to give credit where credit is due though, this game kicks the door down on the idea of 40k space combat, something i havent been able to viscerally see or imagine in a long long time.

I never enjoyed ARK, I own two copies of it with a total of 110 minutes of gameplay. However, Dark and Light gives me a whole different survival experience -- it might be similar to ARK, but it feels like it's in its own genre. The map is huge and is expected to be made even bigger, players are extremely friendly towards each other (at least on my server) and it feels like people treat it more like an MMO than a survival game.
Now, if you're not patient, then perhaps you should wait a couple more weeks/months for some of the gamebreaking issues to be solved. Some of the issues that are gamebreaking right now:
- Extreme rubberbanding, especially on mounts. You will get teleported back 4-5 times to your original position.
- Huge FPS drop in random areas, almost deadly if you're being chased by something.
- Very high chance of yourself and/or your mounts getting stuck in areas. We've lost a couple high level tames due to them getting stuck in the map.
- The PVP is extremely dull, everyone's using the same spell due to it being extremely overpowered - If you go into a PVP server, craft a lightning bolt (2 or 3), it has no travel time and it deals an insane amount of damage.
- Melee Combat is impossible, hits are only registered 2/5 times and if you use the stronger attack (RMB) you will rubberband back a couple feet.
- Raiding is extremely easy, all you need is a Iron Hammer which never seems to run out of durability. It deals insane damage. So if someone wants to get into your house, they will get into your house, regardless of how many pockets or wall levels you make.
- Harvesting materials is out of sync. It can sometime take up to a minute of hitting i.e. a tree until you get something from it.
However, if you are person of patience, then give the game a try. You will have loads of fun and (hopefully) meet new friends. I don't know how it looks like on other servers, but EU Knight 4 consists of friendly folks that will only attack if threatened.
If you want to experience the game without desync/lag issues, give singleplayer a try. You can also spawn items through the console (ARK commands) and test them out before you charge into a multiplayer server.

Being a huge fan of the DOA series since its Playstation 2 debut and owning every title of the Series for every console i will give my honest opinion.
POSITIVE aspects
+ good graphics (i dont mind that they used last gen engines)
+ finally most characters (especially females) have a decent amount of costumes
+ the demands on this game for your hardware arent too high
+ the game isnt that expensive for what it offers
+ new players have a good tutorial mode to discover the skills of each character
+ great gameplay, you get a great beat em up with developed skills and fighting system
+ all original DoA characters included except Bosses like Omega or Tengu
+ offers a real challange to master a characters skill perfectly
+ very detailed characters and clothes
+ more tag team partners can be created
+ added music from previous DoA titles
+ added Steam achivements ( not really affecting the game experience though)
+ a lot of areas can be damaged by throwing, kicking or punching enemies into danger zones
+ can change hairstyles and underwear for females and put on or off accessiores which are suiting  the characters styles nicely
NEGATIVE aspects
- story is the same as in DoA 5 Leon, Marie, Honoka etc are completly excluded
- Marie Rose only got 5 costumes,dlc too expensive
- the game is focused very much on the female cast
- so far you cannot adjust controlls to your own wishes,
- only few different stages, steam version currently lacks of 3 Stages available on consoles only
- no transperency on vehicle windows (strangly we had them in previous titles)
- no steam emoticons or backgrounds (doesnt affect the game in my opinion)
- no plans to add features implemented in console versions like 3 more stages or destruction on Kagura Senran dlc ( which is actually even more expensive on Steam compared to the console versions)
- Online mode still crashes from time to time
- no lobbies for online mode makes it almost impossible to play with friends
- so far no VAC protection

[Compact Review End]
- if you bought the very first DoA 5 you probably have the feeling you wasted 50$/€, now you get an even bigger game for way less money > if you stick to the series and buy all games you feel ripped off your money...
- the game could have offered some new and different modes, something innovative, train your charakter with sportive activities etc > i love the game but this could have been a nice idea since there are so many skills and you could develope an even deeper relationship to your favourite fighter
- dlc is way to expensive , no option to purchase single costumes or smaller packs, ok the clothes are detailed and textures are nice but you could get an entire new game for this price if not more
> maybe you would sell more dlc and make more money by providing it cheaper and i smaller bundles > no clothes damage for the Kagura dlc? Why are you neglecting the steam version so much and ask even for a bigger price?> it would also be great to have dlc with different content and not only clothes
- voices of Virtua Fighter characters could have matched better with DoA voices, sounds very arcadeish while DoA characters do not > good for fans of the VF series but it does sound strange

Lara Croft and the Temple of Osiris is a isometric shooter with puzzle,  The Coop is satisfying and the soundtrack is great. The game has a range of weapons to unlock to accommodate many playstyles. the controls are decent and the story is a good length for it's price point. Unfortunately like the previous game I am a little upset by the small number of challenge levels, however I suspect more will be added as paid downloadable content.
Overall a good game to play solo or better with friends.
Lara Croft and Temple of Osiris. - Sequel to Lara Croft and the Guard of the Light, this game builds on what had been done before. by increasing the number of players to up to four and updating the graphics while leaving the gameplay and style the same. It is a well thought out sequel.
Gameplay consists of traversing various levels and shooting any hostile enemies that try to attack you. With simple puzzles throughout the levels to add flavour.
There are a good selection of things to unlock and to choose from, being able to select 2-3 extra weapons on top of the default is a powerful asset to the game.  The two rings and amulet you can carry also alter the character slightly.
While the release version has a few bugs, but there are quick workarounds for most and with a good number of checkpoints per level there is not much in the way of wasted time should anything happen.
The characters themselves are nice, a few funny lines between the two adventure characters but nothing really substantial beyond that story wise.
I personally found the keyboard and mouse movement to be easy to master, although many people have reported having problems.
The game uses Xinput for controller support but I was able to get multiple non-xinput controllers working with both x360ce and pinnacle game profiler.

At release this game unfortunately for it's voice communications had always transmitting on by default and as such has spoilt public co op games for me. But it is very easy to play privately.
Playing Cooperatively in itself is fun and engaging, the puzzles are modified depending on the number of players and allow for slight variation.
While there are two boss fights without challenges, all the major boss fights and all levels have challenges, (for example: kill a few enemies a certain way) that add a small amount of replay value to the levels. Unfortunately the puzzles, like all static puzzle games once you know the solution, the puzzles rarely cause any problems on other playthroughs.
Unfortunately beyond that I don't expect to see multiple playthroughs unless for speed running.
Besides and the bugs and transmitting always on by default there was one other thing that I was disappointed about.
Although I was okay with the length of the story and the price of the game, much like the previous game, I was a little disappointed with the number of challenge levels.
I hope and look forward to more challenge levels being added as paid downloadable content.

NEO Scavenger's strength lies in worldbuilding and it's game mechanics. The combat gives you a plethora of options like kick, drag, roll etc. Nature can assist and endanger you but it mostly endangers you :D
If you enjoy learning to live off a barren earth and exploring, Neoscavenger is your game.
Cons:
The AI interaction in random encounters lacks depth unless it's combat. Complex diplomacy is not this game's strong suit. This game makes sure to keep you alone in this world. You also can't attack the societies.
Even though lots of the locations are randomized, the same ones appear on every map, so replay value comes more in experimenting with the menu interface than trekking unknown lands. I think this makes the second replay weaker than the first.

Very fun game, I thoroughly recommend it to space rts players and those who are interested in the lore.
The atmosphere is the best done in a 40K game to date by far, the universe feels fantastic.
The tactics are deep and interesting, and each race plays differently to give you good variety. Torpedoes, ramming attacks, carrier tactics, and line tactics are all present and more.
Singleplayer campaign has an XCOM vibe, and you can alter the story by winning/losing certain missions that in the lore went a specific way, essentially changing the way the Gothic War plays. Also included is a single player skirmish mode, a custom game mode, and of course multiplayer with a progression system.
All this PLUS the fact that the devs are giving out the DLC Space Marine faction they are working on right now for free to anyone who buys the game before its released (plus a mysterious second DLC).
So the sum it up we have a great game that does 40K from a good dev and publisher. Overall 9/10

The beta has some issues thus far but most of them are standard beta affair. Errors where if the Host isn't player 1 in the battle lounge, that it just hands and returns to the lobby menu are the most common. Easily remedied right now by going to the back of the queue. Also the beta not lauching until you add it to the exceptions list in your anti-virus, also easily fixed.
However we do get to see that the netcode and how it handles lag is improved since the original release of Street Fighter V.  Certain stages have new gimmicks added to them like crates on Guiles stage, the new character select UI looks good, and all the stats and CFN changes are working and seem very positive so far. Flags are showing instantly on battle lounges too.
Matchmaking has been mostly nonexistant on the first day of the beta and hopefully it will be more present after the first maintenance period is over. Battle lounges have been working better than in the main game with the exception of the above issue.
The netcode now seems to be more prone to skipping frames here or there in the presence of lag rather than having large chunks of rollback severely disrupting play. This makes it much easier to play in lag than it did before. East Coast to West Coast is now fine and East Coast to parts of Europe is mostly fine as well. Other parts of Europe are a bit iffy, but still better than before.
The animations for the new moves in balance patch are a bit wonky  and feel like place holders right now, but you can see their utility. Gief's new headbutt better not make it out of the beta without a nerf though. Overall the balance changes mostly seem positive with the exception of Gief and Cammy.
In general I think the CFN Beta is showing good things for the future of SFV. Its not perfect, but boy is it better. Just remember that it is still a beta and is going thru multiple stages of maintenance thruout the beta, so errors here or there are to be expected and that there is a schedule with listed up times and down times. It is not constantly running, so if you can't log in, that's probably why.

For an early access game, it's not bad.
-The graphics are beautiful and I love the customization of the shape of the wolf.
-The animation itself is fluid and beautiful.
-The atmospheric noise is actually really nice!
However, this game has a few bugs or problems that I found annoyed me during the game. There was a surprising amount that I had found in my 35 minutes of playing, which normally isn't a good sign.
-The hunters seem to be too highly numbered compared to the wolves. There would realistically be fewer hunters but more wolves. Also, hunters may not be near by but the constant sound of nearby gunfire will ring off.
-I was attempting to eat a deer, but once I pressed 'E' I was magically transferred to the cave (a long ways away) and put into the sleep menu.
-Also, once you kill an animal, it may sometimes glitch into the side of the hill, making it impossible to eat it.
-There's nothing really to do except kill off hunters and animals, so I suggest some form of task/quest system.
-Finally, the controls are a little wonky. The turning is rather slow and the areas to press 'R' on dead animals is VERY picky, to where I had to walk back and forth over the animals while pressing 'R' just to get the marker. Also, the turning makes it hard to fight hunters as you want to move to prevent being hit, but it's hard to turn around and attack.
Ultimately, the game isn't bad. If the problems were fixed (which they most likely will be since this is early access) then the game would be more enjoyable. It's beautifully designed and has really good potential. I think the price may be a little high for something that's still in a big state of development, but I still recommend the game to people who want to experience it. Ideally, you should wait until the full release, but it's still an OK in my book.

There are many problems I encountered with this game, but the purpose of the developers putting it in Early Access is to fix issues and to make improvements.
First here's what I like:
-Good graphics
-Great, fluent animation
-If this game persists, then I'm sure it will be a fantastic single-player experience to enjoy in your freetime.
Here's are the problems in it's current state (which can be fixed, of course):
-There is little to nothing to do, it seems like a sandbox
-When attacking certain animals, such as the rabbit, there is a very small hitbox, I would suggest testing and altering hitboxes for certain AI.
-Combinations of certain animations are buggy. When I pressed e to eat a fish after catching it, it permanantly changed my e command to the fish eating animation - instead of howling. This is fixed after making a new save.
-*** The AI seems to be the biggest issue. Especially the hunters' AI. When playing sometimes I heard a glitched gunshot sound from a hunter when there were no hunters nearby.
-Additionally, there are far too many hunters spawning in the map.
-The hunters should not have such distinct and one-way coding. For example, every hunter and even the same hunter has the same attack radius ( I noticed a hunter chasing a deer and everytime he would catch up to shoot the deer he would go back to running because the deer kept repeatedly going out of his range after catching up. So you should make the hunter have the chance to shoot at greater distances with a lesser chance of hitting the target). I think there should be a probability of the hunter shooting at certain ranges at certain time intervals.
-The AI don't seem to realize that there is an object between the two people. So they will continue to shoot even if there is a tree in the way. And if an object is blocking the AI's sight, they will still detect you.

Finally, for a game like this I would rather have you focus with environmental struggles other than the hunters. Encountering hunters should be much more rare and harsh experience.

Crystal Dynamics proves again that this is a spin-off series worthy of the Lara Croft tag.  Now we're exploring some tombs in Egypt, and the graphics are ASTOUNDING for a top-down shooter. Last time around the graphics were a little on the "cartoony" side, but this time there is a lot of detail and the close-ups of the models are great as well.
Gameplay is pretty much the same (I don't know if there's anything new in co-op) with the exception of Lara now having a torch and the staff of Osiris, which help you get more gems and allow you to complete puzzles, respectively.
And this time there's a hub! It seemed very out of place at first, but they made it work really well. You just walk straight into levels from the hub (with a hidden loading screen in between, of course) and there's actually a LOT to do in it. You can actually use your gems now to open up chests that will give you some random equipment (with the more gems you spend getting you more rare items), you can collect the optional red skulls in the hub, and at times when you progress to the next levels there are little action segments that take place in the hub, making it feel more connected.
Overall this is a big step forward from Guardian of Light and solidifies itself as a must-buy rather than the impulse-buy Guardian of Light was. $20 is a bargain for this.

Great game! A little glitchy, and can be laggy at times, but good anyways. If your a fan on the Shelter series, the Might & Delight art style, and amazing music, this is the game for you. It's a simple, but has objectives. It's not completely open ended, you can have aspirations for getting new animals, emotes, and patterned pelts, but you dont have too. You can just find some people (animals), and chill to the music and serene enviroment.

Before we get started I would like to share that I have a lot of experience in the Mine Craft version of The Crafting Dead with thousands of hours on it. (This game is based off of the mod pack and has the same developer if you did not know this information)
Price: The Price 9.99$ is not worth it for this game to be honest i suggest lowering the price to 0.99$ maybe even 1.99$
User interface: The interface for new coming players is friendly, easy to learn and straightforward. Little amount but crucial bugs like inventory items disappearing, Not being able to pick stuff up at times, Inventory is "filled" with nothing at times requiring you to relog, crafting is easy simple and fast which is great. Can not see friends names or tags at a far(Needs to be within 5 blocks in order to do so) which makes no sense in fights or duels with zombies and the other players. The servers were just small and didn't hold a lot of people i say increase it from 16 to 30-50 players. Can NOT exit the game it crashes every time.
Basic Movement Mechanics: Very buggy, gets stuck on corners of many blocks (even grass blocks while running and walking). Many "windows" that are much larger than the character itsself, you can not jump through(No glass windows just air by the way). Occasionally choppy and cluncky. I like that you can walk with your inventory open though.
Gun Mechanics: First things first the bullet drop is inane in this game, shooting from about 100 blocks with an M4 made me aim up 3-5 whole blocks above the player to hit, Snipers can not reach as expected to. Which means increase the range a ton. Guns are unbalanced Rifles Kill in 3-4 Shots, Pistols 4-5. Pistols have a insane fire rate compared the rifles. I like how the bullets can stack and they weren't spread out between rounds like every other game, When testing the guns you could actually see your bullets just curve and drop which I like that you see the bullet but it makes you notice how bad the drop is. FINALLY NO HEADSHOTS?!?! if they are even in the game it's unnoticeable.
Visual Appearance: Overall the game has little to no shading and texturing on blocks. The campsites are just overall beautiful and are visually appealing good job on that but everything else is ehh. The weapons are ok but when you look at the guns they are messy and very sloppy. Everything looks 100% better in the inventory and from afar then when in your hand.
Overall: The game has so so so so much potential but not enough to keep me sitting here waiting for the next couple of patches. The price is high but if you have enough money to blow on an indie game have fun doing so. I suggest lowering the price the 99 cents to 5$ max. Many bugs and glitches when initially playing the game but there are ways around some. A lot of them are game ending like when you get stuck you need a friend to kill you and then you walk all the way back to the location. I do not recommend this game at the current state it is in needs many patches and fixes.
Rating 3/10 Needs a lot of work before it goes positive in my mind and a Price change.

The game does have potential but as is it isnt very good. Yes it just got released but there are some things that should probably have been put into play before actually launching the game, such as headshots, couple glitches like not being able to drink water at certain times and the overall clunkyness of the game. Again I understand that it was just released but they should have put more thougt into fixing or adding some stuff before it was launched. The price seems a bit too much since it isnt really worth a 10 dollars. If it was a dollar than I would highly recommend it or even 2 dollars at most. Now on to the actual gameplay. It was fun for a brief moment but then I ran into a couple of glitches such as zombies being able to hit through walls, invisible bleeding players, getting stuck on certain blocks when running or even when standing there I got stuck on some things (dont really know what it was). The art style of the game is okay but it could be improved greatly as it seems that the creator added more emphasis on the campfire(by far the prettiest thing I saw in the game) than he did of the actual world. The gun mechanics where pretty bad especially the bullet drop concidering your render distance was alot farther than the bullet could actually travel. The bullet would also drop so suddenly I felt like i needed to aim 5 blocks above the person just to hit him even if he was just a couple blocks away. The controls and movement felt a bit off and didnt feel as smooth as you'd hope especially since you cant even change the settings while in the middle of the actual game for some reason (it was literally just shaded off for some reason dont see the point in keeping it there) The map felt a bit too small suprising since it is a 2000x2000 wide map but since the characters could pretty much haul♥♥♥♥♥it felt like some people could just die and return back to where they died in a matter of seconds. There are also issues when playing with friends since most of the time I wasnt even able to tell if the person running at me was my friend or not even with coordination because their name would pop up like a block away or if I was in headbutting distance (not a game mechanic but would be pretty dope). The servers are too small only being able to foster 16 people which isnt so much in a zombie survival game. However there are a couple of positives. I did like how bullets where able to be stacked and some small minor things like only able to get drinkable water from pumps, I also liked how you had to heal via medical supplies instead of just food and water, however at the siame time I do feel like max water and food or close to that should heal the player in some way. The inv is handled pretty nicely although still a bit too clunky. All in all my final remarks are 3/10 it has potential and I do feel like the develepor should have postponed it just to add some final adjustments (like fixing the gun mechanics and adding headshots or something) as well as I disagree with the pricing of the game as well but If some people like it as is and still feel like playing it then have fun.
